I intend, in this place, to report the births and origins of the two primary active natures or essential virtues, which proceed from the two principles of all things previously recited <note>These principles are the "Divine Light" and the "Dark Abyss."</note>, and then afterwards to briefly explain the two passive conditions or properties that arise from the effects of these two active virtues. It must be understood, therefore, that just as the *potential* or *dark* principle is, in its essential property, contrary to the *actual* emanation of the Spirit or the *luminous* principle; so also each of them has produced into the world an offspring or essential property whose condition is mutually contrary and repugnant to the other—namely, **Coldness** and **Heat**. In this chapter, I shall deal succinctly with the mystical method and reason for the production of these virtues or properties, and in the first place, I will attempt to explain the deep origin of coldness to you, according to the small measure of my understanding.

It is clearly evident from those things which were reported before—and it will be said even more clearly in the first book of this second section—that darkness is the immediate effect of the divine Will, or of the Divinity while it is latent or contracted within itself. Consequently, darkness is the mother of the privative property of God, or the divine Power, which is the mother of **Privation**, **Death**, **Vacuity**, **Emptiness**, **Deformity**, and other such imperfections. For the deformed property of the **Nothing** <note>original: "Nihili"</note> or the **Dark Abyss** is to naturally rest, to be fixed, and in no way to act or work. The reason for this is that its desire is to have its existence in and around the **center**, where there is no motion or action by which it might dilate itself toward the circumference. In contrast, the luminous Spirit of God (or God in his open will or nature) is occupied with actions and movements that tend from the center toward the circumference. For this reason, the Dark principle claims for itself—and that by a natural inclination—rest, idleness, and fixation. And this property generates or produces the essential virtue of its own condition, namely, **Coldness**. Coldness is chosen as the **Combatant** or **Athlete** <note>original: "Agonista seu Athleta"</note> to resist the assaults of its opposite, namely heat (from whose company come motion and Action). Indeed, unless coldness is agitated and incited by the agile action of heat, it does not move, but is seen to serve its sleepy mother—

<column-break/>

Darkness and Privation—in a peaceful and quiet manner. The offspring of these, as we have said, are fixation and rest, which cling to the center like sleepers and inhabit it. Therefore, it is against their will to look toward the circumference, unless they are stirred up by violence. And in truth, coldness is an essential act that proceeds from the Divine power, which it serves primarily in its action. For the Divine power, being more focused around the center, contracts its rays from the circumference into itself in this property. This is according to that saying of **Hermes Trismegistus**: *The Monad generates a Monad and has reflected the heat into itself.*
<margin>Pimander, 3.</margin> It is as if he had said: that **Monad** <note>The "Monad" refers to the ultimate divine unity or the number One.</note>, like the divine power, sending out its emanation (which was another monad of one and the same essence), reflected it back into itself—that is, toward the central point from which it sent the Monad—so that it might rest there. And in this way, before any creation of the physical world, the **archetypal world** <note>The "archetypal world" is the divine blueprint or mental realm of God before physical matter existed.</note> was produced.
<margin>Reuchlin, *On the Art of the Cabala*.</margin> To this, the excellent Cabalist **Rabbi Bair** <note>Probably referring to the *Bahir*, an early influential work of Jewish mysticism.</note> also seems to agree: *Wisdom,* he says, *when it was retracted into the Abyss of darkness, remaining idle and looking at nothing, is called* **Nothingness** <note>original: "Ain"</note>; *and in this state, it is called the* **dark Aleph** <note>original: "Aleph tenebrosum." Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, here representing the first movement of creation.</note>. In this contracted, or rather sequestered and private state of Divine unity, God seems to work according to his negative property by means of his agent, **Cold**, whose unique endeavor is to make the waters rest. And this agent of his is proven not to be an "accident" (as the vain doctrine of the **Peripatetics** <note>The "Peripatetics" were the followers of Aristotle. The author is arguing against the Aristotelian idea that cold is just a secondary quality or "accident."</note> teaches), insofar as it is certain that no accident can be found in God. For God is the highest, purest, and absolute simplicity and an entirely formal essence, existing in and through himself, and consequently free from accidents. Therefore, since the divinity is but one essence, it is powerful enough by its own simple nature to produce, as it pleases, any essential property not divided from its divinity. For this cause,
<margin>Wisdom 7:22.</margin> Divine Wisdom is called a **Spirit** that is both **unique** and **manifold**. Second, that the property of cold is attributed or ascribed to the Spirit of God in its Northern action, whether in its privative <note>A "privative" state refers to the absence or withdrawal of light and heat.</note> or hidden condition. For the words are: "Who can stand before his cold?"

Wherefore it clearly appears that there is an essential virtue in Divine power. Third, that it must be an act of the Monad or Unity <note>In this context, the "Monad" refers to God as the single, indivisible source of all numbers and things.</note> in its own dark, abstruse, and privative nature; both because it renders bright, lucid, and clear things obscure and opaque, and because it seems to take away motion, agility, and life from the air, which previously moved, acted, and lived when incited by essential heat. And finally, because it is entirely opposed to the action of heat, which serves the emanating and life-giving divinity. Fourth, that the effects of cold are destroyed and reduced to nothing by the act of the revealed nature of God—that is, by his sent-forth **Word**. For the text says: "He sends his Word, and melts them," namely the snow, ice, and frost. Fifth, that these contrary actions are performed by one and the same Spirit in essence, but multiple in condition, to fulfill the commands of Him who sends it out. Furthermore, that the cold virtue in the wind is an essential, depriving or congealing, mortifying, and contracting act of God, is indicated from these pages of holy scripture: <margin>Job 37:10</margin> "The mighty God produces ice by his breath; by the blowing of God the frost is frozen." I conclude, therefore, that **coldness** is an essential act of divine power, or of eternal wisdom wrapped in a veil of darkness; and therefore we know the divine will in such a state or condition through those effects which it produces; namely, in that by its evident act it contracts from the circumference toward the center. For this reason, that virtue of God is the cause of congealing, thickening, contraction, constriction, fixation or immobility, heaviness, rest and idleness, darkening, mortification <note>In the sense of "making dead."</note>, deprivation, stupefaction, and the like.

In this property, I say, it is said by the wise man to be "more mobile than all mobile things," penetrating or reaching everywhere because of its purity. Thus, just as its privative or Northern property produced rest, idleness, and cessation from operation through contraction or attraction from the Circumference to the center, so in this positive or Southern and Eastern property, it is accustomed to procreate motion and action by way of expansion or the emission of its rays from the center toward the circumference, by means of the essential agility of **heat**. For this heat works assiduously upon the effects of cold by resisting, dissolving, and thinning them, making clear and transparent things out of the coarse.

For one cannot hold dominion until the other is gradually extinguished and, as it were, sent into exile.

Therefore, just as Light, along with all its companions or adherents, is said to be the act of positioning, of informing, of fullness, of motion, and the mother of life, health, and heat; so also heat operates according to the nature and disposition of its tireless and ever-working mother, namely Light, to subvert and turn into nothing the effects of Darkness and cold. We see this in the natures of the warm winds, specifically the South and East winds. For, while the Northern and Western winds more or less gather, contract, harden, condense, make heavy, fix, and render immobile and opaque not only the air but also other things, whether they are of the same or different kinds; conversely, the aforementioned warm winds are accustomed to dissipate, dilate, rarefy or thin, soften, and illuminate or make clear and transparent, volatile, and agile or mobile, that which the aforementioned cold winds had previously altered in the manner described.

From these things, therefore, it is clearly indicated how these two opposite powers, namely Heat and Cold, have their origin from one and the same Spirit in their fundamental essence, which in its hidden nature acts as the formless and dark principle. Hence it is called the **Dark Aleph** <note>original: "Aleph Tenebrosum"; Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, used here by the author to represent the Divine Source in its hidden, potential state.</note> or Divine Power, in which state it seems to us to rest and remain idle around the center of the Abyss. Two things, therefore, consist in one Principle from the principles, and with the principles two essential active properties arise, from which all things exist. Hence God is rightly called by the Scriptures "The One and All," and "All in all," and "without Him nothing," and "the center of all things, whose circumference is nowhere," and "in all and above all," etc.

For it is certain that cold has infinite dominion or power where Heat is entirely absent. For **Chaos** was a certain confused, cold, and dry mass, until the **Divine Light** appeared out of the darkness and acted upon the mass of frozen waters. Furthermore, Light considered in itself—without regard to its action upon the passive mass—was of a fiery condition, inasmuch as action, heat, and dryness were found within it. Wherefore it follows that, just as coldness in effect is nothing other than the act of divine power, and its action and dominion are made manifest and notable by the absence of Heat; so too dryness is nothing else than the passive nature appearing alongside the two aforementioned active virtues while they are in their highest intensity, in which state of activity **Moisture** is perpetually absent. For example, in extreme cold, when all things are thoroughly frozen, dryness is present while moisture is entirely lacking. Conversely, where the fervor of the sun and the breaths of the Eastern winds heat the earth beyond measure, moisture is also minimally found.

As for Moisture, however, we say that it is of an almost hybrid <note>original: "adulterinae"</note> nature, or rather, that it stands in the place of a <term>Hermaphrodite</term> <note>Meaning it possesses characteristics of both extremes.</note>, insofar as it is born or derived from two active natures, appearing to participate in both at its birth. Hence it is that this passive property is in an intermediate condition between those two extremes. Therefore, it serves to receive the impressions of the actions of both ends. We prove and demonstrate all of this by the following ocular observation. The **North Wind** <note>original: "Ventus Borealis"</note> by its dominion converts the existence of the air into snow, hail, frost, and ice: that is, it changes it from a warm and moist substance into a cold and dry one. But where the South and East winds begin to hold dominion, then their breaths gradually penetrate those aforementioned hard masses, and by breaking them apart, they change them into a moist or wet substance. This is according to the sense of the words of the text mentioned above: *When Jehovah sends forth his word, the snow and ice melt; as soon as he breathes his wind, the waters flow.* <note>Psalm 147:18</note> That is, from dry things come moist things. By this it appears that Moisture is nothing else than a mixture of cold and heat in some aerial or aqueous substance—previously hardened by cold—which is potentially capable of flowing; and then, as the extreme cold decreases due to the presence of heat,

<column-break/>

dryness recedes, giving place gradually to moisture. Thus, unless coldness is present with heat, moisture cannot appear. Similarly, unless the southern gusts look back toward the sighs of the North, they would hardly produce clouds and rain. Thus the Western gusts, insofar as they participate in and are in the middle between the warm South and the cold North, usually produce moister weather.

The reason for this <term>fluxibility</term> <note>The capacity to flow or change state.</note> is as follows. We see from the aforementioned that extreme cold renders air and water immobile and fixed. Consequently, it is an evident sign that some wind is beginning to predominate over the frozen mass when it begins to become moist, to move, and to be resuscitated—a function which nothing but heat can perform. In exactly the same way, the uncreated and all-creating **Spirit of Light** operated upon the dark **Abyss**. While it moved over its formless face for the creation of the waters, it caused that dark mass—full of potential waters previously frozen by cold due to the absence of heat—to gradually liquefy. Then, they were openly called by **Moses** by the name of "waters" (actual and real), and by **Hermes** <note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy and Hermetic philosophy.</note> they were called by the name "Moist Nature," and in that same state they remain to this very day. For it is certain that both the subtle or aerial waters and the thick and dense ones, such as the seas, springs, and rivers, are moist and fluid; nevertheless, they are continually changed and altered from one nature into another as the Creator of all things wills. These daily changes and conversions in the universal <note>original: "Catholico"</note> Element of the lower world are performed by his **Angelic ministers** moving upon the wings of the winds, whose task it is to cause the waters to rotate from one nature to another—that is, to be transformed from the form of one into another.

But we must observe that the visible waters and all visible things—whether they be <term>meteors</term> <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, snow, and lightning.</note> or other compounds—were later made and cast from invisible waters according to the doctrine of St. Paul cited before. And Moses recognizes that the sea and the earth, which were the first visible things, were formed from the lower waters, as if from a **Universal Air**. And in that same place, he seems to establish that the earth is, as it were, the dregs or the <term>hypostasis</term> <note>The sediment or solid foundation that settles at the bottom of a liquid.</note> of the entire mass of waters, following the <term>spagyric</term> <note>The alchemical process of separation and purification.</note> division of the world by the act of the Word and the completion of the mundane fabric itself.

But, so that these sorts of mystical secrets of creation may become even clearer to you, I will now confirm with a visual demonstration all that we have previously proven through reasons extracted partly from the Sacred Scriptures and partly from the most exact rules of true philosophy. By this, the faith of diligent readers and lovers of true philosophy may be increased with a more confident zeal to believe those things which have been said.

SECTION 1, BOOK III.

# A visual demonstration showing the reader exactly how the essential properties mentioned above arise and operate.

Before we proceed to this visual demonstration of ours, which will be performed in and through our experimental instrument, we must first consider that the **Universal Air** <note>original: "Catholicus aër." In this context, "catholic" means universal or all-encompassing, referring to the atmosphere of the entire sublunary world.</note>—or the general element of the region below the moon—is a subtler and more spiritual portion of the **Waters** below the Firmament, which Moses mentions. For this reason, it is certain that every particle of this same air corresponds to the whole; consequently, the air enclosed within the glass of this instrument is of the same nature and condition as the universal air of the world. From this it is clear that, because of their continuity, as the general air of the sublunary world is disposed, so too is the particular air enclosed in the glass (which is a part of that Universal Air). This air behaves like the <term>Spirit of God <note>original: "Ruah-Elohim"</note></term>, which moved over the waters: it animated them, gave them life, and formed them by its presence, expanding them by giving them motion. Likewise, by its absence—or the cessation of its active and agile emanation, or the contraction of its rays of activity into itself—the waters are similarly contracted, condensed, made dark, immobile, and still. This is indicated by the condition of the **North Wind**, which proceeds from the "privative" <note>In period philosophy, "privative" refers to the absence of a quality (like heat), while "positive" refers to its presence.</note> or contractive power of that Spirit.

<margin>Wisdom 7</margin>
But, just as the waters by their very existence fill the vast cavity of the world, so too the Spirit that forms all things is recognized to possess and dwell within every particle of them, as the Scriptures testify in the places previously cited. Therefore, as that Spirit works all in all—though in different properties (whence it is called "manifold")—so it sometimes works in these lower waters in its **Privative** property or virtue: namely, in its blowing from the North and the West, to a greater or lesser degree. At other times, it works in its **Positive** nature: namely, when it breathes from the South and the East. In the first property, it contracts by its coldness from the circumference toward the center, as stated above; in the latter, namely by its warm virtue, it expands from the center toward the circumference. Since, therefore, the Waters are the **Universal Passive** element—from which, as the common subject of all things, the figure of the world and all things in it were carved, graphically sculpted, and depicted, as St. Peter teaches us—and since the eternal, activating, and informing Spirit of the Lord is the **Universal Actor** and mover (as Moses testifies), it performs all things in all things within the waters. It does this in and through infinite "organs"—namely Angels, Stars, and Winds. It must follow, then, that this Spirit alone is the radical agent in the general contraction and expansion occurring both in the universal air outside the glass of the instrument and in that

<column-break/>

particular air which is inside the glass. Therefore, just as the Sun, warm winds, fire, and the heat of a natural creature derive their expansive property from the emanating and informing virtue of that Spirit, and bring it about by its power; and just as the cold temperament of the air, winds, and waters stems from a "privative" disposition: so it follows that both the expansion and contraction of the air enclosed in the glass of the instrument proceed from the immediate act of either the positive or privative property of that Spirit. For when this Spirit breathes from the North or West, the air is more or less contracted into a narrower space within the glass. We prove this to be true because, under the dominion of cold in the Universal Element, the waters are drawn higher or raised into the neck of the glass due to the contact between the water and the enclosed air. Again, it is established that the air contained in the glass is contracted more as the Northern cold holds dominion in the external air; this is apparent because it is gathered into a more confined or narrow place than it was before the water rose in the glass. On the other hand, if warm winds or the fervor of the summer Sun should "ignite" the external air, then the enclosed air will also expand itself, and in its expansion, it creates a larger space for its existence. That air is thus expanded by heat is demonstrated evidently because the water enclosed in the vessel is gradually pushed further downward than it was before. Furthermore, if anyone places their bare hand upon the hollow, bulbous top of the glass, the water suspended in the neck of the <term>Matrass <note>A matrass is a long-necked glass chemical flask.</note></term> or glass will move further downward, for the enclosed air will suddenly expand. Now indeed, the scriptures confirm in many places (both before and after in this treatise) that the life-giving spirit—which assigned this heat to both human and animal life—is that eternal spirit which, as the Apostle says, "gives life to all things." And again, this is that spirit which the Prophet calls from the four winds to restore the spirit of life, flesh, and bones to the slain. From these things, it is made manifest and visually demonstrated that **Cold** contracts from the circumference to the Center, and that it thickens and densifies the enclosed air. Although this enclosed and thickened air cannot be discerned by the eye, it is proven because the water is seen by the eyes to be raised higher in the glass by the predominance of cold. Hence, it is necessary that the bulk of the air be squeezed into a narrower space, and consequently, the air is rendered more contracted and dense. On the other hand, that **Heat** expands and dissipates the enclosed air in warm times is clear from the placement of a hand upon the top of the glass, which is followed by the depressing of the water.

### The Argument of this Book.

In this book, the author attempts to explain the entire mystery of <term>rarefaction <note>The process by which a substance becomes less dense; expansion.</note></term> and <term>condensation <note>The process by which a substance becomes more dense; contraction.</note></term> from its roots and according to the natural talent within him. Here, the wonderful causes and effects of these processes are first expressed generally in the creation of the world. Then, it is later recounted more particularly how, through their mediation, the fabric of the world was erected, the orbs of the heavens and the stars shining within them were established, and finally, how the <term>Universal Element <note>original: "Elementum Catholicum." The primary, all-encompassing substance from which everything else is made.</note></term> of the sublunary world was organized into four distinct and properly ordered regions.

->*Here, the common or Universal cause—or agent—of Condensation and Rarefaction is again presented for the careful observation of the reader: For it is proven that two essential properties or virtues, namely that of Darkness, which is Coldness, and that of Light, which is Heat, are the primary and immediate agents in both the aforementioned alterations within the Universal Element of the waters.*<-

[...negli]gence, the text could be corrupted and distanced from the original manuscript, which Saint Jerome undoubtedly possessed; otherwise, the authority, learning, and dignity of that reverend man must necessarily be called into question for such a gross and palpable error. As for his person, it is likely that the entire Christian Church would not have chosen a man of mediocre knowledge and skill in the Hebrew language for a task of such importance and for the common good of the entire Catholic Church—such as the translation of the Holy Bible from the Hebrew idiom into Latin. It would not, I say, rely on a man so lacking in Hebrew and in the judgment of divine mysteries. Therefore, from this consideration of his person, to whose diligence and care such a great work was committed, his sufficiency is established. Consequently, the fruits of his labor should in no way be weighed or compared in the scales of justice with those of Pagnini or Tremellius. <note>Sante Pagnini (1470–1536) and Immanuel Tremellius (1510–1580) were Renaissance scholars who produced new Latin translations of the Bible, often differing from Jerome's Vulgate.</note> Furthermore, no one can deny that the Pope and the entire assembly of the Roman Church assisted him in this business, providing him with ancient manuscripts to direct him in the true way and sense of interpretation, so that the consensus of ancient authority was by no means lacking in his interpretation, by which he could discern between the true and the corrupted text. And therefore, so that we neither accuse the more recent interpreters for their translation, nor detract anything from the labors and merits of Jerome (which are carved as an eternal monument of praise), we ought rather to ascribe the error to the corruption or adulteration of the Hebrew text than to any of them. This is especially true since the harmony of the scriptures in general, and the subject of this entire Psalm in which that text is recited in particular, incline more toward Jerome's interpretation than toward theirs, as I shall prove more specifically by these following arguments. The first of these is taken from the radical subject of the chapter in which these words—**"He set his tabernacle in the sun"**—are found, and also from other places in the Holy Scripture. Third, from the resolution of theologians, with other circumstances pertaining to them. Fourth, from astronomical observation and also from the dignity and excellence of the solar creature. Fifth, from arithmetic consideration. Sixth, from the point and circle in geometry. Seventh, from the consonance of greater perfection in music or harmony. Eighth, from the physical or natural respect. > The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.

By which it seems to imply that the glory of the Creator, which is within the creature, reveals the Creator to us through the creature. But where glory is present, the essence is not absent. From this it follows that this Creator, who filled the celestial sun with His glory and the influence of life and light, has clearly revealed Himself in the entire fabric of the world within the sun and by means of the sun, and from His solar tabernacle, just as will be expressly declared through His natural effects explained in the eighth order. Is this not gathered from the words of the Apostle:

<margin>Romans 1:20.</margin>
> The invisible things of God (he says) are seen from the creation of the world, being understood through those things that are made; also his eternal power and divinity, etc.

By which it becomes known that the eternal Power, and indeed even the divinity of God, are seen in creatures, and much more so in the sun, since it is fuller of light and clearer than any other creature. As Saint Augustine says: "the more light something has in itself, the more of God it seems to claim for itself." Do we not have this whole matter more lucidly explained by the wise man?

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 42:16. <note>Original: "Eccles." usually refers to Ecclesiastes, but these quotes are from the Book of Sirach, also known as Ecclesiasticus.</note></margin>
> The sun, (he says) as it shines, looks upon all things, and its work is full of the glory of the Lord, etc.

That is, it is full of the divine essence or the spirit of the Lord. Yet it is not intended that the divinity is inclusively in the sun in such a way that it is not also exclusively in and over all things; not otherwise than the spirit of human blood is said to have the heart for its principal tabernacle, and yet it is present in every particle of the whole spirit and body. Again, it appears from these words that the eternal spirit of wisdom would choose the celestial sun for its purest vessel or subject, so that it might act or work within it for the quickening, animation, and multiplication of all creatures. For this reason, she says in her own person:

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 24:5.</margin>
> I came out of the mouth of the Most High, the first-born; I made it so that in the heavens an unfailing light should arise, etc.

By these things the Catholic agent of this world argues that the sun is moved in and over it, etc. Whence also elsewhere:

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 43:5.</margin>
> The sun, when it appears, proclaiming at its rising: an admirable vessel, the work of the Most High. Great is the Lord who made it, and at his word it hastened its course, etc.

As if he had said, the sun performs its journey by the divine Word. And if anyone wishes to observe well the sense of that wise chapter, he will perceive it to agree perfectly with that Psalm of David. This Sun is that purest and most essential Light in which there is no darkness at all. Not that the Light is "included" or trapped within it, as we have said, but (as the scriptures say, that the Holy Spirit of God was in the fleshly Christ so abundantly that he was called the Word made flesh, or that the flesh was made the Word) and yet that Word or Spirit was not absent from any of the creatures, insofar as it fills all things essentially and by its presence. For this Spirit of God is in all things, as the sacred scripture records in various places.

Regarding the third point: in the book titled *The Resolution of Theologians*, we find by the consensus of all theologians that the light which was expanded everywhere through the cavity of the heavens and the world before the fourth day of creation, and which served in the place of the sun during those first three days, was on the fourth day contracted and gathered into the solar body. But that light, which was thus dispersed, was the immediate act or emanation of that spirit or **Spirit of God** <note>original: "Ruah Elohim," the Hebrew phrase for the Divine Breath or Spirit from Genesis 1:2.</note> which moved over the waters; and consequently, that light which is in the sun undoubtedly participates abundantly in Divinity, as will be clearly demonstrated in the discussion of the eighth and final argument.

The fourth point is drawn from celestial or astronomical dignity. It is evident that the solar dwelling contains no small amount of Divinity within itself, because the more perfection something has in itself, and the more it excels others in glory and dignity, the more it seems to approach Divinity. For we are taught by Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the Hermetic writings on philosophy and magic are attributed.</note> (in this way not disagreeing at all with the doctrine of Christ) that the Good and the Perfect belong to God alone. Now indeed, the dignity and perfection of the macrocosmic sun is easily discerned in this: that this royal Phoebus <note>A name for Apollo, the sun god, used here as a poetic synonym for the Sun.</note> is carried in his fiery chariot through the Center or middle-point of the heavens. Shining with golden hair, he holds a pre-eminent scepter and the government of the world like a supreme emperor. For under his jurisdiction and command, the virtues and actions of all other celestial bodies consist, as Iamblichus <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher (c. 245–325 AD) who wrote on the mysteries and the soul.</note> and many other learned men assert. And Proclus <note>A Greek Neoplatonist philosopher (412–485 AD) who systematized Neoplatonic thought.</note> says that every power or potency of the stars is gathered into one at the sight of the sun, which

Is it not also by reason of the glory of that celestial vessel or organ that the Wise Man compares the brightness of the uncreated sun (or divine emanation) with it, by reason of its beauty and radiance? <margin>Wisdom 7:29.</margin> Does not Sirach <note>original: "Syriachus," referring to the Book of Sirach or Ecclesiasticus in the Apocrypha.</note> likewise say that the fabric of the sun is full of the glory of the Lord? But more on these things when we discuss the eighth argument.

The fifth point teaches the reason, proven in the manner of Arithmetic, why a remarkable Divinity must dwell in the solar Tabernacle: namely, that it is the one and only stellar virtue from which the entire multitude of celestial stars derive their formal essence, or their Light and influence. This is no different than how all numbers, whatever they may be, are derived from Arithmetical Unity. For the number two has the form of Unity conceived twice; and Unity conceived thrice produces the number three, and so on unto infinity. Or, just as one candle lights another, and a second and a third, and so on unto infinity: so this candle informs the innumerable stars of heaven with its light, and yet preserves its own unity intact and without any loss of dignity, glory, or virtue. Finally, what could impart so many essential virtues, so many graces and ornaments to the Stars, that is not itself rich in Divinity? Or what perfection can it give which it does not have, or has not received from such great Divinity?

Regarding the sixth argument, which deals with Geometry: Since, therefore, in a Geometrical respect the sun is a spherical body, it is necessary that it be endowed with its central point, in which its power or illuminating virtue consists. This is because the circumference is nothing other than a certain semi-diametrical expansion of the existence and essence of the point, from the center to the circumference. And this is the very thing that the Philosophers intended by this axiom of theirs:

->VIRTUE AND TRUTH CONSIST IN THE CENTER.<-

Now indeed, if the admirable beauty and splendid virtue in the sun were not sent out from its Center toward the circumference, it would follow that it did not proceed from an internal Principle; and consequently, that it would require some other external illuminator, in the manner of the Moon. But that this is far otherwise is declared by the fact that there is no body in the entire universe to be equaled to this one in clarity and lucid splendor. By this it is plainly argued that this body of splendor and glory has its beginning from a certain Central Divinity or the lucid and apparent power of God, which, like a soul in the center of a creature, vivifies and activates it, moving from the center toward the circumference of the same. <margin>John 1</margin>
The **Seventh Argument**, proving that the Divine Spirit *placed His Tabernacle in the Sun*, is confirmed by musical observation based on the sun's position in the heavens. For if we consider that God, who is said to exist by Himself, is regarded by the scriptures as having His seat in the "heaven of heavens," and yet does not disdain to look upon the lower heavens, we can compare Him to a **unison** in music (if it is permitted to compare sacred things with profane). For if a string of a musical instrument is plucked openly, it will sound a unison from the bridge or base of the instrument to its head. By similar reasoning, if we imagine a string stretched from the summit of the heavens down to the center or the earth: for this entire space is filled with Divinity, no differently than a struck string of an instrument sounds equally from the head to the bridge. Again, if we press that string of the instrument exactly in the middle or the central point of the line, it will produce the most perfect harmony, the **diapason** <term>Diapason: The Greek term for an octave, considered the most perfect musical interval, representing a 2:1 ratio.</term>. For if any half of the string is plucked by itself, it will sound a Diapason relative to the whole. By this it is clear that the perfection of the whole consists or is situated in the center of the unison. For any portion of an equally divided string will be equal to the most perfect harmony relative to the whole, so that this middle point will mark the center of a circle whose diameter is that entire string. By a similar relation to the Macrocosmic Monochord <term>Monochord: An ancient scientific and musical instrument with a single string, used here by Fludd as a metaphor for the entire universe stretched between God and Earth.</term>...

Astronomers also confirm this, saying that the sun has its seat in the center of the heavens. Truly, this most splendid emanation, by which all things were created and formed in true Harmony, undoubtedly chose for itself a place in this world for its royal aspect toward the creatures, a place most perfect at the point of the diapason, which is perpetually in the middle of the unison, and consequently in the center of the Heavens. But it also appears to our eyes that the sun is disposed by the highest Creator in the midst of the seven Planets. Its player or acting Musician is the Eternal Spirit, who every minute produces tones of life and salvation for the creatures from this glorious organ, imparting to them virtues that give life, multiply, and preserve. For this is the unique office of Christ, or the eternal Word, in this world: in whom (as St. John testifies) is life.

Why then should anyone raise a question or doubt about the indwelling of this Spirit in the Sun? This, therefore, is the chief subject of this 18th Psalm <note>In the Latin Vulgate used by Fludd, Psalm 18 corresponds to Psalm 19 in modern English Bibles.</note>: this is its highest intention—to tell mortals (along with St. Paul in Romans 1 and Solomon in Wisdom 13:1) that the glory and Divinity of God appear to man through and in the heavenly creatures. Again, the philosopher Heraclitus says: "If you take the Sun from the world, what is our little body if the soul is missing?" There, no pulsing vein is felt; there is no vital condition or breathing. For this reason also, the Sun is called the **fount of blood**, which waters and moistens the other members of the body. Thus it is also clear from its effect that the power of growth and the preservation of things, both lower and higher, arises from the Sun; for it imparts and breathes life and heat into lower things by its light, and assigns formal light to higher things. And now this Light is a certain simple act which, through life-giving and innate heat, converts all things into itself; it penetrates all things and guides their virtues through all, while simultaneously dissipating and driving away shadows and darkness. By these things it is clear enough that if life in general is in the Word, as St. John says; if this Spirit of life gives life to all, as St. Paul and Judith affirm; and if the Spirit of Wisdom is the splendor of Majesty and more brilliant than the Sun, and at the same time a pure Spirit which is more

Therefore John says: "The world was made through Him, but the world did not know Him." By this speech he teaches us that it is the Spirit of God alone, and not the creature, who works all things. Consequently, we can conclude that the Spirit of God is essentially in His creatures; wherefore it is necessary that we simply trust and acknowledge Him in His works. ### ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY.

<margin>Romans 1:21, 18.</margin>
...by attending to His works, they recognized who the craftsman was, and so on. It is as if he had said: the Divinity of the Creator itself ought to be discerned by a true Christian within the creature <term>creature: in this era, "creature" refers to anything created, from a rock to a planet, not just an animal</term>. For this reason, the Apostle also says, as mentioned above: **The invisible things of God, from the creation of the world, are clearly seen, being understood through those things which are made; His eternal power also and Divinity.** <note>original: "Invisibilia Dei à creatura mundi, per ea, quæ facta sunt, intellecta conspiciuntur, sempiterna quoque ejus virtus & Divinitas."</note> Because of this, the wrath of God is revealed against such men who suppress the truth of God in injustice, etc. It is as if he said that such learned men of this world—who, through the unjust teachings of the Pagan Philosophers, attempt to turn the ignorant away from the truth—will be strictly punished by God. This is because sincere truth is the power and Divinity of God, which ought to be grasped by men. For it is not that Philosophy which consists of human tradition and follows the Elements of the world that should be embraced, but that <margin>Colossians 2:8.</margin> which is according to Christ, in whom the fullness of the Divinity dwells bodily. He, therefore, is the foundation of Philosophy and its subject. By these things, then, it is proven that Divinity can be discerned in the Creature, in and through the very sight of the Creature. But the Wise Man says: <margin>Ecclesiasticus 1.</margin> God poured out Wisdom upon all His works, according to His gift. This means He imparted a greater portion of it to one creature and a smaller portion to another. We can, therefore, look upon the "physiognomy" <note>the outward appearance as a map of the inner nature</note> of a Creature and judge from it the portion of the gift assigned to it by God. <margin>Ecclesiasticus 42:16.</margin> Yet the Text says: The work of the Solar Creature is full of the glory of the Lord. It follows, therefore, that God assigned the greatest portion of His dignity to the Solar Body among the Heavenly things, just as He chose the body of Christ as His chosen vessel—or "perfume jar" <term>myrothecium: a container for precious ointments or medicines</term>—among men, so that in it He might store His precious Divinity for the salvation of mankind.

<margin>Psalm 18:1 (Psalm 19 in modern Bibles).</margin>
We conclude, therefore, that the Royal Prophet sang correctly: "The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands." But if all the creatures of the heavens declare the glory of God, much more so, and by way of excellence, does the Solar body, which is full of the Glory of God. Therefore he continues: "In the Sun He placed His Tabernacle." <note>original: "In Sole posuit Tabernaculum suum"</note> That is, He chose the Sun as His royal place of dominion in heaven and on earth. Therefore, I say that this Spirit, who uses the Sun as His Tabernacle, distributes from it the gifts of form, life, growth, and multiplication to all creatures. And yet, I do not agree with Aristotle that "the Sun and man generate man." Rather, I believe that the powerful Spirit who gives life to all things is the only one in all things who powerfully, mercifully, and sweetly breathes and grants that force of life and the breath of natural heat to both man and all other creatures everywhere—but especially from His Solar palace. From the fullness of the Solar Tabernacle, He rains down the life-multiplication and innate heat assigned to them, by which the creatures are thereafter sustained and preserved in their being. But

<column-break/>

this (as it seems to me) is the healthy and true doctrine: to ascribe every life-giving action—both the immediate action and that which (according to the world's learning) is called "mediated"—to Him alone who alone acts and works, and not to the organic creature <note>the Sun itself as a physical tool</note> in which and through which the Creator and effector of all things is accustomed to work.

Regarding the translations by Pagninus and Tremellius <note>Santes Pagninus and Immanuel Tremellius were 16th-century scholars who produced new, literal translations of the Bible from Hebrew</note>: namely, "He placed a Tent for the Sun in them" <note>original: "Soli posuit Tentorium in ijs"</note>: if such were truly the original Text, what instruction, salvation, or benefit, I ask, could such an interpretation bring to us men? The first translation <note>the Vulgate's "In the Sun He placed His Tabernacle"</note> teaches us that the Spirit of the Lord is in the most luminous creature of heaven. From this, it warns us that we should ascribe praise and glory for His benefits to Him who made such an instrument for the health of creatures, and who works within it—and not to the creature or its Tabernacle itself. This is exactly what the Pagans did, who were accustomed to worship the rising Sun as God. Therefore, it is of the greatest use to us to be taught by this to avoid the Idolatry of the Ancient Pagans.

Furthermore, it allows us to recognize by way of excellence that Divinity reigns within the creatures. On the other hand, the second interpretation <note>the "Tent for the Sun" version</note> seems to be a matter of such small importance and so little conducive to the salvation of men that it does not seem worthy or useful enough to be written by the finger of the Spirit of God among the monuments of salvation. Consequently, what new thing could this interpretation bring to men: "God placed a Tabernacle for the Sun in the heavens"? For who is ignorant of this, or from whom could it be hidden, that the sun has its seat in the sky? Does not every child of simple intellect understand this, directed only by the evidence of their eyes without the warning of a Prophet? In what way, I ask, does that interpretation <margin>Psalm 18:1.</margin> pertain to the preceding text: "The heavens declare the Glory of God," etc.? Why would he immediately mention the Sun? Does it logically follow that God simply made a Tent for the Sun? Not in the least; rather, we should understand that the beauty and luminous glory of the heavens proceed from that splendid Spirit who made the Sun His Tabernacle, and that from Him, sweet and benevolent influences are abundantly distilled and rained down upon the creatures of the lower world.

Many Philosophers, therefore, agree on this: "In the light," they say, "is the divinity; in the divinity is the light." And Plato says: "Do not speak of God without light." # BOOK IV, SECTION ONE.

...is elsewhere **a consuming fire.** <note>original: "ignis consumens"</note> And elsewhere: it is **Light, in which there are no shadows at all.** I conclude, therefore, that St. Jerome made his interpretation in the true sense, and consequently we can gather from it the most true and fundamental reasoning for **Rarefaction** <term>Rarefaction: the process by which a substance becomes thinner or less dense, like water turning to steam</term> and **Condensation** <term>Condensation: the process by which a substance becomes thicker or more dense, like steam turning back to water</term>. Indeed, the former arises from the Sun's presence or the living activity of the spirit within the Sun, while the latter arises from its absence, and consequently from the greater or lesser ceasing of the Sun’s active heat. These, I say, are the causes of the alterations in the **Universal** <note>original: "Catholico," meaning universal or all-encompassing in a physical sense</note> Element of the lower world. This whole process is easily observed in an experimental instrument: for the more the sun approaches us, as happens in summer, the more the air in the glass will expand, which is manifested by the fact that in summer time the water is usually pushed down. On the other hand, the more the sun recedes from us, and the deeper it is immersed in the depth of winter, the more the air in the glass is condensed; and this is manifested by the rising of the water into the neck of the glass. Nor indeed do we say that the whole cause of

<column-break/>

**Rarefaction** and **condensation** proceeds solely from the Spirit existing in the sun; for that same spirit is present both in the Elementary region and the Ethereal region. It holds the power of life and the strength of the winds in its dominion, by which it either raises or lowers the waters in the glass in both winter and summer. Consequently, it is the immediate cause of the condensation and Rarefaction of the air both inside and outside the instrument's glass. In this way, it effects the daily change of the fourfold condition in the general Elementary waters below the moon—or the universal element of Moist Nature—changing it in many ways from one state to another. These changes in that Element were called "the Elements" by the Ancients, whom our own scholars follow, as will be demonstrated more clearly below. But first, let us approach the reasoning behind the construction of the heavens, a work which was completed through Condensation and Rarefaction by the operation of the *Ruach Elohim* <note>original: "Ruach Elohim," Hebrew for the Spirit of God</note>, as will be explained in the following chapter.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*By what means the eternal Ruach-Elohim, or Spirit of the Lord, which moved upon the waters, formed and arranged the heavens out of them through Rarefaction, and how He produced the stars within them by way of condensation.*<-

<margin>2 Peter 3:5</margin>
It is indeed the assertion of the Apostle Peter that the heavens existed long ago, and the earth was formed out of water and through water by the Word of God. From this discourse, we derive both the "material cause" from which the world and consequently the heavens were created—namely, the waters—as well as the "efficient cause" or the Divine Architect in that stupendous work: specifically the Word or *Ruach-Elohim*. Through Him, such a construction was made and sustained by the act of rarefaction and condensation. For by the way of condensation, the thin and invisible waters, and then those thick visible waters, were contracted into the visible earth; He performed all these things with His cold breath. Therefore, after the subtle waters were divided from the thick ones while still in a confused state, the Spirit of the Lord (or the Word) set about the construction of the heavens by means of greater or lesser Rarefaction. First, by His most vivid, agile, and bright breath, He refined the upper waters and assigned the rarer and more noble portion of them to the construction of the **Empyrean Heaven** <term>Empyrean: the highest part of heaven, thought by ancient philosophers to be made of pure fire or light</term>. He so animated and shaped it with His fiery spirit that it might remain in that state perpetually by the power of the Word. Because of the dominion of that Divine spirit within it, it is called the "fiery" or "Empyrean" and "intellectual" heaven. Therefore, this blessed place, because of the abundant presence of God within it, is assigned as the dwelling place of the good Angels and blessed souls. Next, that Spirit approaches the lowest portion of these upper waters with a lesser power of Rarefaction,

<column-break/>

and according to His pleasure, He distinguished them into eight spheres or regions. These are: the heaven called the "firmament," which He later ordained as the seat of the fixed stars; and the heavens or spheres of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon. He arranged all these spheres by His rarefactive power and caused them to stand apart and differ from one another so that they might best suit both their location and nature, according to the properties granted or "breathed" into the individual stars by God through His great Angel. ...and in the proper and fitting number, namely into the Empyrean heaven <note>The highest, most spiritual part of heaven, associated with pure fire and light.</note>, the Firmament, and seven distinct spheres, along with infinite condensed bodies. For although the heavens are composed of air and fire—that is, from a portion of the fiery Spirit which it received from the luminous Spirit of the **Elohim** <note>original: "Elohim," a Hebrew name for God</note>, and a portion of thin water, which is why the Ether is often called a sort of "fiery air" <margin>Hebrews 11:3</margin>—nevertheless, we are instructed by the axiom of St. Paul, who says that visible things were first made from invisible things. Thus, we learn that both the visible bodies in the sky and all visible lights were originally derived from invisible waters and invisible formal light, which has its root in the primary unity of God, the source of all created numbers. Therefore, as **Aristotle** <note>The Greek philosopher whose physics dominated medieval and Renaissance thought.</note> says, the stars are the denser portions of their spheres; so I also say that the substance of heaven is invisible because of its "rarefaction" <note>its thinness or lack of density</note>. Conversely, the stars are visible because of their "condensation." For it was condensation that produced visibility, while rarefaction was the cause of invisibility.

And yet, we do not conclude with Aristotle that the stars are simply denser parts of their spheres, but rather they are lights that were enclosed within the spirit of the **Dark Abyss**. This spirit, during the separation of light from darkness, tended upward by the power of the light’s fiery nature enclosed within it. Thus, it is sustained according to the proportion of the formal, eternal fire it contains—which it retains to this day as a "Cornerstone" in the elevated position assigned to it. It is not unlike that artificial fire called a **firework or rocket** <note>original: "Pyrobolus seu fujus"</note>, which we see rise higher or lower in the air according to the proportion of **gunpowder** <note>original: "pulveris Bombardalis"</note> or artificial fire relative to the weight of its body. There it remains while the power of its corruptible fiery life lasts; when that fails, it falls back down. But stellar light—the spiritual body in which it resides—having been raised out of the darkness, ascends as high as the proportion of its enclosed light allows, and stays there by its own agile power, considering the weight of the stellar body. Thus, it hangs perpetually in the ether at a fixed distance from the center. This is because its fire or light is of an incorruptible and eternal nature and will never fail like that of a rocket. You will find all of this expressed more clearly in Tract 1, Book 5, Chapter 3 of my *History of the Macrocosm*, to which I refer you. Now, just as all illuminating strengths and life-giving virtues or flames imparted to the universal waters are given to them by that splendid spirit or emanation, so there are none of those lights that are separated from the essence of that spirit. From this it follows—since every light had a different proportion of formal clarity and a specific measure of bodily thickness—that one celestial body differs from another in its position and the power of its brightness, as well as in its motion and influence, according to the will of the Creator. We see, therefore, from the consensus of the wise Fathers of the Church, what the cause is of the cold, condensing night, and who is the author of the hot, rarefying day. And this, therefore, must be the primary reason for all condensation and rarefaction to this day. ### CHAPTER V.

### How the lower waters—otherwise called the Catholic, watery, sublunary Element—were distinguished into distinct spheres (which the worldly call Elements) and arranged by the Divine act of Condensation and rarefaction.

<margin>Genesis 1</margin>
Since it has been clearly demonstrated through the preceding arguments that the entire substance of the world-machine would not exist except from a single, solitary matter—which was extracted from the bowels of the potential **Dark Abyss** by the spagyric <term>Spagyric: an alchemical term referring to the art of separating and recombining elements to purify them</term> power of the Divine Word—which <margin>2 Peter 3, 4</margin> **Moses** (as was reported) called "the waters," and **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary sage to whom many foundational texts of alchemy and philosophy were attributed.</note> called "moist nature"; from which and through which (as both Moses and Peter say) the heavens and the earth existed previously through the Word—it must follow that from this **Catholic** <note>original: "Catholicum," used here in its original sense meaning "universal" or "all-encompassing," rather than referring to the Roman Catholic Church.</note> mass of waters, the universal sublunary Element (so commonly distinguished by the name of "air") as well as that portion of moist nature called "ether," was fundamentally derived. For the mass of visible waters was first extracted and separated from the invisible air by condensation; and again, that visible water was changed into earth by the same act. Does not the Apostle confirm this in the place previously cited, saying: By <margin>Hebrews 11:3</margin> faith we recognize that it has always been thus with the world through the Word, so that from those things which could not be seen, those things which can be seen were made? Furthermore, **Solomon** <note>Referring to the Book of Wisdom, traditionally attributed to Solomon.</note> says that the world was made or created from invisible matter, and consequently, so were water and earth. But what need is there for sacred Authority, when common experience teaches us that condensed air becomes a cloud, and a cloud becomes rainwater, and ice (which is of the nature of earth) is made from water by Northern condensation? Furthermore, that earth was once water, and that water was air, is evident in this: that great trees, by burning, are turned into vaporous smoke and consequently into air; finally, air is changed into fire by excessive thinning. By these things it is certain that earth and waters were first extracted from an invisible thing—namely, from the Catholic air—and consequently it is proved that the Catholic air of the world, which Hermes called "moist nature," is the Catholic Element of the sublunary world. Through its various mutations, that fourfold nature is produced which is commonly called the "four elements," which in truth are nothing but one Element

altered in a fourfold way. For it is evident from what has been said that the Catholic sublunary air is the radical subject and material substance of those things which the world calls "Elements." And that air is altered from one state to another through the Word or **Ruach-Elohim**. Now let us consider with ourselves how that powerful spirit accomplishes its Protean <note>Protean: like the Greek god Proteus, capable of assuming many shapes; ever-changing.</note> transmutations in one and the same homogeneous, invisible water and thin, moist nature or air. By this, the rotation of one nature into another appears more clearly; these natures, being so different, are therefore called "Elements" by the ancients. It is necessary, therefore, that we consider first that this was that life-giving spirit <margin>Ezekiel 37:5</margin> whom the Prophet invoked from the four winds, saying: "Come, O spirit, from the four winds and breathe upon these slain, that they may live again," etc. From this it is clear that this unique spirit, the **Ruach-Elohim**, was the royal commander of the four winds, and consequently, it was in its power to contract the air by the mediation of its windy organs, and again to dilate it. Therefore, it was without doubt this spirit, and no other, which commanded the various souls or dispositions of the four winds and their Angelic overseers (whose duty it is to govern under him), and agitates the invisible air into various visible or meteorological species, where and when it pleases him. And first, regarding his general act of forming true <margin>Job 37:21</margin> images from the Catholic air: "Air," says **Job**, "is suddenly gathered into clouds, and the passing wind shall drive them away." From all these things we can note and infer that the visible elementary air is the real and radical subject in which the spirit of God works in this sublunary world to bring the aforementioned visible effects into action.

### BOOK IV OF THE FIRST SECTION.

<margin>Habakkuk 3:3.</margin> confirms this: "God came from the South, His glory covered the heavens and the earth was full of His praise: His brightness was like the light, and Death shall go before His face." <note>The author is quoting a Latin version of Habakkuk 3:3-5, often used in mystical physics to describe the movement of divine power.</note> And the Devil—or as Pagninus <note>Santes Pagnino (1470–1541), a Dominican friar and leading Hebraist of the Renaissance known for his literal translation of the Bible.</note> has it, the "pestilence"—shall go forth at his feet. By this, he seems to indicate invisible effects, namely the corruption and infection of the **Universal Element of Air**, which that spirit, in its wrath and malevolence, sends out from the South.

<margin>FIRE.</margin> Truly, when the Spirit operates through its windy instruments of the East, it generates fiery or parching impressions in the Universal Element. For its existence in nature alters the disposition of fire, and then the Philosophers ascribe the title of the "Fiery Element" to it. We can confirm this from many places in the Sacred Text: For, the Lord commanded (as Jerome says in his translation) a hot and burning wind, or (as Tremellius <note>Immanuel Tremellius, a 16th-century Jewish convert and leading biblical scholar whose Latin Bible was highly esteemed for its accuracy.</note> interprets it): 
<margin>Jonah 4:8.</margin> "He prepared a silent East wind," so that the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, so much so that he grew faint, and requested of his soul that he might die. And elsewhere: 
<margin>Ezekiel 19.</margin> "A parching wind" or "the East wind shall dry up its fruit and its branches shall be shriveled with decay." <note>The author likely cites Ezekiel 19:12.</note> And again: <margin>Genesis 41.</margin> "The East wind shall scorch 
<margin>Amos 4:9.</margin> the ears of grain." And elsewhere Jehovah says in his wrath: "I have struck you with a parching wind," etc. And again: "After the East wind comes, the wind of Jehovah ascending from the desert, its spring shall fail and its fountain shall be dried up." And 
<margin>Hosea 13:15.</margin> <note>The source text cites Hosea 2:18, but the content matches 13:15.</note> the Prophet Haggai: "I struck you with a parching wind," 
<margin>Haggai 2:17.</margin> etc. From these things it is clear that when the East wind (or *Eurus*) blows, the Universal Element—which is moist by nature—becomes parched and fiery, so that it inflames and disturbs the bodies of creatures with hot excess, and destroys vegetation by drying and scorching it. Finally, from the opposite side: West winds are found by experience to be opposite in nature and condition to the East winds. For they are accustomed to reduce the Universal Element back into the cold and moist nature of visible water: from which they bring forth rains and warm showers. Thus, from these examples one may see that the formal act in any of the four Angels at the corners of the earth (whom the 
<margin>Revelation 7:1.</margin> Apocalypse mentions) has an essential power assigned to it specially by God according to His will; and that this was assigned in the instant of its creation or formation. Therefore, that Angelic creature operates in that same property within the common Element of the "lower waters," in which the will of the creating Spirit specifically resided when He formed it. Thus, the common or **Universal Element** is informed daily anew by the essential act of the Angelic wind blowing with dominion in it at that time. For example, if the Eastern Angelic wind informs it anew, then it migrates into the condition of the Element of Fire: because it heats and dries preeminently by reason of the excessive **Rarefaction** <term>Rarefaction: the process of making a substance thinner or less dense, the opposite of condensation</term> of the air. If, however, the Southern Angelic winds send their smoky breaths into that element,

<column-break/>

then it is altered into the vaporous nature of Air, because in a smoky manner it is rendered hot and moist. Thus it plays the part of the Element of Air. If the Western Angelic winds have dominion in it, then it is turned into the temperament of simple water, and remains under the name of the Element of Water. And finally, the breaths of the North wind (*Boreas*) render it earthy.

Therefore, from these points, that immense and labyrinthine doubt—which, like another **Gordian Knot**, has for so long disturbed the minds of the Peripatetics <note>Peripatetics: followers of Aristotle's philosophy. The "Gordian Knot" refers to an unsolvable problem.</note> and has never been resolved by them to this very day—can be most easily dissolved and unraveled through our discipline. Namely, we can divine what the essential form of the elements truly is. For by this philosophy of ours, we are taught that it is a certain essential Angelic virtue sent out via a windy vehicle into the open field of the Universal Element; or (if you prefer) it is an essential blast or breath of wind sent from the Spirit of God into the common air (or the passive moist nature) to alter and change it from one condition to another according to the will of Him who sent it. Furthermore, the Universal Air, animated in such diverse ways, is accustomed to produce "meteors" <term>Meteors: in this era, this referred to any atmospheric phenomenon including rain, snow, or lightning, not just falling stars</term> of many conditions. For example, the Element when changed in an Eastern manner brings forth offspring like itself: namely, ignited meteors, such as flashes of lightning, thunderbolts, ignited comets, etc., according to the nature of the "seeds" of that breath which has newly informed it. The Southern Element will bring forth vapors, sultry clouds, lightning, and thunder. The Western Element will produce rains, cold showers, and snow-like meltings. The Northern Element produces snow, frost, ice, etc. Finally, for a clearer unraveling of the aforementioned doubt, it must be known that God gives life to all things through **Jesus Christ our Lord** alone, through whom all things exist. He created the Angelic "organs" whom He inspired with His spirit, the essential life. Since this essential spirit in the Angels is of the Divine Essence, it cannot be separated from Divinity. Therefore, that essence assigned to any Angel retains the same will and disposition that the Spirit had in the act of breathing into him. For there is no creature which He did not make for a purpose best known to the Creator Himself: namely, so that He might fulfill His will in this or that property. Hence, it is not that there is an Angel who simply "owns" this or that cardinal wind, but rather it is the Divine Spirit acting in the Angel as an instrument, who informs and vivifies the Universal Element in this or that essence-making virtue. Therefore, it is certain that the daily formation of the single Universal Element is a virtue or act of Divinity through an Angelic organ...

But as for our **Universal Element**, <note>original: "Elementum nostrum Catholicum." In this context, "Catholic" means "Universal" or "all-encompassing" rather than referring to the Church.</note> I know that it will be objected by the "wise" of this world: "If there is only one Element, which you call Universal, what will you do about the Earth? And what do you think of the water or the sea? Are these not distinct Elements that have existed as such from the beginning?" To these I answer that the earth was previously from the waters and through the waters, as the Apostle Peter testifies. <note>referring to 2 Peter 3:5.</note> Wherefore it is evident that the waters preceded the earth in time; and again, the heavens were made before the earth. Therefore, it appears that the earth was nothing but the dregs and sediment <note>original: "fax & sedimentum"</note> of the lower waters, separated by the <term>spagyric</term> <note>Spagyric refers to the alchemical art of separating and recombining substances to reach a purer state.</note> power of the Word, as appears from the teaching of Moses. Furthermore, that the visible waters were formed and produced from invisible air through condensation is testified by the Apostle in the place cited above. <margin>Hebrews 11.</margin> Wherefore it is clear that the changes of all things, both visible and invisible, are brought about by the condensing and contracting property or faculty of the Spirit of God acting in many forms; and that the reduction of them back from a state of visibility into invisibility is brought about by the act of rarefying

<column-break/>

and expanding of that same Spirit—which is one in essence, but multiform in the property of its action. Consequently, just as air is transformed by the same act of the Spirit into water, and water into earth, through degrees of cold condensation, so also by the contrary act of the same Spirit—namely, by way of Rarefaction—earth is changed into water and water into air; and this by various degrees of heat. Indeed, if this were not so, how, I ask, would it be possible that so much water falling from the clouds does not daily cause the seas to swell and increase wonderfully in quantity, while the air, on the contrary, would steadily decrease? Or why, when so many trees and fossil coals are consumed by fire, is the earth not diminished? This would happen if there were not a constant replenishment through the transmutation of air into water and water into earth. Although the divine nature effects this alteration or "rotation of nature" in a secret and imperceptible manner, yet daily experience teaches that this is the case. For when wood and coals are resolved and consumed by fire, we find indeed that their entire earthly bulk has gone off into aqueous smoke and will be changed into vaporous air. Now, it is a philosophical axiom that "any thing is resolved into its first matter or principle." Therefore, it is manifest that both the water and the airy smoke, from which the composition of the earth of wood and coals was made, were previously invisible air. Again, if these elements did not exchange with one another, the sulfur, powders, and stones daily descending from the sky (as Scripture testifies) <note>Likely referring to accounts of meteorites or "fire and brimstone."</note> would increase the mass of the earth more and more every day. But, setting aside these speculative proofs, I shall proceed to clearly demonstrate and confirm all the aforesaid things for you from the observation of my experimental instrument.

### A Visual Demonstration.

We observe that the entire portion of the instrument, or "Calendar Glass," <note>An early type of thermoscope or weather-glass used to observe changes in air volume due to temperature and pressure.</note> which extends from the lowest part of the glass neck to its top or head, is filled only with invisible air. Yet, in that small amount of enclosed air, quite a few various alterations and changes are found by the power and act of the four winds blowing in the open air. For when the **East Wind** blows with dominance, then that enclosed air dilates and expands itself in the neck of the glass, and it presses the water (which had been raised by the power of cold) downward, more or less according to the degree of the heat's dominance. From this it is clear that the expanding spirit of such a wind causes the open air to incline toward a fiery nature; insofar as fire is discerned to be nothing other than extremely dilated air, even though in reality it is the overflowing presence of a light-form, which so dilates it through the heat that perpetually accompanies its motion. But if the

<column-break/>

**South Wind** blows, then the enclosed air also flows out, but not to the degree of fire, but only of air; and consequently, it does not push the water (which was raised into the neck of the glass by cold) down through as many degrees. However, if the **West Wind** has dominance in the free air, then the air enclosed in the glass will render itself even thicker; and for that reason, it does not thrust down the water exalted in the neck very much, because coldness has sufficient power in that wind and consequently condenses the air more than it dilates it. Finally, if the **North Winds** govern in the world’s air, then the enclosed air will be all the more contracted and compressed, and consequently will require less space for its habitation, the colder the act of those winds shall be. This is proved by the fact that the colder the wind is, the higher the water will be raised in the neck of the glass. From which it is established that the more the air is contracted...

**2. ○○** argues for the actual emanation of uncreated light from the unity or divine potential, by whose presence a moist nature appeared out of the **Dark Abyss** (namely from **1.**) in the form of waters. Therefore the series stands thus: **3. ○○○**, as light, water or air, and heaven. The final scale in the progression to the creation of the world stands thus: **4. ○○○○**, which implies the fourfold alteration of the Universal Element, effected by the word of God in the four winds of the world on the third day of creation. For that Universal element was nothing else than the general waters of the sublunary region altered in a fourfold way; or, if you prefer, let the **4. ○○○○** stand for the four Elements.

This, therefore, was the state of the world at its creation, and it remains in plainly the same condition to this very day, and shall remain in the future until it perishes and is purified by a **fiery trial** at the end. <note>original: "igneo examine." ...the principle of principles, that is, as much the principle of **privation** <note>original: "privatio"; in Renaissance philosophy, this refers to the absence or withdrawal of a quality, leading to decay.</note> and **corruption**, as of **position** <note>original: "positio"; the act of placing or establishing something into existence.</note> and **generation**; of which one is the radical act of life, namely **Light**: and the other is the passive subject of both life and death, namely the **Waters**, insofar as they were revealed out of the darkness. From this it follows that, by reason of the darkness, they participate in their passive state in both the privative and the positive principle. For this reason, the actor in both extremes is God himself, who is **Unity**. By withdrawing his life-giving spirit from the watery existence of the creature, He brings it under the dominion of the privative principle; from this, **Death** and **corruption** follow. On the contrary, through the continuation and presence of the incorruptible spirit in the creature, the creature remains without corruption by the spirit's power. Furthermore, just as God, after He has withdrawn His spirit from the creature, causes it to die; so indeed, by returning that same spirit of life to the creature, He causes it to live again and rise from the dead. This was the reason for the resurrection of our Savior in one sense—who for this cause was called the "first-born of the Resurrection"—and in another sense, it was the cause by which Elijah raised the widow’s son from the dead, and by which the bones of Elisha caused the slain Amalekite to rise again; and also why Christ restored the dead Lazarus to life, as will be discussed more widely in what follows.

Here, first of all, it seems to be acknowledged that every creature was made by eternal wisdom, and there it denotes that creatures live by the presence of this Divine Spirit. When God (says the Text) gives to the creatures, they gather and are filled with goodness (that is, they live). By "turning away His face" (that is, the living sight of His spirit) they are troubled (that is, if He partially turns away His sight or spirit from the creatures, they grow sick and weak). By "taking away their spirit" (that is, if they completely receive back into themselves the incorruptible ray of life) they fail (that is) they die. But if He sends forth the spirit of life again, they shall be recreated, and "you shall renew the face of the earth" (that is, by the returning of the incorruptible Spirit they will live again, and rise anew to life). It is manifest, therefore, that by the presence and kindly action of the incorruptible Spirit of God, life is present and continued in the creature: and conversely, by its total absence, death is introduced. But by its partial withdrawal and its **contraction** <note>original: "contractione"; Fludd believes life is an expansion of the spirit outward, while sickness and death are the spirit shrinking back toward the center.</note> from the circumference to the center, the creature is troubled and grows sick; for it cannot die as long as any portion of the incorruptible spirit of God remains in it.
