### APPENDIX TO THE FIRST SECTION

...you bring such great loss and evil upon the Christian Church while you train your disciples in pagan <note>original: *Ethnica*; refers to non-Christian, specifically classical Greek and Roman, culture and philosophy</note> doctrine from their very cradles. You thrust that poison into their mouths like pre-chewed food <note>original: *veluti præmanſum*; a vivid metaphor comparing the teaching of classical texts to a nurse feeding a child food she has already chewed</note>, by which they are led away from true and healthy doctrine. Furthermore, by this profession of yours in pagan writers, you provide an excuse to the pagans themselves, preventing them from embracing the Christian faith; instead, they persist even more obstinately in their blindness. God will seek and demand the blood of those who have been seduced—those hindered from eternal salvation—at your hands. Do you not think it will come to pass at the Last Judgment that your disciples, whom you led away from God, and the pagans, whom you hindered from reaching the knowledge of truth, will most gravely accuse you and complain of you in the highest degree? The former will complain because you led them from the true path of the Christian religion into the trackless wilds of the pagans; the latter because, through your public lectures and the profession of pagan writers in your schools, you confirmed them in their heresies and errors. You rendered them so much more obstinate that they never heard the solid principles and foundations of Christian truth among you; much less were they warned to abandon false doctrine and idolatry to embrace the true Christian religion and seek Christ the Savior within it. Yet, you do not yet believe these things will happen; but to your great misfortune, you will eventually experience them to be only too true. Or perhaps it

<column-break/>

seems a light thing to you to abandon the fear of God and divine precepts to follow the false doctrine of the pagans? Are you ignorant that the deities and idols of the pagans are true devils, from whom they borrowed their false doctrine, arts, prophecies, and deceptions? What were Apollo, Diana, Jupiter—what were the Sibyls? What were the "mountain women" <note>likely referring to Oreads or local Germanic folklore spirits</note>, the Pygmies? What were the forest gods? What were the virgins or water Nymphs? Did they not consult all of these in their needs and difficulties? Meanwhile, they abandoned the true and only God, who nevertheless offers you all grace and mercy of His own accord. He wishes to open and reveal to you things past, present, and future—indeed, the great and wonderful mysteries along with His treasures. And yet, a madness still drives you to prefer following the devil and his lying oracles, seeking counsel from them and promoting their false and fabricated doctrine, rather than adhering to and being saved by the living God alone. Do you not know that He is a "jealous God" <note>original: *Deum fortem, zelotem*; a reference to Exodus 20:5</note>, who will not give His honor to another, but requires that we fear Him alone and observe only His precepts and decrees? He requires that we turn away from all pagan and idolatrous things, and by no means have or adore any other God besides Him. Thus you see that all your actions and works are mere vanity, in which you will utterly perish unless you bid farewell to pagan doctrine and turn with your whole heart to God and His teaching.

Although the essence of the spirit is exceedingly bright, splendid, and fiery, nevertheless that splendor—with its light and fire—is in no way perceived. Rather, all these things are hidden from bodily eyes, which are covered and hindered by thick darkness. Indeed, this darkness is so great that the splendor of the Sun can scarcely penetrate and illuminate them enough for them to perceive this visible light and contemplate God's creatures. And, although these holy ones <note>referring to spirits or angels</note> are quite great in their essence, and moreover the transparent heaven itself along with the air is entirely filled with these spirits and angels, no mortal possesses such holiness and integrity—nor is anyone reconciled with God in such a way—that they can behold even the smallest spirit with the sharp-sightedness of their eyes.

<column-break/>

The sole cause of this situation and evil are those carnal and damnable works: the unjust, fornicators, adulterers, the lewd, and incontinent Sodomites, the greedy, the luxurious, the blasphemers, etc. Likewise, such people will see absolutely no Holy Spirit or Angel in its true essence. Fol. 63.

# ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY. Fol. 63.

Indeed, this world is blinded to such an extent that no one believes such grace can be shown to a man by God that he might see a spirit. This unbelief betrays and identifies them as false Christians, whose faith does not even equal the size of a grain of mustard seed <note>A reference to Matthew 17:20; the author argues that even a tiny amount of true faith should be capable of moving mountains or performing miracles</note>; rather, it is nothing at all. Yet these very people wish to be regarded as Christians and as Sons of God, even though they possess no faith that is effective and alive. They believe only with the mouth, but in no way with the heart; they think it sufficient for themselves if they confess their faith only with their mouths and lips, while meanwhile their heart is as far from it as possible—separated by a distance no less than that which divides the East from the West. It is necessary for faith to take root in the heart and breast, and from there to grow upward and bring forth fruits worthy of a Christian man. Therefore, these people boast of their faith in vain, since not even the smallest fruit of faith is discovered in them.

Who among them, by the greatness and constancy of his faith, has restored health to his neighbor? Or who has himself recovered through it? Who has beheld any divine vision by the power of his faith? Or who, through its truth and constancy, has obtained anything memorable or noteworthy? Let even one come forward out of many thousands of thousands and show at least the smallest effect of his faith. I would make a wager that you are all going to say that you could not heal the official’s son <note>original: *filium Decurionis*; likely referring to the story of the royal official's son in John 4:46-54</note>; and if asked at the same time what the cause is that you were less willing to perform it, the Lord will answer you: that this impossibility lies with your unbelief. If you cannot certainly work anything, you do not have true faith. If you do not have true faith, you are not Christians. And if you are not Christians, why do you glory in the Christian faith? Surely this path of glorying and boasting ought to be blocked, and you should be excommunicated until a promise is made that you will admit and teach a better and fuller instruction of faith in the Christian Schools.

As long as this does not happen, you are to be regarded as unbelieving Pagans <note>original: *Ethnicis*; refers to non-Christians or those following classical Greco-Roman traditions rather than the Gospel</note> and must be expelled from Christian society. For you treat Christ with indignity while you profess his name and faith but are caught in your lies. Indeed, because of this, the name of Christ is torn apart with blasphemy and insults among the Gentiles, because your faith is empty and dead, and performs or achieves nothing at all in the name of Jesus. You Magistrates, what care do you take for your Schools? How is your youth instructed in the faith? Where are your Christian books? In what way do your Teachers present Moses, the Prophets, and the Gospels along with the Epistles? When, finally, will the fruits and

<column-break/>

operations of faith follow from their teaching? How is it that no effect of that thing is seen? Truly, your pagan and poisonous books, and your damnable sophistries <note>original: *Sophisticationes*; refers to the complex, logical hair-splitting of Scholastic philosophy which the author believes obscures simple biblical truth</note>, are at fault; they hinder you from being able to produce any work or fruit of faith.

But you, in truth, have something far different to answer, asserting of course that there is no need for miracles at this time, since those signs were necessary only in the Primitive Church so that the unfaithful might be converted to the Christian faith. You claim that such things are no longer desired in this age of ours, but that it is enough for the faith to be presented to men through sermons without miracles. I, however, my friends, would like you to answer me on one point: What did Christ do? What did his Apostles do while they traveled in this world? Is it not true that they taught and announced repentance, the remission of sins, and the kingdom of God for eternal life through faith in Jesus Christ? And did they not likewise heal those sick in both body and soul, cast out demons, and thus leave an example for posterity to follow in teaching the people and healing the bodies and souls of the sick?

Or did the Lord not also send his Apostles into the world in this manner? "Go into the whole world and announce the Gospel to every creature; he who believes and is baptized shall be saved; but he who does not believe shall be condemned. And these are the signs that follow those who believe: In my name they will cast out demons, they will speak with new

<margin>Mark 16. Luke 10.</margin>

languages, they will drive away serpents, and if they drink any poison, it will not harm them; they will lay hands on the sick and they will be healed." <note>A translation of the Latin paraphrase of Mark 16:15–18</note> Indeed, those who believe will perform miracles much greater than those which the Savior himself performed. So also the Lord signaled his works through messengers, namely: the blind see, the lame walk, the

<margin>Matthew 11. Luke 7. Isaiah 61.</margin>

lepers are healed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, and the Gospel is announced to the poor. Thus you see what sort of doctrine ought to be in your Schools, what your Teachers ought to say, and by what method it is necessary for them to present, announce, and spread the faith along with its fruits.

To teach and believe without the fruits of your faith is to be regarded in no other way than that of the unbelieving Pagans, who neither announce the faith nor work the fruits of faith. Nay, you are even worse and more wicked than the Pagans themselves, inasmuch as you glory in faith and yet prove it by no deed. For, according to God's command, doctrine and works must be joined. But let someone dare to approach within your borders who heals the sick by his faith, who casts out demons by prayers and fasting, or performs other works...

->### APPENDIX TO THE FIRST SECTION<-

...expedite the Christian cause: Is it not true that you are continually asserting that anyone who performs such works is a Samaritan and has a devil <note>original: "Samaritanum & habere diabolum"; a reference to the accusations against Jesus in John 8:48</note>, and that he accomplishes all these things through the devil’s power and might? But if the devil can provide this, what can you provide? Or is the devil more effective than your faith? It is your duty to cast out demons through faith in Jesus Christ. Yet you completely invert this, attributing that honor to the devil—claiming he effects this or 그—by which very act he besieges you, weakening and undermining your faith. What "excellent" Christians you are! When did any devil ever cast out another? How would his kingdom stand? When did a devil ever heal the sick in body and soul? 

And if indeed the devil can perform such great things, where is your Christian faith, which ought to be demonstrated by such following signs? Truly, you are cold and listless Christians; I would not buy your faith for a hollow nut, since you are able to produce absolutely no effect through it. Your schools are partly Pagan <note>original: "Ethnicæ"</note> and partly Christian, and here is the origin of every evil: while you corrupt your children with those absurdities, you prevent them from being able to attain and embrace the true foundation of the Christian faith. In those schools, the books and sciences of the Pagans are read to them, while in the meantime, a profound silence is maintained regarding how God—for the kind granting of His Grace, favor, wisdom, understanding, and Holy Spirit—is to be invoked. Nor is it taught how those divine gifts, along with the confirmation of faith, are to be petitioned and obtained, so that all diseases might be healed in that most effective name of Jesus Christ, demons cast out, and unbelievers converted to the true Christian faith. Your Doctors and schoolmasters <term>Ludimoderatores; literally 'play-leaders,' a common term for grammar school teachers</term> ought to be occupied with this. 

<column-break/>

But you cannot be persuaded of these things. Hence it happens that you cannot even stir a mustard seed with your faith. How then will you obtain from God that illumination of your eyes by which you might see any Holy Spirit, or an Angel, or even God Himself in His glorious essence? You are so truly blinded by these darknesses of yours that you can distinguish neither day from night, nor truth from falsehood. Much less can you protect yourselves from that poison of the Pagans, filled with the devil's pestilential arrows, for you are already so infected and occupied by it that in your blindness you mix the sacred with the profane. You neither know nor see God or His saints in their essence. Convert at last! Purify your schools, cleanse your hearts, and call upon the Holy Spirit; only then will your faith be so confirmed that you may produce the signs of your faith and behold spiritual realities.

### The third part of this appendix from chapter 105, book 5, of the *Table of the Revelation of Divine Majesty*, in which the creation of the Thunderstone is discussed against the Peripatetics. <note>The Peripatetics were the followers of Aristotle; the author is challenging the standard Aristotelian meteorology of the time.</note>

---

The greatest part of men cannot be led to believe that anything falls or is cast down from the air to the earth. If ever frogs, cows, calves, or other miraculous things fall <note>Reports of "animal rain" were common in early modern wonder-books</note>, they think all these were first suddenly lifted into the air by the force of the wind and thus later fell back to the earth. When they hear that a thunderbolt <note>original: "jaculum tonitrui"</note>—polished like some transparent crystal, or even a Thunderstone <term>Ceraunium lapidem; "thunderstones" were often ancient stone tools found in the earth, which people believed fell from the sky during storms</term> of white, blue, green, and various other colors—is sent down from heaven, by which houses, towers, fortresses, and even sometimes stony cliffs are crushed, shattered, and set on fire, they respond with an explanation. They say those stones are born from fine dust raised upward by the heat of the Sun and drawn into moist clouds, where they are squeezed into partly oblong and partly round shapes. Once hardened, they claim the stones are violently cast down and dislodged when a more vehement heat exerts its power against the moist clouds. 

This is that so-often-chanted Aristotelian Philosophy. It is a sorrow that they speak so futilely, ineptly, and ridiculously concerning the miracles of God, turning their backs on true knowledge and delighting in these lying dreams as a substitute for the truth. They are not even ashamed to

<column-break/>

boast and glory in them. But it is difficult to turn them away from their absurdities, even though they ought to know that these stones are prepared by the Angels of God and sent down from above. Even those animals mentioned earlier are born in the water in higher regions, as was briefly indicated before. The air itself and the heaven were made from water and even now are water <note>This reflects a "Mosaic" cosmology where the firmament divides the "waters above" from the "waters below" (Genesis 1:7)</note>; and all gems and metals in the earth arise and grow from water. 

It follows, therefore, that gems and metals are made from water in the air or heaven, and are sometimes cast down into these lower parts. Thus, those golden flints and other stones born above in the water are cast down to us humans on earth in many places, through which divine miracles are revealed and God is celebrated among the human race. However, although these and other points are very frequently disputed in many places to explode the doctrine of the Pagans—and are proposed, confirmed, and announced upon the solid foundations of truth in the assembly of Christians—nevertheless, no effect truly and actually follows from it. Indeed, even in this age of ours, one may see how the books of the Pagans are used not only in all Universities and common schools <term>Trivialibus scholis; referring to schools teaching the Trivium: grammar, logic, and rhetoric</term>, in the cities...

Fol. 64.

-># ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY.<-

...in cities and towns they are read and drilled into the youth; but furthermore, they are even illustrated with immense commentaries, not without the highest devotion, labor, and sweat, by both Churchmen and secular scholars alike. In these works, there are various disputes concerning the immortality of the soul, its essence and actions, and other matters more than well-known—yet in such a way that nothing follows from it, except as if a cow were to lick its calf clean; for that calf then remains exactly as it was <note>This is a colorful proverbial way of saying that for all the "polishing" and effort the scholars put in, the underlying pagan subject matter remains unchanged and unimproved.</note>. In the same way, I say, the matter stands regarding those kinds of glosses and commentaries: although many people devise many things regarding those writings of the Pagans <note>original: "Ethnicorum"</note>, those writings nevertheless remain, just as they were from the beginning, the poisonous and damned doctrine of the Pagans. And thus even those very "reverend" Doctors—if it pleases the gods <note>original: "si Dijs placet"; a sarcastic Latin idiom used to mock the pretensions of the scholars</note>—because they let the Holy Scriptures slip from their hands, frequently do not rightly understand or grasp in their entire commentaries what the soul is, what the Holy Spirit and His gifts are, or where the Holy Spirit has and exercises His dwelling and school. Indeed, the madness of the Pagan writers so greatly agitates those fools that they are not ashamed to interpret the Holy Scriptures according to the traditions of the Pagans, or rather to

<column-break/>

pervert them; whereas Scripture is to be explained not through Pagan darkness, but only through the illumination of the Holy Spirit. Who, therefore, would entrust their children to these rash and wicked men, only for them to drink in Pagan poison from them, and together with their masters and teachers be made sons of perdition? True and sincere Christians have received this mandate from God: to hear and follow Moses and the Prophets, and indeed Christ their Lord. From these, therefore, all Pagan teachers and disciples are removed and excluded, as Christ Himself asserted when He said: *He who is not with me and does not hear my word is against me, and is not my disciple; he who does not gather with me, scatters; he who does not follow me is not worthy of me.* <note>A paraphrase of Matthew 12:30 and 10:38.</note> But now, the Pagan teachers do none of these things: for they do not hear Moses, nor the Prophets, nor Christ. Even if they do hear them, they despise them; they cannot be called His disciples, but are excluded from them or from their number. If they are excluded from their number, they are not the children of God but are the impious; if they are impious, they are not partakers of the kingdom of heaven, and consequently are utterly removed and cast out from God.

## The fourth part is chapter 78 of the 7th book of the tables of the Revelation of Divine Majesty: which explains the mysteries of the air and the true nature of Meteors against the minds of the Peripatetics. <note>The "Peripatetics" were the followers of Aristotle. In this period, "Meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning.</note>

---

All things were created through the Word of God: therefore, all things are also governed, moved, and led by the Word of God. The "wise ones" of this age do not want to admit this, but they fashion for themselves a peculiar opinion in which they determine that *Nature* performs all things, and that Nature operates through secondary causes into tertiary ones, and generates "one fool from another" <note>This is likely a jab at the Aristotelian idea of biological and mechanical causality, which the author views as a cycle of ignorance.</note>; yet these figments and opinions of theirs are nothing other than pure and simple lies. For that "Nature" does not exist in the entire universe of things as something that might work or produce anything in the way God does, who created all things by His Word. Whatever blessing He has bestowed and attributed to each creature, that creature obeys it; it complies with that Word and Divine command, and does not depart from it even a finger's breadth. All creatures whatsoever persist within the boundaries and limits of Divine obedience—except for man, who withdraws from God, despises His precepts and doctrine, fashions gods and idols for himself, and establishes his own peculiar religion and decrees in sacred buildings. Man perverts the Word of God and compels others to prefer his own ordinances and traditions over the Word of God: to invoke saints, to venerate the relics of saints as sacred objects, to pray for the dead, and to administer the sacred Supper instituted by Christ under only one kind <note>A reference to the Catholic practice of "communion under one kind," where the laity received only the bread, not the wine.</note>, along with whatever other ravings of this

<column-break/>

sort exist, which are observed to the disgrace and diminishment of the Divine Word; that Word, however, will nonetheless remain firm and will eventually judge those who despise it. In the same way, the "Wise Men of the World" or Philosophers rave, for they do not concede that God works all things in all, and that His Word moves, stirs, and preserves all things. Instead, they ascribe it to their "Nature," pretending that God works through means, and indeed through secondary and tertiary causes. And so those raving wise men either willfully refuse to understand that God works solely through His Word and not through any other means, and thus by no means through those "causes" alleged by them, but rather He works *within* those things.

The first body, namely water, God created as something moist or humid through His Word, and this very thing even today, after the lapse of so many thousands of years, remains moist. No other cause is seen there that might moisten the water or render it wet. Above and in the water, God established the air, so that it might float upon the waters and impel and move them, and preserve them in that liquid and flowing substance. This likewise happens even today. Along with the air, He also created by His Word the Angels and spirits, who dwell in the air concerning the direction of storms, rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, thunder, fire, and *Chasmata* <note>term: Chasmata (A term used in early meteorology to describe openings or "chasms" in the sky, often associated with auroras or atmospheric optical phenomena).</note>...

# APPENDIX TO THE FIRST SECTION

...thunder, waters, heat, cold, moisture, dryness, and many other things of that kind, they perform and carry out their duty and office. And this very thing happens even today through His Word. Concerning all these things, those secular wise men, or Philosophers, write books for themselves that are marvelously foolish, in which not even one single point—let alone a whole letter—is true; rather, whatever has flowed from their brains into the pen and from there onto the paper, only that which is read in them is nothing other than a pure and simple lie. Indeed, even the very spirit of the mouth in those "wise men" is entirely lying and false; nevertheless, they wish to be called wise, and they try to persuade others to present their books above all to students in their schools, and to exercise them thoroughly in those works so that they might turn out more learned; for they claim the whole foundation of all the remaining arts consists in them.

But observe how futilely they write about those matters already mentioned—namely, whence clouds, rain, snow, hail, frost, heat, cold, lightning, the <term>thunderstone</term> <note>original: "lapis Ceraunius"; historically, these were believed to be physical stones that fell during lightning strikes, often identified as prehistoric stone tools or fossils</note>, floods of water, and good and bad storms arise. Truly, no more foolish dreams could occur to anyone than those with which these <note>original: "asini"; literally "asses"</note> blockheads describe the things mentioned. This happens solely because they know neither God nor His most holy Word, and thus they even despise Holy Scripture; they do not read it but instead dwell only on their own ravings, sewing lie upon lie.

But if they had read Holy Scripture with the same zeal with which they turned over their lying books and volumes, they would have found the truth about the air and the storms: namely, that the matter does not stand as they have written in their lying books. Instead, God has His own particular <term>storehouses</term> <note>original: "arcas Thesaurarias"; a reference to the "treasuries" of snow and hail mentioned in the Book of Job 38:22</note> for these types of things already mentioned, from which He produces the winds and the storms, and that He "makes His Angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire" <note>A quotation of Psalm 104:4</note>. If all these things were drawn from the Holy Bible and bound together, as it were, into a single bundle—as perhaps at some point a partial sketch of all of them will be made in a special book—where would you lying <term>meddlers</term> <note>original: "ardeliones"; refers to busybodies or people who interfere in matters they don't understand</note> go with those fictions and ravings of yours? For since God has His own particular storehouses for bringing about the variety of storms, along with His Angels and Spirits, and from there brings forth all those things we see—how wonderfully, for instance, storms arise, how miraculously the thunderstone hardens, by what means heat and cold generate thunder so that it reaches even to citadels, houses, and trees—by what pretext of truth will you ever prove or defend these and your other ravings, O most impudent liars, against the express Holy Scripture? You will never be able to

<column-break/>

prove it, even if the salvation of your souls were most at stake—unless perhaps Holy Scripture is false and lying. But Scripture has already endured its examinations through so many thousands of years and has been found true in past deeds; it has uncovered your lies and malice and has confounded you and your books in such a way that you have no more been able to stand the test than your father, the devil. What profit is it to you now to have fashioned, described, and publicly spread so many great lies among men? Truly, you are a laughingstock and a mockery to the whole world, and you desire nothing more than that what has been done could be undone.

Furthermore, God also created the light, the Sun, the Moon, and the stars, the day and the night, by His Word, and He imposed His own services upon them; and therefore all those things also perform their duties according to that Word. Where then is your "Nature" which carries these things out? There is absolutely nothing anywhere except the one and only Word of God which works all these things. God founded and strengthened the world by His Word; therefore, it also stands firm in that Word. Where then is your "Nature" which preserves the terrestrial globe in this continuous and unmoved firmness? God made it so that the earth brings forth plants of every kind through their seeds; He did all this in the Word of God. Where then is your <term>Peripatetic</term> <note>Refers to the school of Aristotle, whose followers were known for walking about (peripatein) while teaching</note> Nature to produce them? God also created all the animals on the earth, in the air, and in the water, and finally He even made man from the earth, and by His most holy Word He bestowed His divine blessing upon them so that they might increase, multiply, and fill the earth. All these things too, the Word of God has effectively worked in men and in all animals from the founding of the world until the present hour, so that animals of all kinds and men have been born, have grown, and having been multiplied, have filled the earth. All this, I say, the Word of God has worked until now in animals and men, and it still works the same. Where then is the <term>Aristotelian</term> <note>Pertaining to the philosophy of Aristotle, which the author views as a pagan distraction from divine truth</note> Nature?

Accordingly, everyone understands from the solid foundations of truth that all things were created through the Word of God, and through the same Word they are directed, governed, moved, and led in the course originally instilled in them at creation. Just as the air also floats in the Word of God and is led by the Angels of God appointed for this purpose, where and how God wills: and so also, by divine command through <term>Moses</term> <note>original: "Moysen"; referring to the plagues of Egypt, such as the hail and darkness described in Exodus, which the author attributes to direct divine command rather than natural laws</note>, difficult storms were moved and stirred up in Egypt according to the divine will. For God alone, and no one besides Him, holds the key and the rudder of the storms and of all other things and operations by which He moves and impels them here and there, according to His whim and pleasure; nor can anyone place any obstacle, hindrance, or delay in His way, no one...

Thus, if dangerous storms ever arise, they may call upon God, so that He might mercifully turn away that danger of the storm, and in its place grant kind rain, and at the same time defend, protect, and preserve the fruits of the earth along with men and cattle from every evil; and so that, besides all this, they might consider other things which can result in the honor of God.

## Fifth Section, extracted from Chapter 22, Book 7 of the Table of Divine Revelation: In which the offices and acts of the Angels are described.

The first among the Angels is that great spirit who directs the immense and most widely extended water which is called "heaven," and preserves it in its essence, and wonderfully grants motion to all growing and living things. In the second place are positioned the Cherubim, who guard and watch over the Tree of Life. Likewise, some foretell future things and teach men; others kill and repel enemies; others send down snow, rain, lightning, and thunder onto the earth; and so it goes with the rest. Yet all serve God together, while they carry out His will in all things—in the heavens, in the air, in the earth—and indeed in absolutely all places, and that too in various and wonderful ways, as is right to gather from the Scriptures.

<column-break/>

corporeal things between heaven and earth, and indeed even in the earth itself, are carried out through motion. The Word of God moves the Angels, and the Spirits move the air; the air moves the waters; the water, by its radical moisture <note>original: "humiditate radicali." In early science, this was the essential fluid believed to sustain the life and "heat" of all living organisms</note>, connects all visible things on earth and pushes forth all kinds of the earth's fruits in the Word of God. Men and all animals are moved through the Word of God—namely, through that by which they received the blessing—so that in that motion they might generate, grow, and multiply, etc.

<margin>

You "Heathen Christian" Doctors <note>The author's derogatory term for Christian scholars who favor Greek philosophy over biblical literalism</note>, you are little or even not at all concerned about the Holy Spirits and Angels, or what they have done at all times or still do by the command or Word of God; instead, you are content with your Heathen Evangelists, Prophets, and Seers <note>Referring to pagan philosophers like Aristotle or Plato, whom the author believes the schools treat as if they were prophets</note>. Therefore, it is no wonder if you do not know whether they do anything or what exactly they perform. But I would have you and your students know that God has worked through His holy Angels at all times, from the beginning even until the present hour, etc.

Christians must take care not to fall into the snares of the devil. Concerning all these matters, the Gospel, together with all the Apostolic Epistles, proclaims these words: *that your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour* <note>original: "quòd adverſarius veſter diabolus circumeat tanquam leo rugiens, quærens, quem devoret" — a citation of 1 Peter 5:8</note>. The goal, however, toward which every Christian ought to strive is to seek the light that is essential in every way. But the followers of worldly, dark, and Heathen <note>The Latin "Ethnicae" refers to non-Christian, specifically Greco-Roman, pagan traditions</note> doctrine do not notice such a great light kindled in this first chapter of Genesis. Furthermore, they do not observe the splendor of that very light, and consequently, because of their blindness, they see neither God, nor His creatures, nor even themselves. Therefore, God willed that this declaration be prescribed for them to recognize that light, so that they may understand what this Word of His means:

->**LET THERE BE LIGHT AND THERE WAS**<-
->**LIGHT.**<-

How widely this light extends itself into all places—above, below, and to the sides—and how it penetrates and illuminates all things, so that those very works of God may be encountered by His children and be made clear and known in all things. In the same way, all the words of this first chapter of Genesis are illuminated by that light, so that by their splendor, God may be recognized and grasped along with His creatures, and held in perfect cognition and science <note>original: "scientia" — in this period, "science" referred to any organized body of certain knowledge, not just the physical sciences</note>. What more should God have done than to establish them in the radiance of this light and the knowledge of all things? Since they, on the contrary, with all their strength, strive to escape from that li-

<column-break/>

-ght and gape at the darkness, in which they are already immersed up to their necks. For this reason, they are unable to reach a knowledge of any divine creature, not even the lowliest. I will pass over in silence for now the fact that they have entirely cast out this light of the Divine Word from themselves. However, when God kindles the light of His Divine word for them and the whole world—and thus even the knowledge of all His works in the aforementioned manner—and prescribes this declaration besides, He wishes to warn them by this very act. He wants them to finally emerge from those shadows they so greatly desired into His light, to be illuminated by it, and to attain a true knowledge of all things. They should use that knowledge piously, solely for His praise and honor, for their own salvation, and for the benefit of their neighbor.

These are his words: and many other things are scattered here and there against the incongruity, defect, and contamination of the arts of this age, as well as the insufficiency of the Philosophy and Science of the Heathens. To describe all of these in this place would be too long and perhaps tedious for the reader. It is enough that through these things, anyone who is wise and of sound mind can see that the arts and Philosophy of the Heathens are so opposed and mutually contradictory to the truth or holy wisdom (which is the foundation of true Philosophy), as are Light and Darkness, Good and Evil, and finally, God and the devil.

<header>TO THE BENEVOLENT READER. Fol. 67</header>

I would have you know (reader adorned with learning and piety) that, just as the primary intention of the first section of this Philosophical Treatise was to contemplate the Creator in his creatures with an elevated mind, so indeed this latter section is occupied with both the speculation and the practice of the wonderful and secret <term>Sympathy and Antipathy</term> <note>Natural attractions and repulsions believed to govern all physical and spiritual interactions</note>. These two most opposite properties in both the celestial and sublunary worlds, the Divine Majesty exercises according to His pleasure, either to join and reconcile creatures through love and concord, or to pursue them with mutual hatred and malice. Observe, therefore, and diligently extract, if you please, the hidden marrow of this second section—especially the mystery most profound of all, most difficult to understand and observe, and therefore most worthy of weighed investigation. Re-examine in this place those three <term>Mosaic principles</term> <note>Likely referring to the alchemical/Paracelsian principles of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury, or the biblical elements of creation</note> for the extraction of so deep a secret; and that I may add a marrow yet more living and essential to them, I am urged by the necessity of the matter itself, and persuaded by the desire of my soul to enlighten your understanding. Farewell.

### BOOK ONE OF THE SECOND SECTION
concerning Sympathy and Antipathy.

The Argument of this first Book.

After the Author of this treatise, with diligent investigation leading the way, had understood that all Sympathy and Antipathy arose immediately from certain differing passions of the soul or the vivifying Spirit—one of which is <term>concupiscible</term> <note>desiring or seeking the good</note>; the other indeed <term>irascible</term> <note>rejecting or fighting the harmful</note>—and yet had perceived that these were present by their effect in creatures, whether animal, vegetable, or mineral, he was inflamed with no small desire to find and recognize the radical cause of this matter. However, when he had reflected again and again within himself that the eternal power (which is the head and root of all things) is a simple and absolute nature in itself, he could discern no such diversity in its essence, insofar as it exists eternally as a single and same Identity in itself. For according to the intention of Holy Scripture, "as is his darkness, so is his light." <margin>Psalm 138:11 <note>original: "GL. 138, 11" referring to the Vulgate numbering of Psalm 139</note></margin> From this he gathered that a dual equal effect, of which one is contrary to the other in condition or disposition, must necessarily emanate from two different properties in the same whole essence: namely, from its <term>Noluntas</term> <note>Non-willing or divine withdrawal</note> and its <term>Voluntate</term> <note>Willing or divine outpouring</note>, one of which is expressed through darkness, the other through light. For, when the eternal mind and infinite light (in which truly there are no shadows) does not will, it then withdraws itself from creation and reserves itself within itself—that is, it reflects its ardor back into itself—and thus creates or informs nothing by its lucid presence, but leaves the entire abyss (which in this state is said to exist in divine power) overwhelmed on all sides by darkness, formless and destitute of life-giving splendor. And this negative or contractive action of His is the perfect Character of His "non-willing," the general effects of which are Darkness and privation. But, when from the opposite side, that hidden unity emits a benign and salutary ray and splendor of its essence (which is the expression of its will) into the Chaos or deformed abyss, then darkness and privation are forced to give way to light and position, as if to the act of life and formal existence. Through such an object of his contemplation, he perceived that the acts of both willing and non-willing were contained in a single essential unity, which in and through itself is total goodness; and consequently, that "non-willing" in it is nothing other than its "will." For, insofar as it is one and all, so indeed its will and non-will is but a single Identity in it, and yet all things and through all things: For, by means of it, the worker [God] does whatever he wills, in both a privative and <margin>Dionysius 4 <note>Likely referring to Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite</note></margin> [positive] manner...

# THE ARGUMENT OF THE SECOND SECTION. BOOK I.

...rather than positive, both in the powers of the heavens and in the inhabitants of the earth:
Wherefore it follows that darkness and light are one and the same in that Archetypal unity <note>original: "unitate Archetypica"; the original, perfect model in the mind of God</note>: Since everything in that unity is good, insofar as the unity itself is sole and absolute goodness. Regarding the effective and shaping emanation of light, these things certainly appear as such to created beings, and indeed they seem to produce various—even infinite—contrarieties in this world, which are judged by mortals to be either good or evil according to the effects they experience from them. Nevertheless, it seems evident to the Author that these two contrary outpourings or extensions, proceeding in effect from one and the same eternal essential strife, were the principles of all things; insofar as the dark Chaos brought forth waters from its bowels by the presence of light, which were that unique matter from which the heavens and the earth, and consequently the entire world, were made. For the life-giving eternal emanation of light imparted to them form, figure, power, and motion.

Therefore, these things having been seriously considered by the Author, his reason immediately informed him that the world was composed and fabricated from matter or a subject contrary in its disposition. For it is not possible that parents differing from one another by nature should give birth to offspring who are consistent and harmonious with them in condition and nature; and yet such was the will of the Creator: that these two properties, like dissonant tones, should be bound together into a union of unison or unity—as if after His own image—by the inviolable bond of the Spirit of eternal love and concord. Thus, matter, which is the substance of the dark waters, might serve in the place of the female to the formal and masculine emanation, or the illuminating Spirit sent forth from the unity.

By this means, finally, a Triple Pattern <note>original: "Trium Typicum"</note> was established from the duality or the blending of unities according to the image of the Archetype; which, existing as purely Spiritual, was that radical eternal life and essence of the world which was without beginning. And for this reason, it is necessary that the world, being created after the image of the Archetype, should enjoy a Universal Soul <note>original: "animâ Catholicâ"; the 'Anima Mundi' or soul of the world that connects all living things</note>, by whose mediation it can act and live according to the pattern of Him from whom both its form and matter are derived. Consequently, it is necessary that it be clothed with the two aforementioned properties, namely that of Willing and Not-Willing <note>original: "Voluntatis & Noluntatis"; the divine impulse to create/affirm versus the impulse to withdraw/deny</note>.

From this, therefore, the author observes that both the internal and the external Pattern, or the Patterned world, must necessarily be subjected to contrary passions and alterations which arise from those two properties in the Archetypal unity. Namely, sometimes its soul is inclined toward a dark and privative disposition, following in that property the nature of the waters, which are the offspring of the Dark Abyss or the unformed chaos over which divine power holds dominion. In this state, it seems to take on the character of "Not-Willing" within the unity. And sometimes the soul itself affects and imitates the action and property of light which emanates from the eternal source of unity. In this state, it clearly seems to act, to give form, and as it were to "Will," or to take on a positive and lucid nature, and consequently to be sealed by the signet or impression of the "Will" within the unity.

And this is that efficacious effect of the sacred will: For, it appeared to the Author that, insofar as the whole world was composed of two contrary properties—namely, from formal light and dark moist matter—it must consequently follow that the Universal Soul in the world, or the Spirit of the same, which gives life generally (and consequently every particular formal existence derived from the Universal Soul, no differently than infinite rays from a single sun), is liable or subject to passions and alterations of opposite conditions. From this, therefore, arises that constant friendship and enmity observed to exist between good Angels and evil Spirits. From this come those daily changes and variations, as much lovely as hateful, which occur by reason of the variety of influences—either harmonious or discordant with one another—both in heaven...

From this source, both concord and discord, along with a multiform diversity of meteors, are produced within it. Hence arises the multiplicity of affections, the opposition of dispositions, the passions of Spirits, and—to speak truly—that sympathy and antipathy observed to exist between creatures, whether simple or composite, be they animal, vegetable, or mineral. The Author, therefore, established upon these foundations, concludes that it is right and just to agree with the opinions of those two most excellent philosophers, Heraclitus and Empedocles, regarding this matter. One of these opinions is that all things are made through strife and enmity—that is, out of Enmity and Friendship. The other is that the soul is composed of the four Elements and of friendship and strife. From this, he argues for that contrary disposition which exists between the watery Spirit (or the moist nature of the world) and the clear ray of the lucid mind, in respect to their origin. For by "strife," he understands both spiritual and corporal contention; specifically, in respect to that power or contrary strength which exists between the formal light that informs all things and the dark matter. This applies both by reason of the body in the act of corruption, when the soul is ready to depart from it, and in the antipathetic or irascible passion regarding the soul, in which the Spirit labors and suffers unnaturally. And these opinions of the aforementioned philosophers do not seem to differ from the sense of the Wise Man <note>Likely referring to Solomon or the author of Ecclesiasticus.</note>, who says that God made all things in pairs, one of which is contrary to the other, and nothing was made that is defective.

## CHAPTER I.
->*In this chapter it is demonstrated that God is that pure, most simple, and Universal Unity, which comprehends all number and multitude within Himself.*<-

There is no one, however much exalted by the sphere of *Mathematical* perfection, or deeply immersed in the hidden bowels of mystical *Arithmetic*, who, by the agile intuition of a more mature intellect, can observe or discern anything that can justly claim a place before Unity, either in order or antiquity. (Hence, Unity is acknowledged by the wisest of Philosophers to be the principle and root of all numbers and multitude). Thus, indeed, any consistent person cannot deny that this radical identity, as it is considered in its pure and simple nature, cannot be limited by any quantitative dimension, nor included or comprehended in any number, nor divided into distinct portions, nor defined by any substance or Entity. And from this, it is concluded by the wise that Unity is the principle of all things, inasmuch as it comprehends in itself all substances, quantities, and qualities. This is not unlike how the point in *Geometry*, considered in its naked and simple essence, is observed to be indivisible—indeed, something scarcely perceptible and almost nothing determinable. And yet, the point is acknowledged by *Mathematicians* to be the infallible root, not only of any *Geometrical* line, but also of all other continuous dimensions in *Mathematics* and *Physics*, insofar as it comprehends all magnitudes within itself and is comprehended by none.

So too, the two Principles of any dimensions whatsoever, insofar as they preceded and excelled all other things in the nature of things by order and time. Experienced *Mathematicians* have found, in imitation of the *Typical* <note>The word "Typical" here refers to a "Type" or symbolic representation of a higher reality.</note> or image of the most internal, central, and hidden point in the divinity (or the type of Unity), that the most genuine [Unity] appeared, yet it did not seem to be esteemed as the highest good insofar as the abyss was still overwhelmed by darkness, or deformed matter <note>original: "hyle deformata"</note>, and did not yet participate in His lucid and life-giving goodness. For, the most ancient and most radical [principle] of things still...

# SECTION TWO, BOOK I.

<page-num>N</page-num>

<header>OF THE SECOND SECTION, BOOK I.</header>

it was still empty and void; nor could it be called beautiful and shapely, because it had not yet communicated the rays of its beauty with the creature. Nor ought it directly to be called eternity, since in its hidden state it appeared to human capacity not to exist at all; indeed, it was esteemed as nothing, and consequently had no commerce with eternity, sempiternity <note>original: "aevialitate" - referring to *aevum*, the middle state between time and eternity</note>, or temporality. Furthermore, it could not claim the name of "Beginning" in such a condition, since it had as yet no relation to the creation of any thing; so hidden and obscured was it from the apprehension of mortals, and in its order and antiquity so unknown, and also so inscrutable and incomprehensible in its essence, that it could in no way be concluded to be a substance, quantity, or quality, but rather a certain **Transcendent Being**, reserved and consisting only in itself; having no beginning or root from which it might be drawn. Nevertheless, in its divine power—as if in a place containing all things without end or limit—all things which now appear explicitly were then contained implicitly: although, in respect to the meager capacity of mortals, they were esteemed as **Nothing**. And for this reason, some who were versed in the laws of true wisdom left in their eternal monuments that this **Mystical Unity**, since it was darkness and enveloped in the mists of the abyss, and remained as if empty <margin>Reuchlin in book 3 of *On the Kabbalah*</margin> and idle, was regarded as "from nothing." For it was not the end. Since the thinness and poverty of the capacity of the human mind in the consideration of divine things is such, that it is accustomed to imagine and judge those things not to exist at all which do not appear to the eyes. For this cause, the more excellent of the Kabbalistic crowd called that radical unity in its abstruse and occult condition the **Dark Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, used here to represent the primal unity of God before light emerged</note>, which Hebrew letter is received among the Doctors or Rabbis of the Jews as the figure of unity in arithmetic, and consequently is understood **Hieroglyphically** for God, in His absolute **Monadic** nature, insofar as He is seen to be contracted in Himself alone without any sign of emanation. In which state **Mercurius Trismegistus** <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the Hermetic corpus</note> describes Him in these words: <margin>Timaeus 12. Timaeus 3.</margin> "The Monad," he says, "before the beginning of the world, shone for itself and not for others." And elsewhere more plainly: "There was an infinite shadow in the water of the Abyss above, and a thin intellectual spirit was in the Chaos through divine power." And **Moses**: <margin>Genesis 1.</margin> "Darkness was upon the face of the Abyss." By which the wise are able to discern, albeit from afar, that there was a divine power before any creature appeared explicitly from the dark Chaos; and they can also easily conceive what the radical principle of darkness was—namely, the retention or hiding of the actual rays of eternal light in that lucid unity, in which there is no darkness at all. Thus, **Original Darkness** can be regarded as nothing other than the mere absence of the lucid emanation from the radical unity, which is the source and origin of all action; nor can that light of divine vivification be present or emanate where the will of that simple and absolute absence in unity is negative. Hence it follows of necessity that darkness was upon the face of the abyss, and that the earth was empty and void or unformed, before the divine essence shone forth and was borne over the waters; and that darkness was made a **Tabernacle** of idleness and rest: since, where the divine act or sacred emanation is absent, or at least does not wish to act and emit its rays, all things are said to remain in **potentiality**, and consequently exist without actual virtue—that is, as if dead and immobile. And while the dominion of this privative power lasts, the property of cold and stupidity is in force, since heat is generated by motion, and motion is something inseparable from light: and that light has its root in the lucid unity, which for this reason is called the **Father of Lights**. Wherefore it follows, that this divine essence in this state contracts and retains itself in itself: and then the dark Chaos reserved in the divine power must be deprived of motion and heat: and that it is inclined toward density and thickening by reason of the dominion of cold: and that it is the foundation of privation and consequently an enemy to the essence of life and creatures, insofar as its nature is opposed to act, motion, and heat (which are the ministers of divine emanation), and consequently is the origin of death, corruption, and deformity.

We conclude, therefore, that just as light is the beginning of life, position, motion, and the divine will in its revealed nature, so also the primordial darkness is the head and fountainhead of death, emptiness, privation, rest, and finally the **"un-will"** <note>original: "noluntatis" - the divine choice to withhold action or will</note> of the divine essence. And hence the sacred scriptures testify, that when it pleases God to emit the saving rays of His countenance to the creatures, they are recreated with good and life; but when He hides His lucid face in part, then they are sick and troubled; but if He should totally take away the aspect of life, they immediately expire and die. Hence also **Moses**: "God leaves the wicked and hides His face from them," and <margin>Psalm 29. Deuteronomy 1.</margin> "Why do you hide your face from me? Cheer me with your face; your visitation preserves my spirit." By which it is clear <margin>Psalm 103.</margin> that this divine essence observes the action of its "un-will" and will both after the creation of this world and before it: in the former, it is accustomed to withhold life from the creature by means of an act of privation; in the latter, it imparts life to it and preserves it. For by its **rarefying** property, it created and vivified the world and all things that are in the world.

## CHAPTER II.
*In which it is proved that all things were implicitly and Ideally in God and from God, before anything was explicitly prepared or made.*

The state and mode of existence of the eternal unity before anything was created, according to the small strength of my intellect, as well as the effects which it produced in the potential or unformed subject of all things, I have explained clearly enough in the preceding pages. I also expressed there that all things in that state were **implicitly** <note>folded together or hidden</note> and secretly contained within the almighty and incomprehensible point of divine perfection. In that condition, they remained and existed as "Nothing" in relation to us, insofar as no form (which is what assigns a name and being to things) had yet been put on. Therefore, in the state of this unformed power, the wise have called it "Divine Potentiality" with respect to our existence. But, so that we may confirm these things, the Apostle says: *From him, through him, and in him are all things.* <margin>Romans 11:36</margin> And elsewhere: *All things are from God.* <margin>1 Corinthians 11:12</margin> And elsewhere: *One Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in us all.* <margin>Ephesians 4:6</margin> And again: *All things were created through him and in him, and he is before all, and all things consist in him.* <margin>Colossians 1:16-17</margin> And elsewhere: *He is all in all.* <margin>Colossians 3:11</margin> And Sirach <note>Ecclesiasticus</note> says: *We have said many things, yet we have not reached the end; the sum of our words is: He is all.* <margin>Ecclesiasticus 43:27</margin> With these sacred words the Poets seem to agree, saying: *Jupiter is whatever you see, wherever you move.* <note>Lucan, Pharsalia 9.580</note> And: *All things are full of Jove,* etc. From these it is very easily gathered that God generated, produced, made, and created nothing that was not eternally from himself and in himself, so that all things emanated and proceeded from him—namely, from the hidden into the manifest, from the unknown into the known, from pure and **Archetypal** <note>the original divine pattern</note> Simplicity into a **Typical** <note>the physical reflection or copy</note> likeness, from the fountain into the sea, and from the point into the circle. This verifies the saying of the wise Philosopher: *God is the center of all things, whose circumference is nowhere;* or, as others prefer, *He is the center and the circumference.*

Hence, let me be permitted to infer that every thing begotten, originated, created, produced, or separated comes from the unbegotten, infinite, unoriginating, unproduced, unseparated One: every lower thing from the higher, every corporeal thing from the spiritual, every visible thing from the invisible, every temporal thing from the age, every age-enduring thing from the eternal. Hence, just as it is said of God that *from him and through him and in him are all things*, so it is also said that he is *over all and through all and in all*. There follows, therefore, a consideration of the universe by its egress and descent, or as if by a progress from the center toward the circumference. In God all things were, and were nothing but purely God; from God all things <margin>Romans 11:36</margin> <margin>1 Corinthians 11:12</margin> <margin>Ephesians 4:6</margin> <margin>Colossians 1:4</margin> <margin>Colossians 3:11</margin> <margin>Ecclesiasticus</margin> <margin>Asclepius</margin> came into the **Principle** <note>the beginning or first foundation</note>, and then all things were nothing but purely the Principle, while God nevertheless remained in himself. From the Principle all things proceeded into the **Word**, and then all things were nothing but purely the Word, while the Principle nevertheless remained. From the Word all things proceeded into the **Spirit of the Lord**, and then they were nothing but purely the Spirit of the Lord, while the Word nevertheless remained. From the Spirit of the Lord all things proceeded into the waters—namely, the higher waters—and then all things were nothing but purely waters, while the Spirit of the Lord nevertheless remained. From the higher waters all things descended into the lower waters, and then all things were nothing but purely lower waters, while the higher remained. From the lower waters, as if from a **Universal Element** <note>the "Catholic" or all-encompassing matter</note> altered in a fourfold way and by invisible stars, all things proceed into visible bodies, and then all things are nothing but purely visible bodies, while the Elements and invisible stars nevertheless remain. Finally, when all these things have been unfolded and completed, the whole universe is contracted into a "fifth being"—that is, into **Man**—where all things are nothing else but purely man, while the Universe nevertheless remains safe and whole. Thus, man exists as the last of all, who has and carries in himself all things, and is all things; for he is essentially the image of him who was prior to all, who is the blessed God, who was all things, who poured out all things, and who concludes all things in man.

Indeed, we can confirm this whole matter by holy testimony and the assertions of the **Cabalists** <note>Jewish mystical tradition</note>. For we have in the scriptures that God, the fountain of all, created the darkness, and that this dark abyss was the unformed principle which implicitly contained all things in itself; and that the **Word** was in the beginning, and again, that this Word went out from the darkness. <margin>Isaiah 45:7</margin> <margin>Wisdom 11:13</margin> <margin>Genesis 1</margin> And that the Spirit of the Lord was moved over the waters, which appeared from the bowels of the dark abyss. And that all things in the beginning were waters, though the luminous power of the spirit was not extinguished. And that these waters were divided into higher and lower, but the first force of creation was open in those higher ones, since the **Empyrean heaven** <note>the highest, fiery heaven</note> was created before the **sublunary Element** <note>the world beneath the moon</note>. Then, from the higher waters with the bright spirit with which the heavens were adorned, the lower waters were formed and ordered; for lower things are ruled by higher things. Finally, all things composed of the lower waters were created by the mediation of invisible stars sent from the higher waters, and at last, the perfection of all, **Adam**, was made in the image of God as a compendium of the whole world, having it within himself. Hermes says this: *Pimander, the mind of divine power, changed his form and suddenly revealed the universe: for I perceived...*

## OF THE SECOND SECTION, BOOK I.

...everything turned into a light so sweet and pleasant that it delighted me wonderfully as I gazed upon it. A little later, a certain horrific shadow glided beneath in an oblique revolution and migrated into a moist nature, or rather broke out into a great sound. And from that sound a voice went forth, which I judged to be the voice of light; from the voice of light the Word <note>original: *Verbum*</note> came forth. Truly, standing by this moist nature, it nourished it; and from the bowels of the moist nature, a pure and light fire immediately flew forth and sought the heights. The air, also light and obeying the spirit, took up the middle region between fire and water. The earth and water lay so mixed together that the face of the earth, overwhelmed by water, was nowhere visible. Afterward, the earth brought forth the living creatures it had held within. But the Father of all, being Mind <note>original: *intellectus*</note>, Life, and Radiance, procreated a Man similar to himself, etc. By these things he argues that God, or the divine mind, was in his simple unity a divine power, and thus in God all things were nothing but truly God. Then he changed himself into a Dark principle, and then all things were nothing else than the Dark principle, for in it all things were present in a folded state <note>original: *complicité*; a philosophical term meaning "enfolded" or "potential"</note>, yet God remained. Then a bright emanation was made, by which, the darkness having been put to flight from the principle, the Word was made; and then all things were nothing but the Word, yet the principle remained. From the Word all things proceeded into the Spirit of the Lord, and then they were nothing but the Spirit of the Lord, and so on for the rest.

Furthermore, it is also written in the book *Bahir* <note>A foundational work of early Kabbalah</note>: Nothing is the principle except Wisdom; since this is retracted into the abyss of darkness and remains as if idle, or (as they say) looking toward nothing, it is therefore called *Ain* <note>Hebrew for "Nothing" or "Naught"</note>. Nothing, Non-being, and No-end <note>original: *non finis*, referring to the *Ein Sof*</note>, because we, punished by such a thin poverty of intellect toward divine things, judge those things which do not appear in no other way than those things which are not. But when it shows itself, that it is something and truly subsists, then the dark *Aleph* is converted into the bright *Aleph*: or the great *Aleph*, when it desires to go out and appear as the cause of all things, through *Beth* (the next following letter) it is named **כ Ab**, that is, the Father of all generation and production, for he makes all things. Thus he says: from which it is clear that this digression is made by the consensus of both Holy Scripture and the wisest Philosophers and Kabbalists. 

But if, in a backward manner, we wish to ascend from the circumference of things into their central point—as if from the earth into the highest heaven—we think we must begin with man, inasmuch as he was the last and lowest step of the superior scale, through which we descended from heaven to earth by a demonstration *a priori* <note>from cause to effect</note>, and as if from Alpha to Omega. And so, by a demonstration as if *a posteriori* <note>from effect back to cause</note> and as if from Omega to Alpha, we shall proceed in this manner: Eve, the Mother of all living, was not made from absolutely nothing, but essentially from Adam, who says: "this is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh." And before Eve was extracted from Adam, then indeed in Adam there was nothing but Adam himself. He, who was the microcosm <note>the "little world" or man as a reflection of the universe</note>, was not made from nothing—that is, not from himself, nor through himself—but from the Macrocosm, the greater world. And before he was extracted and came into his own being, then he himself in the macrocosm was nothing else than the macrocosm or greater world itself. The Macrocosm was not made from mere and absolute Nothing, but existed from the higher waters, that is, from the Angelic world; and before this happened, the greater world in the higher waters was nothing else but the higher waters themselves, or the Angelic world itself. The Angelic world or higher waters did not exist from nothing, but from the Spirit of the Lord, who poured them out from himself and was moved over them; and before this outpouring happened, all the higher waters or Angelic substances in the Spirit of the Lord were nothing else but the Spirit of the Lord himself, without any distinction or multitude. The Spirit of the Lord did not come from nothing, but from the very Word brought forth from the mouth of the first-born; and before the Spirit of the Lord was distinguished or proceeded from the Word into its own being or person, then it in the Son and with the Son was nothing else but the Son, without any distinction or multitude. The Word or Son did not come from Nothing—that is, not from himself—but from the Principle, according to that saying: "The Word was in the Principle." And before this Word was born from the principle into its own person, then the Word itself in the principle was nothing else but the principle, essentially one in and with the principle, without distinction or multitude. But the Principle, in which the Word was, did not arise from nothing, nor from itself, but from God: for it came forth from the mouth of the Most High; and before it came forth, then the principle in God was nothing else than God himself, essentially, eternally, and most simply one and the same without distinction. 

Thus God, the unity of all, had all things in himself from eternity; and he, as he is one in himself, so also he was all things, yet in such a way that he remained in himself without change or diminution of himself. And so he produced all things from the beginning and distinguished each in its own being, having no business with any Negative Nothing (of which we made mention above), since he himself in himself is one, or that eternal unity, comprehending all things in himself in a folded state; and consequently he is the source and origin from which all things, both eternal and temporal, proceed and consist in their essence: not otherwise than how all the numbers of Arithmetic proceed or emanate from unity and are comprehended in unity. For, however widely a number extends itself, it always has unity to begin it, and likewise to conclude it, and in the truth of the matter, it has nothing besides unity.

But for your better instruction, through a diligent inspection into **Cossic numbers** <note>Cossic numbers refers to early algebraic notation (from the Italian 'cosa' or 'thing'), used here to relate algebra to the structure of reality.</note>, you may observe how this Divine, central, and essential unity comprehends all creatures within itself, both before and after their creation. For we ought to know that there is nothing in this world which is not either a **root**, a **square**, a **cube**, or some other existing composite figure. The **root** represents the principle of all proportions or Cossic magnitudes; the **square** designates a simple and spiritually-originated figure, which is created or produced from the multiplication of the root; while the **cube** is established from the augmentation of the square (or the originated figure) within its own root. From this, one may see that the entire cubic body, and consequently the square itself, is contained within the root, and in conclusion is nothing other than the root itself multiplied in and by itself.

But, so that this demonstration of mine may come closer to the intuition of your understanding, I persuade you to consider the nature and property of this **Divine Monad** <note>The Monad refers to the 'One' or the ultimate indivisible source of all being.</note> or unity with a little more accurate diligence. Namely, as it exists in its simple and sincere being, you will then find that in the **typical world** <note>The 'typical world' refers to the physical world of forms/types, as opposed to the 'archetypal' world of ideas.</note>, without any departure from its punctual or central depth, it contains the three aforementioned Cossic dimensions within itself implicitly, and consequently all other things which it has now explicitly produced through creation. And this is clearly proven through this arithmetical demonstration: For if we unfold unity in itself and through itself as a root, it will produce nothing besides itself for a square; which again, by multiplying only itself in itself, it will bring forth in place of a cube—namely, mere unity. Thus, you will find the root, the square, and the cube to be nothing but one and the same.

From this it is evident that although we have here three branches of a single point, which seem to differ in their formal progression (I mean the root, the square, and the cube), yet in essential truth, there is nothing but that Real and radical unity or identity, in which all things remain potentially or implicitly, and that in the most abstruse manner. And for this reason the wise man says: *To God all things were known before they were created.* <margin>Ecclesiasticus 23</margin> And **Esdras**: *The power of God is the end and beginning of all things before all were created.* <margin>4 Esdras 6</margin> And **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the Hermetic texts.</note>: *All things depend on one principle; the principle is from the one alone; and the principle is moved so that it may again stand as the principle, yet it remains one and does not depart from unity.* <margin>Pimander 10</margin> These same things also seem to be intimated by those words of the **Savior**: *I and the Father are one,* <margin>John 10:30 <note>Original text cites John 13:10, likely a scribal error for 10:30.</note></margin> *the Father in me and I in the Father, and the Father remaining in me, he does all things.*

Hermes also seems to speak in this sense concerning the **Archetypal structure** of the world, according to whose image this typical world was formed. Wherefore he calls the Son of God visible to all: *The Monad* (he says) *generates a Monad and reflected the heat into itself.* <margin>Pimander 4</margin> By these words he seems to argue that the Typical world was implicitly described in the Archetypal world (God so willing), which he then afterwards explicitly depicted. From which it is clear that this world was made in the image of the Archetypal world.

But lest some captious people, attacking this opinion of mine, should take exception against it, alleging that it contradicts the consensus of the ancient Fathers of the Church in every way, I will explain the sentiments of some of them on this matter in this place. **St. Augustine** says: *Ideas are eternal and unchangeable forms in the divine mind.* <margin>Book 83, Question 46; Book 1 on Divine Questions 3</margin> **Scotus** <note>Duns Scotus, the medieval scholastic philosopher.</note> says *that they are objective things, known by the divine intellect.* But there is nothing in God which is not God, since the Deity is nothing but one and the same spirit. From which it follows that the Ideas in God, although they are many according to the various pleasures of the divinity (for man was made in one way, and a horse in another, etc.), yet all are nothing but one in God, as St. Augustine seems to confirm more clearly elsewhere in these words: <margin>On the Trinity, Book 6, last chapter</margin> *The first and highest intellect is a certain art of the Omnipotent and Wise God, full of all living, unchangeable reasons, and all are one in it, just as it is one from one, whereby it is one.* And elsewhere he says: *You are my God and Lord of all things which you created, and with you are the causes of all stable things, and the unchangeable origins of all changeable things remain with you, and the reasons of all rational, irrational, and temporal things always live.* <margin>Soliloquies, Chapter 31</margin> And **Boethius** has these lines:

->You lead all things from the heavenly example,<-

Finally, **Anselm** most learnedly expresses the mode and progression of every exemplary thing from the Ideal source: *The form of a thing,* he says, *is the Archetype and truth of the Craftsman; and while it is produced from potentiality into act, it is motion; but in the matter already produced, it is a likeness and image.* And for this reason that most learned **Abbot Odo** says: *The Ternary number <note>The number three.</note> is the principal example in the mind of the Creator for things to be created.* <margin>1. rest. on the Ternary</margin> In which sense also Hermes, in the place cited before: *The Monad generates a Monad and reflected the heat into itself,* <margin>Pimander 12</margin> because unity in the fabric of the Ideal or Archetypal world sent forth the Word, as an essence generated from itself, and in unity not at all distinct from it, and finally reflected that spirit of wisdom proceeding from both into itself. Hence the **Son of Sirach**: *The source of Wisdom is the Word of God on high, and its going forth is eternal commands.* <margin>Ecclesiasticus 1:5, 4</margin> In this manner, therefore, was the Archetypal world
