### OF THE SECOND SECTION, BOOK I.

The Philosopher <note>likely referring to Aristotle</note> called the human soul a natural fire; and Prometheus called it a celestial fire
<margin>Prometheus.</margin> enriching men with life. And because that Prometheus is handed down by tradition to have held possession of that fire, he is therefore
imagined by the Poets to have been severely punished by Jove for his surreptitious theft of that fire from heaven.
<margin>Hermes, Zoroaster, Heraclitus.</margin> But Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus</note> calls that fire a word adhering to a moist nature. And Zoroaster and Heraclitus say that it was an invisible fire, by means of which all generation and multiplication is accustomed to happen. Since, therefore, that fire of life is never to die in an animal Creature, it is necessary that for its preservation and multiplication it be nourished by its like in the air at every moment of time: which, unless it happens, it is necessary that the life of the creature vanish, and so the Creature perish.
<margin>Parmenides.</margin> And this is that which Parmenides seems to intimate when he says: *Nature rejoices in its own nature.* For this reason the fiery virtue of life, having its position in the center of the creature's heart, attracts its like from the air by means of inspiration <note>breathing in</note> with joy, delight, and a notable appetite through a certain magnetic property. For (as I have said) the hidden food or nourishment of life is in the air. This, therefore, is the reason why a certain anonymous Author, most excellently versed in the mysteries of God and nature, says this: *O nature of celestial truth multiplying natures! O strong nature! Nature conquering and overcoming and making its own natures to rejoice!* By which he argues that by the help and visitation of that celestial nature, the vital spirits and the flames enclosed in them grow and multiply. For by the virtue of this, not only life, but also the fruits of generation proceed and are produced in an infinite manner. We infer from these things which have now been said, that the Elementary air is full of the influences of life, vegetation, multiplication, and formal seeds: insofar as it is the Treasury chest of God, rich and overflowing with divine rays and celestial gifts. Nor does this assertion of mine look only to the animal kingdom of composition, but also to that of vegetables: for by this very spirit they vegetate, and by this they multiply unto infinity, and have their existence. For I am myself an eyewitness, and can also, if there be need, demonstrate that the spirit of vegetable wheat, in which the secret spirit dwells, is a pure volatile salt, which is nothing else than the air of the specific thing, or of the wheat, made essential. That volatile salt is an unctuous liquor as white and clear as Crystal, the interior of which is nonetheless filled with vegetable fire, by means of which it is multiplied unto infinity. For that formal fire is a certain Magnetic force, through which its like of life and vegetation is extracted abundantly from the rays of the Sun (which is the Treasury chest of God of life and vegetation) by means of the aerial vehicle. Perceive, therefore, that this vegetable spirit, free from its Elementary bonds and reduced into the form of a most limpid liquor, is so desirous of the formal solar rays and seeking them with such sympathy, that having been exposed to the solar rays for the space of three hours, it attracted to itself such a solar or formal tincture, that from a whitish and Crystalline color it was made into a blood-red ruby. By which experiment the formal method of multiplying both animals and vegetables was most easily revealed. For, this is the reason that a grain of Wheat [multiplies] unto infinity as to multiplication. Furthermore, no true and skilled Philosopher can be ignorant that the nitrous nature of any thing, which is nothing but air, which by the virtue of that secret spirit which inhabits it, attracts to itself both the air and the celestial form: since the formal act cannot be inspired into the creature except through an aerial medium or vehicle. And this is also the reason why both the quantitative substance of the creature in respect to the aerial vehicle, and the formal essence of the creature, increases daily and has its growth: Whence it is clear, that from that same spirit both vegetation and multiplication arise. These things therefore being perceived with diligence, the reason will be at hand, how the Chylous <term>Chyle: a milky fluid formed in the small intestine during digestion</term> whitish humor is transmuted by exaltation into the ruddy color of blood, and also the manner of vegetation and multiplication in animals and of multiplication or increase by way of the generation of animals. But, since in the first treatise of my Anatomy, where I made a discourse on the Anatomy of Wheat or Bread, I spoke amply of the admirable properties of that vegetable spirit, I will therefore not speak more of them in this place, but will turn myself to the mystery of the microcosmic soul. The spirit of life was in such a manner breathed by God into the earthy man, that suddenly the mass was reduced into an animal creature: Not otherwise than when the *Ruach-Elohim* <note>Hebrew: Spirit of God</note> had breathed upon the waters, they were immediately animated, vivified, and formed into the image of the great world: for which reason the Platonists called it the "great animal": But, as the world was made in the image of God before man was created, and then afterwards man himself by the virtue of the same spirit was formed in the world according to the exemplar of the word of life or the image of the aforesaid spirit: so we ought to consider that man has his mode of vivification, sustenance, preservation, and multiplication from the soul of the world and the Elements of the same. Wherefore Hermes, not indiscreetly, describes the descent and entrance of the vivifying spirit of the world into the human body in this manner: *Air,* he says, *is in the body, the soul in the air, the mind in the soul, in the mind the Word; but the Word is the Father of them all.* By which he argues that distinction previously related by me, which is between the mind, the soul, and the spirit, and shows that the highest mystery of the soul

# ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY

The mind is composed of the Father and the Word. Furthermore, it appears to coincide that the Word is the image of God, the mind is the image of the Word, the soul is the image of the mind, the air is the image of the soul, and the body is the image of the air. By this we can discern that admirable bond and connection which the members of the world have among themselves. It is also declared that the primary portion of Elemental matter is air, and that the primary sublimity in the air is the vital form or soul, whose head is the divine mind and whose root is the Word, in which there was life. Therefore it is clear that this mind in the soul is taken for the spirit of wisdom, inasmuch as its source is the Word of God, as Sirach <note>Ecclesiasticus/Sirach 1:5: "The word of God on high is the fount of wisdom."</note> testifies; for it is this which fills and gives life to all things. For in it, according to the testimony of David <note>Psalm 33:6: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made... and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth."</note>, is all the virtue of the heavens, and consequently the power of forming, generating, giving life, nourishing, and multiplying. And so I might say with Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with alchemy and philosophy.</note> that the bright and eternal spirit of God, within the Quintessential or Ethereal spirit, creates the soul in the air, and introduces it by means of the aerial vehicle into the human body, in which it produces the effects of vivification and the multiplication of the species. Wherefore he says elsewhere: The soul of man is carried in this manner: the Mind in the reason, the reason in the soul, the soul in the spirit, and the spirit in the body. The spirit, diffused through the veins <margin>Ecclesiastes 1</margin> <margin>Timothy 10</margin> and arteries and the blood, moves the living creature on every side, etc. We must therefore imagine that the air, which is drawn to the heart through inspiration, is full of this kind of divine Treasury of life; being introduced to the human heart in its vehicle through inspiration, it never ceases to attract its like to itself by a certain Sympathetic virtue. For nature rejoices and delights in the presence of its like, as we have said; and again, that the heart is the precious sanctuary of the vital treasury, David seems to acknowledge in these words: "Guard your heart," he says, "above all observation, for from it proceed the actions of life." <note>Proverbs 4:23, here attributed to David/Solomonic tradition.</note> The manner and the instruments through which that spirit attracts in a Sympathetic way, and after attraction expels that aerial vehicle which is superfluous, are of this sort. Since without the sparks of life and generation, which swim in the air in a hidden way, no mortal—indeed, no creature—could live or endure for a moment of time, it is necessary that these be attracted by the creature assiduously and at every minute interval and introduced through inspiration. For without that salutary act and its effect, the animal must immediately be suffocated. For by the suppression and deprivation of air, the soul will instantly cease from its vivifying act or operation, as it is nothing other than the act of eternal light in the mundane soul. For the soul is fashioned, as has been said, from the bright virtue of the emanating divinity and the subtle moist nature of the world, the former of which assigns the innate heat and the latter the radical moisture to creatures; and therefore this double virtue is renewed and multiplied by the assiduous or continuous inspiration of air. This spirit of the animal, and consequently of man, is therefore drawn by inspiration into the left Chamber of the heart, <margin>Psalm 123</margin> or the ventricle, by the contraction of the straight fibers of the heart, in which act the transverse and oblique fibers are relaxed, whence the region of the heart is dilated and opened; and this action is called **Diastole** by Physicians. In the time or space of this motion, the heart, by a certain attractive virtue, introduces the air with its vital treasury through the venous artery of the lungs <note>The pulmonary vein.</note> into its left region by means of inspiration. This Treasury then serves afterward not only for seminal vivification and generation, but also for spiritual multiplication and for the nutrition of the vital and internal spirits of generation, just as the Liver is accustomed to entice the chylous juice of gross nourishment to itself through the mesenteric veins for the nourishment and increase of the natural spirits; which natural spirits are destined by the Creator for the vegetation and augmentation of the parts of the body. Again, after the vital nature has received that aerial spirit with its secret Treasury, and has introduced it into the left Chamber of the heart as if into its well-furnished and subtly adapted laboratory, it begins to sift or Anatomize it, to open it and search its vitals. It separates the celestial nature with its divine act—the true (I say) Treasury of life or invisible fire of life—from its grosser and more useless aerial vehicle by a divine and admirable Alchemy. It encloses a certain subtle, volatile salt and more worthy portion of the air (which is the essential and immediate vehicle of the vital Treasury, and as it were the ethereal soul in the air, as Hermes says) into the aorta or great artery, as if into a sanctuary or perfume-box <term>myrothecium: a container for ointments or oils</term> of the vital spirits, and it emits the superfluous portion of useless air in an instant through expiration. And this expulsive action is performed by the contraction of the transverse fibers in the substance of the heart and the dilation of the straight ones. For by this action the heart is also contracted and compressed; and this action is called **Systole** by physicians. It must be understood, however, that for the better preservation and containment of this golden Treasury of life in that arterial sanctuary, God ordained three semilunar valves in the opening of the Aorta annexed to the left region of the heart, which are opened by the entry of that vital food, and then immediately closed, lest that enclosed Treasury should exit again through the same gate it entered. For this reason, therefore, those valves are so formed by God that they are opened from within and closed from without, just as, on the opposite side, those two valves which are inserted at the opening of the venous artery are open on the outside and closed on the inside; these are called **Mitral** because they are very similar to the mitres of Bishops. Their duty is to let in the inspired air as well as to emit its superfluous and useless portion. Whence it is clear that an easy access is granted to the air, as if to the Treasury of life, into the Chamber of the heart, but the Treasury is denied an exit once it has entered.

# SECOND SECTION, BOOK I.

## SECOND SECTION, BOOK I.

Now indeed, I shall express in a few words the action and effects of that spirit of life, after it has been so enclosed within the arterial trunk. It is certain that, having been made a captive, it dilates itself throughout the entire human body within the branches and subdivided channels of those same arteries. For through the branches of the Great Artery <note>The aorta</note> called the Carotids, a rectified portion of that already specified spirit ascends to the brain; through those (I say) tiny channels and conduits, the more celestial part of that extraction in "natural Chemistry" <note>The author views bodily functions as alchemical processes</note>—being more excellent in dignity and subtlety than the rest of the fountain of life, and consequently more filled with the knowledge of the divine mind—claims for its seat the highest region of the Microcosmic palace, its very Empyrean heaven. For hither the mental ray ascends in its rational vehicle, and chooses that place for its "heaven of heavens": yet under this law and condition, that the rays of its virtue and power expand or extend themselves through all the branches of the Universal Artery. For this reason, all physicians, both Heathen and Christian, conclude that the voluntary action of man has its seat in the brain, insofar as that is the region of the "animal faculty" <note>From 'anima' (soul/breath); the faculty responsible for sensation and movement</note>; whereas, conversely, his other two actions—namely the vital in the heart and the natural in the liver—seem to be subject to that animal faculty, since they are involuntary actions. And this is the cause why the brain is the seat of reason and intellect, and as it were the "prime mover" in the microcosmic machine.

Then, in the second series, that portion of the introduced spirit which is purified in the workshop or laboratory of human nature and adapted for vital action, is carried into those small branches of the Great Artery which are called cervical: these are the arteries which assign life to the regions of the chest. In this place, therefore, that portion of the spirit puts on the impression of that spiritual liveliness which pertains to the vital and thoracic parts; and also in the branches called the Coronary arteries, it assumes for itself the internal "idea" of those spirits which look toward the quickening of the heart. And so it is in the other arterial branches—namely the Humeral, Thoracic, Axillary, and the rest—along with that life-giving spirit which they contain. For, just as this spirit was in the open air, so it was Universal and possessed every virtue in potential and in "complication" <note>original: *complicité*; a philosophical term meaning 'enfolded' or 'infolded'</note>. But when it has entered any creature, it is then specified and "explicated" <note>unfolded into a specific form</note>, converting itself into the nature and condition of whatever region of the animal creature it occupies.

Thus, that invisible spirit, lurking in a vehicle scarcely perceptible and swimming as if in the thin substance of an aerial spirit, not only expands and dilates itself for the quickening of every member of the body and the sustenance of life, but also—by contracting itself into a scarcely perceptible spermatic cloud (which happens in the act of coupling or coitus through a certain magnetic virtue animated by divine love)—and now possessing the impression of the whole generator by a marvelous and swift action and passage into <column-break/> the two arterial "preparing" spermatic vessels, namely the right and the left, it descends from every member of the body, but especially from the three principal ones. And there, that celestial spirit, overflowing with divine fire, contains the internal and invisible [form] of that body which was afterwards to be visibly and realistically delineated and produced—that is, the figure of the spiritual [man] within itself ideally—according to the image spiritually and ideally sketched and enfolded before it was unfolded to our sight. (This is not unlike how King David boasted that he had the image of the temple totally described by the finger of God, which was then afterwards actually built by Solomon according to that pattern). This stands as the counterpart to the external and corporal man, or the effigy, which is compacted from the four Elements. From the visible sperm of man contained in the two venous "preparing" seminal vessels, it proceeds: so that from the concurrence of the sperm of the arterial vessels with that of the venous vessels, a mixture is made between the matter and the form of man—that is, between his internal and external. In this, the internal is that aforementioned divinity, which conforms its external mistress to the image of the species. But we have confirmation of all this from the sacred page. *You possess* (says David) *my reins, from the time I was covered in the womb.* <note>A reference to Psalm 139:13</note>

Whoever understands the action and the path of the spirit, by which it proceeds in that work, may know the manner through which it operates these things so wonderfully. <margin>Job 10:10.</margin> But all of this is explained more clearly by Job: *Did you not,* he says, *pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese? You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews. You have granted me life and favor, and your providence has preserved my spirit.* Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was with you, etc. From this thread of discourse, every question and difficulty in this matter seems to be removed; indeed, the entire mystery of this thing is opened through his observation, both in the act of generation and in the preservation and continuation of the infant's life, as much in the mother's womb as after its birth. For in that phrase (*you poured me out like milk*), he seems first to argue that the spermatic mass, in which man was folded and contained <note>Latin: *complicité*, meaning "enfolded" or potential</note>, was well-disposed and composed by the spirit of life and even injected into the womb. From which then afterwards, through the secret path of the spirit, man was explicitly produced or formed. 

Then he proceeds to the second stage of generation. (*You curdled me like cheese*, etc.) By which he argues that this divine spirit, immediately after the injection of the sperm into the womb, curdled and thickened it into a more solid substance in the likeness of cheese. According to that preceding text: <margin>Job 10:9.</margin> *Remember, I beseech you, that you have made me like clay*, etc. Then he proceeds to the third stage of generation. (*You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews*, etc.) The aforementioned stage of coagulation being finished, he now comes to the completion of the parts of the human body, from which the external man is shaped in the mother. From these things it is established that the divine spirit in the seed fashions the internal man in his own person, and then proceeds thus to the quickening of that external man fabricated from the elementary sperm: *You have granted me life and favor*, etc. From this he argues that, the material work being completed—as if a palace were made fit and appropriate for receiving the God-like Spirit—He breathed into it the breath of His life. And so man was endowed not only with life, but also with the ray of Mind and Reason. <margin>Acts 17.</margin> Whence the Apostle most rightly says: *In Him we live, move, and have our being.* 

Nor is it enough for anyone to say that God does all this not from within, but from without; as if the Spirit of God were not everywhere, insofar as it fills all things, and consequently can in no way be absent from the act of generation; since the life of a thing is the inspiration of the Almighty, and since His incorruptible spirit is in every thing. Is it not also said in Ezekiel: <margin>Ezekiel 37.</margin> *Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and you shall live: and I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you shall live.* And the Prophet said: *Come, O Spirit, from the four winds and breathe upon these slain, that they may live; and the spirit entered into them and they lived.* From which things one may see, first, that it was divine power which formed the external man before he was endowed with a living soul, and that then afterwards he was endowed with the breath of life. Furthermore, just as this spirit was in the subtle macrocosmic wind <note>The "Great World" or universe</note>, so also it is present in the vital seed, which is nothing other than a wind or a spirit scarcely perceptible. 

By those things which have been said, that doubt—whether the soul be created by infusion or not—is explained more than enough. For I first explained how the soul of the world was created into a mundane spirit by the breathing of the Divine Spirit; then afterwards, I demonstrated that all souls drew their origin from that source and said that the quickening rays of that spirit, descending from heaven in the manner of an invisible fire, fill the air. I affirmed that this fire of nature, insofar as it is free from specification, is in potential to be transformed as much into the nature of a vegetable or mineral species as into that of an animal; and that as soon as it has penetrated an individual of some species through inspiration, it is immediately converted into its nature, and works as much toward its generation as its multiplication with the preservation of the species—namely, by procreating like from like.

Now indeed, if it be asked why the universal spirit of mundane life, since it is but one, nevertheless produces every birth or fruit according to its own species, and not according to its own unity in essence, as a single and non-differing thing. I respond that I have said in the preceding pages that every specific creature was radically—and that by the command of the Creator—distinct from one another in its species and procreated differently, and always multiplied by the creating word or spirit and continued in the same species of form which was assigned to it in creation. And truly it is likely that God in His secret counsel ordained a mold and model, as it were, in which and according to whose exemplar the potential creature ought to be formed before it came into actuality. For a better understanding of this matter, we ought to know that there are four spermatic vessels of preparation, namely two on each side, of which one is a venous vessel and has its origin from the *vena cava*, and from this vessel is obtained that sperm which is ordained for the constitution of the infant's body. And that sperm is nothing other than the subtle composition of the Elements in the body of the parent, extracted from the flower of nutriment; it is a visible thing and is called by the twin name "Sperm." The other is the Arterial vessel, as if springing from the trunk of the Aorta, in which the spirit of life dwells; it is the fountain and origin of the internal man: for in it is the invisible fire of life. And it is properly called "Seed" <note>Latin: *Semen*</note>, which is none other than the central, internal, invisi- <note>The word "invisible" is cut off at the bottom of the page.</note>

# BOOK TWO.

## *In which those mystical radiations—which are treated in a hidden manner as arising from two opposite principles, namely Darkness and Light, and their Sympathetic and Antipathetic effects—are examined.*

### The Argument of this Book.

After the author had found the essential roots of Sympathy and Antipathy through diligent inquiry and explained them in the preceding book (in which he proves they are nothing other than a single Universal <note>original: "Catholicam," meaning universal or all-encompassing</note> simplicity in essence, even though that unity is endowed with two properties of an opposite nature and condition, much as a single will is capable of both willing and nilling), he did not think it sufficient to gather and conclude that the matter simply *is* based only on circumstances and reasons backed by mere probability. Therefore, in this present book, he strives with his greatest effort to show the *reason why* <note>original: "dioti," a Greek philosophical term for the underlying cause or "the why" of a thing</note>, that is, why and how that twofold act is scattered into the vast cavity of the world. 

And truly, he found this last branch of study so difficult for mortal capacity to investigate that in the inquiry of so great a work, no small amount of labor and the deepest contemplation of a Master-Artisan is required. For this reason, he is content to be directed and led along so rough and difficult a path by the light and polar star of those sublime Spirits—both Theological and Cabalistic—who received the resolution and unshelling of so great a doubt from the eternal Spirit of Wisdom. For He alone is the revealer of such deep secrets, as the most wise Solomon, the Prophet David, and the Royal Psalmist testify. Indeed, He Himself, since He is the only sufficient actor in Sympathy and Antipathy, is entirely capable of revealing this secret to mortals and depicting it in its living colors—a thing which worldly Philosophers hunt and seek with such industry and labor of mind, though in vain and without fruit. 

Therefore, from the observation of Canons and Axioms of both the Sacred Scriptures and the most learned Rabbis, both Hebrew and Egyptian, he has gathered that the eternal Archetypal world proceeds radically from a single, simple, and Universal source of light. This source sends out an emanation or outflow endowed with ten various properties into the Aeonial or Angelic world. Likewise, the Angelic world pours those divine outflows of light through an Angelic vehicle into the temporal world. Thus, the ethereal or celestial region of the temporal world is made a sanctuary of divine influences, from which they are rained down into the Elementary world—more or less according to the will of Him who sent them—to carry out His commands, whether severe or benign. 

By this kind of descent <note>original: "degradatione," referring to the step-down process from the divine to the material</note>, he perceived that God, by means of His Word, imparted a single, unique, and distinct essential emanation to the entire universe. Thus, all things in it, participating more or less in the single Universal essence, differ from one another both in species and as individuals. He also perceived that the multiform property of that divine outflow established and created Angelic creatures—spiritual organs of differing conditions and offices—through which and in which He operates centrally at every moment of time with various and multiform power. Consequently, it appears clearly to him that since there are properties of contrary strength in the divine outflow, it is necessary that there also be *Angelic Spirits* corresponding in nature and condition to each Divine property, through whose mediation affairs are administered in this world. For in these spiritual organs or Angelic Instruments, and through them, the rays of the splendor of eternal influence descend first into the starry region of the temporal world, and then afterwards are poured out from there into the sublunary or Elementary world, and...

There, he contends that the Devil can achieve nothing except through the mediation of God's creatures and their virtues, which are destined by God, the Creator of all, for the use of men rather than for the Devil.

### THE FIRST MEMBER OF THE SECOND BOOK.

#### CHAPTER I.

> *That Sympathy is the offspring of Light, just as Antipathy has its origin from Darkness. Furthermore, the Etymology or true meaning of both words, as well as their nature, are discussed in this chapter.*

**I**n the upper portion of this work, you have had revealed in general words the radical and essential **Unity** with its two branches of opposite property (which are the Characters of **willingness** and **unwillingness**), as well as its two Universal effects: namely, **friendship** and **hatred**, both in good and evil things, and all those passions, whether spiritual or corporeal, which are derived from them. It remains now for us to descend into the depths of our discourse and penetrate to the very marrow of **Sympathy** and **Antipathy**, which are manifested by their effects not only in the things of the temporal world, but also in those of the eternal world. For no one, even moderately versed in science, provided they have been instructed by Mother Nature, can be so enveloped in ignorance that they do not discern with open eyes the hidden effects of celestial and terrestrial things in Sympathy and Antipathy, implanted in them at creation. 

But, before I immerse myself in the detection of so profound a matter, it will be worth the effort to first open up the meaning or Etymology of the words Sympathy and Antipathy, so that you may better and more directly perceive their distinct natures or essences. **Sympathy** is a Greek word, namely *Sympatheia* <note>original: "Συμπάθεια"</note>, and is derived from *Syn* <note>original: "Συν"</note>, that is, *with* or *together*, and *pathos* <note>original: "πάθος"</note>, that is, *passion* or *suffering*, which proceeds from the verb *pascho* <note>original: "πάσχω"</note>, that is, *I suffer* or *I experience*. From this it is clear that the former passion proceeds from the divine act or the positive, luminous unity, like concord and love, and is properly called **compassion** <note>original: "compassio"</note>. The latter passion, however, arises from the divine potential or the dark and privative unity, like discord and hatred, which are the effects of two natures of contrary strength fighting against each other. 

We may therefore not inaptly define Sympathy as the emanation of two spirits, either from the same divine property or radiating from two similar ones—that is, those who draw their radical emanations from the same or two similar divine properties. For example: all creatures that participate in those benign and lovely rays or irradiations, which are sent by God through the Angelic organ into the **Sphere of Jupiter** <note>original: "Iovis"</note>, are poured down from its orb or Sphere even to the earth, and are communicated to those infinite creatures therein, which under that property of God's will...

But, since the general cause of Sympathy and Antipathy is a certain hidden and secret emanation or irradiation from one creature into another, *it will be necessary* to look into the marrow of so profound a business, so that we may more plainly and clearly discern the general source and root of all radiations and emanations: For by this method we shall detect the abstruse cause of the differences in them, and follow their extensions, namely from *their* root to the trunk, and from the trunk to the branches, and finally from the branches to the twigs and leaves, descending as if into infinite individuals.

Wherefore the wiser of the Cabalistic Rabbis affirm that there is not any plant or herb below which does not have a star in the firmament that strikes it and says to it, "grow." But since the radical investigation of this matter requires a still higher speculation, I desire first that we search with diligence how every creation was effected by the emission of rays, and whether that emanation of rays was ordained in a multiform property, or of one and the same condition. I have manifested to you clearly enough in the preceding pages that all things were created in the beginning of things by one eternal spirit of Wisdom, who, like an eternal messenger or Universal Angel from *Ein Sof* <note>original: "Ensoph" — The Infinite or Boundless God in Kabbalah</note> (as the Cabalists say), that is, from the infinity or infinite source of light, was sent out under the form of an emanation or most splendid flux to inform all things reserved folded within the divine power and to lead them into explicit act: and I will endeavor to prove this from these testimonies of holy scripture. Wherefore it is clear from the aforesaid that this spirit, in respect to its essential essence, is eternal, but by reason of its emanation into the world, it is called "aevial" <note>A term for "everlasting" or "aeonic," often used to describe the duration of angels which is between time and eternity.</note> or of an Angelic nature: Whence the preceding text says: *And the understanding of prudence from eternity.* We proceed, therefore, in the progression and multiplication of that emanation in this manner: From the trunk of the tree go forth branches, both general and special and individual, of which those that are stronger after the trunk are like the Arms of the body itself, then follow the smaller branches and finally the twigs. To which we refer the various stations of the Angels in the aevial or Angelic world, assigned according to their dignities by reason of the divine influences which they receive from their universal branch or holy emanation, Jesus Christ, sent forth from the *Ensoph* root or his Father. The Apostle confirms this in these words: Christ is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature, because in him all things were founded in heaven and on earth, visible <margin>Colossians 1:15, 16.</margin> and invisible, whether Thrones, or Dominions, or Principalities, or Powers; all things were created through him and in him, and he is before all, and all things consist in him, etc.: so that all the Angels of the higher or empyrean orders proceed from him in the first series no differently than the arms of a tree from its trunk. And just as we see that the arms, being closer to the trunk, are more robust, more beautiful, and firmer than the branches: so the Empyrean or super-substantial Angels are closer and more joined to the universal emanation, and consequently are more opulent in divine virtue and light and more adorned in beauty; and that is through degrees of dignity according as they more or less immediately approach the seat of the uncreated source of emanation—that is, they more closely approach the face of the shining uncreated essence, which imparts to them the most excellent light and glory. Not otherwise than we see in the arms of a trunk, that the closer they are to the trunk, the larger they are in their existence or substance. After these, we see that the smaller branches arise immediately *from* those arms, and they have a place for their consistency distinct or divided from the arms, even though their bulk is not divided from the arms. By the same reasoning, we observe that the intelligences or Olympic <note>Referring here to the celestial or planetary spirits.</note> or ethereal Angels draw their virtues and life immediately from those Empyrean ones; and that in different forms and in a variety of measure of excellence, who reserve those influences in the stellar bodies, as if in their treasury-chests, for the use of lower things. Then, as the branches proceeding from the tree-arms attribute life and being to other twigs arising from them: so also the Olympic Angels pour their influences into those Elemental ones, whose princes are four in number—those who preside over the four winds and the four cardinal points of the world, assigning to them the force or power of life, growth, and generation, and also of corruption. By which it may be seen that God, through the spirit of wisdom sent out by way of emanation, and consequently the great firstborn Angel—being created first of all and having His name—imparts his virtue to the Empyrean Angels, who then afterwards pour out the manifold nature of the same into the Olympic spirits, from whom again the Elementals draw their essential faculties. And yet all these essential virtues, as much in the Empyrean heaven as in the Ethereal and Elemental, are continuous and indivisible from the holy emanation, which is inseparable from its root: Not otherwise than the trunk of a tree is perceived to be continuous and indivisible from the root, the arms from the trunk, the branches from the arms, and the twigs and fruit and leaves from the branches. Behold, therefore (judicious reader), the dimension of the aevial world according to the saying of the preceding text: *Christ is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature, in whom all things were founded in heavens and on earth, visible and invisible, whether Thrones, or Dominions, etc.*: That is, the creatures of the aevial world, both in the heavens and elements as well as on earth, were founded in Christ: But this also from the Fathers of the Church...

For 2 are the root of matter, and 3 are the formal root: as 1 is the formal root in the Archetype to 3, and the material to 2: so indeed 2 are the material root to 4. The seventh Kabbalistic numeration or branch of the Sephirotic tree has for its Lord the title of God *Jehovah Sabaoth*, as if to say God of Hosts, and the God of jubilation and perfection. Therefore the attribute, gate, or channel through which its rays or brightness go out is called *Netzach*, as if to say Triumph, victory, and also justice, charity, and love; wherefore the influences of generation, multiplication, and delight proceed from this emanation. Its treasury among the heavenly bodies is the star of Venus.

The eighth name, by its property, is *Elohim Sabaoth*, or God of Hosts, and the gate through which its rays pass is called by the Hebrews *Hod*, that is, praise, honor, and beauty. The celestial storehouse, which is ordained to receive and preserve its influences, is the star of Mercury.

The ninth, which is assigned to the ninth branch of the tree, is *Elchai*, that is, the living God, or *Shaddai*, that is, God Almighty; and its numeration or gate is *Yesod*, that is, basis, foundation, rest, and redemption. The celestial Moon receives the outflow of this, which is like a small earth, receiving all the aforementioned influences in general which descend from on high. This is the reason why she is subject to so many changes or alterations, the effect of which is seen as much in generation and corruption as in the rising or falling of the sea.

The final title, which presides over the tenth gate called *Malkuth*—that is, kingdom and dominion—is *Adonai* or Lord, which indeed brings severity and captivity to creatures through the wrath of God; the effects of this attribute fall into the Elemental region.

By these observations and collections of the wisest Rabbis, we find that in these ten general properties of the eternal divinity signified by the ten attributes, all things in this world are disposed—whether they are esteemed by a creature as good or evil, positive or privative, harmonious and lovable or discordant and hateful, and, to put it in a word, whether they are secretly or openly opposed, or agreeing in nature or condition—and they descend from a single unity. From this it is clear how that unity in essence is manifold in property and condition, according to whose diversity in "Willing" and "Not Willing" diverse and plainly opposite things are done and operated in the world, both celestial and elemental; indeed, it is so in the Empyrean <note>The highest heaven of pure light and fire</note>, and that by particular emanations springing from the Universal and Archetypal emanation. And again, each of the said ten Sephirotic emanations is distinguished by almost infinite other radiations not discordant from the will of their source. From which it also follows that each of these properties has stellar receptacles in the ethereal heaven, both fixed and wandering <note>planets</note>, which pour out their virtues into infinite sublunary creatures—animal, vegetable, and mineral—all of which are observed to vary from one another according to the properties of the influences, both in form and nature. And the reason why the divinity created or sent out one outflow of rays contrary to another was as much for the preservation as for the destruction of creatures. For, just as the final effect of these emanations was the creation, generation, and preservation of creatures of their own condition and nature, so indeed these effects are usually applied either for the preservation of failing and infirm creatures—namely, when we apply some poisonous simple <note>A medicinal herb or mineral</note>, whether animal, vegetable, or mineral, to drive away a most dangerous disease; for example, in the animal kingdom the viper, the scorpion, the toad, the spider, or the blistering Spanish fly <note>original: "Cauthari-dem veficantem"</note>, etc.; in the vegetable, the dulling poppy or sleep-inducing opium, the cauterizing spearwort <note>original: "Flammulam"</note>, vomiting hellebore, aconite, etc.; in the mineral, arsenic, quicksilver, red arsenic <note>original: "Refalgar"</note>, antimony, etc. All these simples have the property both to take away diseases and to induce them in animals; indeed, they certainly sometimes lead to killing them. For in this the more skilled in Theology agree: that just as the higher orders of Angels receive their lights and most splendid emanations immediately from God, so indeed they emit and manifest them to the lower orders of Angels; and for this reason they are called polished mirrors, insofar as they receive their lights from the face of God or His eternal emanation: which (as I have proved before) is the head of all these Angelic lights. And again, as the more abstruse Theosophists <note>original: "Theophi"</note> have observed through their serious collections from the sacred page ten distinct properties, and also as many various names or names of God appropriated to them: so indeed they perceived that there is some singular Angel who would receive the influence of each of their irradiations, and would be endowed with the nature and property of that influence, namely, by means of which they live and are animated; insofar as, just as the external of an Angel is spiritual air, so his internal is that formal emanation whose power he is the vehicle of: and this is the general opinion among the occult Theosophists, with whom Dionysius <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, author of 'The Celestial Hierarchy'</note> and Bartholomew seem to agree, namely that one Angel ought not to mix himself with the business or office of another, nor undertake the labors of another, unless it be such an Angel of a lower order who is subjected to the Authority and government of his Archangel, with whose property and nature he is also marked, as will be said more widely below.

For, says Paul, he is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature, in whom all things visible and invisible were founded, whether Thrones, or Dominions, or Principalities, or Powers, all things were created through him and in him, and all things consist in him. <margin>*Colossians 1:15*</margin> Wherefore also the Hebrew Rabbis apply Metatron, who is said to have made his way into the world through the royal gate of Kether <note>original: "Cheter"</note> or the Crown, and is called the first creature, insofar as he denotes the Universal spirit of the world, who first of all received the firstborn or imperial emanation from the attribute of God *Ehyeh* <note>original: "Ebieb"; the Hebrew name 'I Am'</note>, which is the name of eternity, since it looks to the present and future time. For that cause, therefore, the Great Angel names himself *Alpha and Omega*, the beginning and the end. Thus *Keter* <note>original: "Cheter"; the Crown, the first Sephirah</note> is sent forth into the highest order of Angels, called the *Seraphim*, who, by reason of their proximity to the Throne of God, are said to *burn* and be inflamed with fiery love; and it is from this that this order is adorned with such excellence and beauty, namely by reason of that primary and most brilliant emanation, which is filled with the abundance of so lovely and benign a Father of Light. From here, therefore, this powerful Angel conducts these lucid outflows into the cavity of the ethereal heaven, and reserves them in it as if in his universal sanctuary: and by the presence of that spirit of light, it is presently animated and quickened, so that by the admirable reason of its action it is called the first mover of the heavens, as that in which the *primum mobile* <note>The "first moved" sphere in Aristotelian astronomy</note> is moved, by whose motion the remaining orbs of the heavens, constituting the natural world, are carried from east to west in the space of 24 hours.

From these things, therefore, it is clear what the soul of the world is, namely that holy emanation so clothed by the spirit of the heavens, a Divine irradiation, penetrating through the second gate *Chokmah* <note>original: "Hochma"; Wisdom</note>, which is emitted from the divine name *Yah* <note>original: "Iah"</note>: it passes through the orders of the *Cherubim*, which signifies the fullness of knowledge and the abundance of the gifts of wisdom: and the influences of that irradiation are said to be received by the Archangel *Zophiel* (which name denotes beauty) as far as the infinite particular <unclear>vibalistis</unclear> <note>likely a typo for Cabalists</note>, who call this conductor of these rays *Raziel*, who directs them immediately into the Firmament or starry heaven, and especially into that Zone of the heaven which is called the Zodiac and the sign-bearer, proving by this Etymology of its name that the rays hidden folded within it ideally delineate the infinite species of particular creatures, all of which it afterwards depicts realistically and explicitly in the Elementary region.

The third outflow of rays occurs through the gate *Binah* <note>Understanding</note>, over which the divine name *Elohim* presides, and it descends immediately into the order of *Thrones*; arguing from there the severe property of God and one full of judgment. These rays are received by the Archangel *Zaphkiel* <note>original: "Zabkiel"</note>, or, as others wish, *Zaphiel*, signifying the Spirit of great Wrath. And this spirit conducts these influxes to the Sphere of Saturn, which he fills with Spirits or Intelligences of his own nature, whom they call *Saturnines*, or *Bene-Elohim* <note>Sons of God</note>: and finally these pour forth into the Elemental world—namely, air, water, earth—the influences or subtle spirits of nature.

The fourth emanation is conducted through the Channel *Chesed* <note>original: "Cheſed"; Mercy</note>, over which the holy name *El* presides; it is received by the Archangel of the order of Dominions, who demonstrates power against malignant spirits, and assigns life and breath to creatures: and that Archangel is called *Zadkiel*, which signifies the spirit of justice, and that spirit, according to the nature of the influence which he conducts, is a friend of true justice in the proportion of life and the Elements: and consequently a favorer and Patron of the life of creatures. He carries these rays downward into the orb of Jupiter, fills it with infinite spirits of his own nature and condition, which are called Jovial Intelligences, which rain down a portion of their influence upon the sublunary creatures subject to them, which live, multiply, and are preserved.

The fifth emission of rays occurs through the gate *Gevurah* <note>original: "Geburah"; Severity/Strength</note>, over which the divine name *Elohim Gibbor* <note>God of Might</note> presides: and these rays are said to descend to the order of Powers, and the Archangel to whom these rays are committed is called *Samael*, or, as others wish, *Hamael*: and he is the Spirit who brings terror: and that Intelligence conducts those rays into the Sphere or orb of Mars, and fills it with spirits or Intelligences of his own nature, and by the fiery heat of his condition he fashions the Martial star, from which Martial influences are poured forth into the Elemental region, and especially to the creatures subject to it.

The sixth emission of divine rays occurs through the Sephirotic Channel *Tiferet* <note>original: "Tipbereth"; Beauty</note>, whose lord is the Name of God *Eloah*: and these descend immediately into the order of Virtues. Hence *Isidore* <note>likely Isidore of Seville</note> says that the Angels of this order receive illumination, purgation, and perfection from God; and under the leader Archangel *Michael* (which signifies "who is like God") they are conducted into the Sphere of the Sun, and from there they are distilled to the lower parts for the quickening, multiplication, preservation, and adornment of creatures.

The seventh extension of rays occurs through the gate *Netzach* <note>original: "Nezaeh"; Victory</note>, over which the name *Jehovah Sabaoth* <note>Lord of Hosts</note> presides, and from it they pass to the order of Principalities, from which they are carried by the Archangel *Haniel* <note>original: "Anäelem"</note> to the Sphere of Venus, from which they afterwards descend to the creatures subject to it in the Elemental world.

The eighth emission of rays occurs through the gate *Hod* <note>Splendor</note>, and over this the name *Elohim Sabaoth* presides: these descend into the order of Archangels, where they are conducted by the Archangel *Raphael* into the Sphere of Mercury, and from it they are sent into the creatures subject to them in the Elemental world.

The ninth emanation of light occurs through the gate *Yesod* <note>original: "Iefod"; Foundation</note>, over which the name *Shaddai* <note>original: "Sadai"</note> presides, which descends to the order of Angels, and there they are received by the Archangel *Gabriel* and descend to the lower parts for the animation and quickening of the creatures subject to him.

The tenth and last extension of rays occurs through the Channel *Malkuth* <note>original: "Malchut"; Kingdom</note>, over which the name *Adonai* rules, and this descends immediately (as the Cabalists wish) into the order of blessed Souls, from which into the Elemental region...

...the Elemental world. These are the intentions of the Cabalists <note>original: "Cabalistarum" — practitioners of Jewish mysticism, often adapted by Renaissance scholars</note> concerning that mystery of angelic irradiations.

Through the continuity, therefore, of those individual emanations and angelic irradiations—extending from them to the sub-Olympic demons <note>spirits residing below the highest celestial spheres</note>, and from them to the lunar spirits—we can gather, first, that God alone works all things in all people. Secondly, that according to the variety of His will, He acts in diverse forms in this world. Consequently, we ought to know that His will is multiform in its property, since things are brought about both in heaven and on earth according to a multiform operation, as may be gathered from the effects. Therefore, if God works all things in all, it is necessary that the diversity of that work proceeds from the multiplicity of His will. For this reason, Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the Hermetic corpus</note> says: "The will of God is the highest perfection of things, which necessity follows, and effect accompanies necessity." Consequently, he concludes that in a moment of time, God is accustomed to fulfill both His will and the effect of the same. But that which He does not wish to exist, that indeed cannot be. Therefore, whatever exists in the nature of things, of whatever property it may be, is brought about according to the will of one of those divine attributes. <margin>Asclepius 4</margin> "Nor," says Hermes, "is it believable that anything would displease God which has pleased Him, since He knew long before both that it would be and that it would please Him." And likewise Solomon <margin>Wisdom 11</margin> <note>original: "Sap. 11" — The Book of Wisdom, Chapter 11:25</note>: "How would anything have endured, unless you had willed it?"

Thirdly, we gather that according to the variety of the divine will, all things were created, of which one either spiritually sympathizes in affection with another, or both have antipathy <term>Antipathy/Sympathy: the hidden natural attraction or repulsion between objects</term> between themselves, by reason of the rays giving either a similar or an opposite nature of angelic irradiation—or the emanation of rays from one spiritual creature to another. This contrariety of conditions proceeds from the variety of properties which are in the will of the one eternal Essence. In this manner, therefore, all creatures of this world, both spiritual and corporeal, were composed; and in this way they were quickened and animated through rays, of which one is contrary to another in condition, or by reason of their harmony and similarity of nature. They exult greatly when the rays of one influence look upon each other.

We must know, however, that although every creature has its radical formation from these emanations, yet in their generations and multiplications they can vary and differ from the condition of their creators or their parents, by reason of the union of two different irradiations at the hour of birth. From this it happens that a son can be unlike his parents both in figure and condition: for instance, a horse more furious or mild than its sire; a plant or fruit more loose, watery, and unhealthy than the tree from which it was taken as a shoot. Consequently, through the application of angelic rays of contrary strength at the birth of a man, the irradiation—or the emission of rays from a plant, flower, or beast, etc.—can perpetually hold an antipathy with that man. Just so, I knew a noblewoman to whose nature the irradiation of a rose was so contrary that by its mere touch while she was sleeping, a blister was raised on her face. Furthermore, another held a cat, and another a duck, in such great hatred that by their mere sight they were accustomed to fall into a faint <note>original: "lypothymiam" — a swoon or fainting spell</note>.

And while the opposition between the Elements is manifest in respect to that contention and fight which is between dissonant natures (namely cold and heat, etc.), so that in this case the root of such Sympathy and Antipathy—or rather the opposition of the Elements—is well known by all (namely the reason for the enmity between water and fire, and between air and earth); it must nevertheless be understood from what has been said above that there is a cause yet more hidden and internal for true Sympathy and Antipathy in things. This is ascribed by some to the occult natures of the stars, when in the truth of the matter it proceeds from those angelic influences of contrary strength which emanate invisibly and in an abstruse manner from creatures that were born under contrary, dissonant emanations.

Indeed, Reuchlin <margin>Reuchlin, Book 1 on the Art of the Cabala</margin> <note>Johann Reuchlin, a famous German humanist and scholar of the Cabala</note> proves to the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle</note> that every spherical heaven, besides its essential form, has an "assisting intelligence" as the mover of its orb, which is called an Angel; and that this angel, sent for this office, understanding and willing, fulfills the commands of the Creator as a middle power between God and nature. From this power operations are made in things which their nature either had not made, or had not made in such a way—which some say come from an "occult property," and others "because it is such." From these points it is clear that the occult Sympathy and Antipathy of things, both in celestial and terrestrial matters, proceed and are derived from the mystic and secret actions or irradiations of Angelic Spirits. These spirits first receive those properties from those peculiar influences and emanations which descend from the Sephirotic gates <note>The ten attributes/emanations in the Cabala through which the Infinite reveals itself</note>, or from the eternal source.

But, since it is not the office of the Astrologer to immerse himself so deeply in those mysteries which belong to the eternal world—inasmuch as it is his task to make the celestial stars the source and origin of those effects which descend to work through both Sympathy and Antipathy in lower things—I wish now, in the manner of an Astrologer, to indicate how both Sympathy and Antipathy arise from the manifold influence of the stars.

## CHAPTER IV.

->*Wherein the astrological reasoning for Sympathy and Antipathy is explained; where it is also proved that, since all lower spirits receive the influences of their natures from above, and since Elemental creatures are nothing but images of the heavenly ones, it must necessarily follow that, just as there are both Sympathetic and Antipathetic aspects or radiations between two or more heavenly bodies, there must likewise be an emission of rays from one Elemental body to another, which, according to the nature of their emanation, are either Sympathetic or Antipathetic.*<-

Having held a fundamental discourse with the mystical Hebrew and Cabalistic <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism exploring the relationship between the infinite and the finite universe.</note> Theologians concerning Sympathy and Antipathy, it now remains for us to reveal their secrets in the Astrological manner—namely, by taking the visible instrument for the invisible agent. This means taking the external form of the creature for its internal Angelic virtue, and the stellar influence for the hidden and central emanation of the Divinity. This divinity (as I have said) is poured out into those spirits or intelligences that inhabit and illuminate the Stars; from them, they emit the influences of that light into the Elemental world to animate the winds—according to the fourfold change of the common Universal <note>original: "Catholici"</note> Element—and for the procreation of multiform Meteors and the production of perfectly mixed bodies.

It is necessary, therefore (speaking Astrologically), that there be a manifest opposition and agreement, not only in respect to the manifest Elements or winds, qualities, or natures which are discerned to be in the fixed stars as well as the wandering ones <note>The planets.</note> (for the watery signs of the zodiac are contrary to the fiery, the nocturnal to the diurnal, the eastern to the western, the masculine to the feminine, etc.), but also in respect to more hidden matters. For those more skilled in Astrology have noted that just as Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon are joined in friendship with Saturn, so indeed Mercury, Mars, and Venus are his enemies. Again, all Planets except Mars are friends to Jupiter. Furthermore, there is none of the planets, except Venus alone, who is a friend to Mars; but among the rest, the Sun and Mercury are his greatest enemies. Also, Jupiter and Venus are friends of the Sun; on the contrary, Mars, Mercury, and the Moon are the Sun's enemies. All planets are said to love and cherish Venus except Saturn. Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn are friends to Mercury; his enemies, however, are the Sun, the Moon, and Mars. The friends of the Moon are Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn; her enemies are Mars and Mercury. The friends of the Dragon's Head <note>The North Node of the Moon, considered auspicious.</note> are Jupiter and Venus; its enemies are Saturn and Mars. Finally, the enemies of the Dragon's Tail <note>The South Node of the Moon, considered inauspicious.</note> are Jupiter, the Moon, and Venus; while on the other hand, its friends are Saturn and Mars.

Beyond this, it should be noted that there is another kind of friendship and enmity between the planets—namely, when one of them is in its exaltation <note>A position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is most powerful.</note> in the house of another; in this case, the subject matter influenced by the one will lovingly receive the aspect of the other. Conversely, the Detriment <note>A weak position for a planet, opposite its home sign.</note> of one in the house of another will cause the spirit of a creature born under that planet (which suffers detriment through the bad aspect of the other who is in its own house) to look Antipathetically upon any thing subjected to the Lord of the other. In this way, I say, the presence of a thing born under a planet is a detriment to the Lord of that birth in the same house.

On the contrary, it should be observed that two creatures sympathize with each other and look upon one another with joy and gladness when the Lords of their births agree in nature, hidden virtue, and strength. For example, if Mars is the Lord of the birth of one and Venus of the other, these two Planets agree with each other by a certain natural instinct; and likewise Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, and the Moon accord with one another. Furthermore, we ought to know that a sign of the zodiac which possesses many dignities <note>The various ways a planet gains strength in a specific sign.</note> of a single planet—such as House, Triplicity, Face, Exaltation, Term, etc.—will best Sympathize and accord with the birth <note>original: "genitura"</note> of that planet. On the other hand, a sign or some fixed impression of the firmament which is in an opposite condition to the planet, or full of misfortunes (for example, if a Planet were in its Fall or Detriment, etc.), creates a certain hidden hatred by means of its rays. Moreover, the manner of the ejaculation of those rays from one another at the birth of an animal, or the true aspect of the rays, will remain and be expressed in the thing born or the vegetation produced. Therefore, I intend to express the nature of those rays or secret radiations that accompany the influences of the stars in an even broader and fuller way, since in them consists the secret of Astrological Sympathy and Antipathy in lower things.

First, therefore, we must know—according to the opinion of the most profound Astronomers and especially Al-Kindi <note>A 9th-century Islamic philosopher and scientist who wrote extensively on the "stellar rays" that influence the world.</note>—that every star possesses its own nature and condition, in which the ejection of rays with others is contained; and just as each one has its own nature, <margin>Al-Kindi [on] the rays,</margin> which...

For every star has its own position in the **world-machine** <note>original: "mundana machina" — a common Renaissance metaphor for the universe as a divinely crafted mechanism</note> distinct from all others. From this it necessarily follows that every star obtains a different relationship than any other toward all other things and places contained in the world. Moreover, the variation of the aspect <note>The angular relationship between celestial bodies</note> varies the effect of the rays, just as the other properties of the stars themselves vary.

From this it happens that every star works differently and in a different manner in diverse places and things, however small and however slightly they differ; since the entire operation of the stars proceeds through rays, which are varied within themselves in every different aspect. For the ray which proceeds from the center of a star to the center of the earth is proven to be the strongest in the species of its operation; but those which are slanted from the center of the earth are weakened in effect according to the proportion of their slant, except insofar as they are strengthened in those same places by the concurrent rays of other stars. For every star pours out its rays into every place, because of which the diversity of rays, fused into one, varies the contents of all places; since in every different place there is a different tenor of rays, which is derived from the total **harmony of the stars**. 

Furthermore, because this is continually changed by the continuous motion of the planets and other stars according to the location of the **World of Elements**, it continually moves all their contents into different conditions coming into action, according to the requirement of the harmony of that same time, although to human senses other things of the world seem to remain permanent. It is clear, therefore, that all different places and all different times constitute individuals in this world: which the **celestial Harmony** <note>The mathematical and musical order of the heavens</note> performs by projecting rays into the world, continually diversifying itself. By these things it is clear that the irradiations of all stars have different operations in the things of this world according to the diversity of the properties of things: insofar as all things exist and are derived from the emanation or emission of these rays. 

Furthermore, it should also be noted that the condition of celestial harmony is such that, since all stars are of different natures, and for that reason all their rays are of different effects in the Elementary world, it happens that their ray-like operations are assisted in the same matter or subject, and again in another they are hindered among themselves. It must also be observed that over any thing of this lower world, a **predominant star** is ordained, and again there is a certain celestial sign <note>A zodiacal sign</note> that presides over the work and property of the same. From this condition of the rays of the stars among themselves, so great a difference and diversity of things arises that two or more things can hardly be found in the world which are similar to each other in every respect, even if the human sense in some cases is sufficient to perceive their difference.

They conclude, therefore, that celestial harmony works so differently in different places and times that sometimes it produces similar things and sometimes dissimilar things, as much in shape as in property. Even now, it produces similar things through similar motion, and sometimes dissimilar things through dissimilar motion—namely, through slow and fast motion. When these things are well weighed, and since it is evident that the Elementary world was made according to the **celestial exemplar** <note>The idea that the physical world is a copy of a higher, heavenly pattern</note>, so that whatever is contained in the elemental world contains in itself the image of the celestial, we ought by no means to doubt that all things in this world, whether they be substances or essential accidents, emit their own rays toward one another in imitation of those stars under whose dominion they originated. For otherwise it would be impossible for them to comprehend within themselves the figure of the stellar world. 

But this is manifested and sensibly confirmed in certain things: for fire emits heat to its closer parts, and likewise the earth breathes out rays of its coldness from every side. Even medicines taken internally, or applied externally, ejaculate the rays of their virtue into the body. We also observe, by the collision of two solid bodies, that sound is produced by the pouring out of rays in its own way. Again, colored things extend their rays, by means of which they are perceived by the eyes; odorous things also emit rays of their virtue on all sides, so that they may be perceived by their scent. Since this is so, we can boldly assert that every thing of this world which has actual existence emits its rays everywhere in its own manner, filling its surroundings. 

And for this reason **Alkindus** <note>Al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD), a Persian philosopher who wrote "De Radiis," a fundamental text on the theory that everything in the universe emits rays</note> testifies that every place of this lower world contains the rays of all things which actually exist in it. And as every thing differs from another, so also the rays of any subject differ in nature and effect from the rays of all others. Whence it happens that the operation of the rays of all things in any different thing is varied and distinct. Thus far I have explained the opinions of the most learned **Astronomers** in this matter, namely concerning the irradiation of the celestial bodies, by which it seems to become known to us that every creature of this Elementary world is not only formed by these celestial rays, but is continually preserved by the mediation of their successive influences; and consequently that all things which exist in such influxes of heaven are **types or images** of those celestial spirits by whose rays they were formed. Wherefore it is necessary that it follows by the rule of Alkindus, that if they are types or **Icons** <note>original: "Icones" — images or representations</note> of the celestial figures which formed them, then it is necessary that in a similar manner [they emit] their own rays...

For the Genius <note>A guiding spirit or inherent nature assigned to a person or thing at birth.</note> of the former is terrified and excited to hatred at the sight of the other, because its star was an enemy to the first star and stronger in heaven. But you ought to observe that, although the stronger rays are antipathetic to the weaker, it does not follow that the weaker are antipathetic to the stronger: since it always happens that the stronger passion is in the weaker, while the stronger action remains in the stronger. But if a subject or creature under some star in heaven presents itself before a subject or creature whose Lord in heaven is an enemy to the aforementioned star, if there were no malevolent aspect in the birth of the former between those stars, an evident antipathy would not follow between those two objects from their irradiations; and yet their rays are all the more inclined toward actual opposition if, at the time or hour they are present, they are [influenced by] the Lord and rays of another planet. These two subjects, emitting their rays here onto the earth, shall also be joined in friendship: and they agree all the more among themselves in nature, property, and benevolence of aspect at the instant of their births or productions.

Regarding the active intellect or *Metatron* <note>original: "Mitattron"; the supreme angel in Jewish mysticism</note>, as he is the presiding governor of the whole world—whom I have previously called the Soul of the World, which animates every particular thing by emitting its infinite formal rays—we can conceive that the mystical Hebrews signified the same power that the Apostle, in the preceding passage, assigned to our Lord Jesus Christ. Just as they made their *Metatron* the Universal Angel or president of the universe, proceeding by way of emanation from *Ein Sof* <note>original: "Ensoph"; the Infinite or Divine Origin in Kabbalah</note> or infinity, so the Apostle seems to argue that all forms and every other thing proceed from God the Father and have their existence through the one Lord Jesus Christ.

To the point, then: Just as God ordained two principles contrary in nature from his infinite source of unity—namely, light and darkness—so indeed the first-born of darkness was Strife, or the Prince of Darkness, who is called Satan. His dominion is in the darkness and over all dark things and privative properties. And he has under him fourfold angels or demons of differing conditions, who have dominion over the four winds and the Universal Element; they are most ready at the commands of their prince to carry out dark business and, consequently, discord, antipathy, and privation. This is according to that passage in the <margin>Revelation 7:1</margin> Apocalypse:
> *I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that they should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree. And I saw an angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God, and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, etc.*

Now truly, each of these presiding angels has many divisions and subdivisions of legions of demons or spirits under his command, who act according to their will when the power of breathing and disturbing the air is assigned to them. However, all of these are animated by influences poured out from the Olympic or celestial spirits, just as they themselves have their animation and times of dominion assigned by the imperial Archangel who ascends from the rising of the sun. And these angels of the winds are the immediate dispensers of the eternal and radical will in the Elementary world. For this reason, as we see with our own eyes: that the solar rays totally illuminate the object they gaze upon, and that this illumination happens by reason of the multitude of rays united within it; so also all emanations carried down into the stellar bodies fill them with an infinity of rays. These rays serve them in place of subdivided angels and render or convert them into the nature of that entire emanation which animated that star. For this cause, all Olympic stars are similar in property. The same logic applies to the angelic rays, which are sent forth from the Thrones of the winds to the air and all lower things—namely the air and the earth—filling them with an infinite number of spirits that are harmful by their nature.

And yet this is certain: that as God created all things so that they might exist and be (as Solomon witnesses), so He, out of His paternal goodness, took care that as many good angels with their subject spirits, gushing forth from His good rays, should preside over the evil ones themselves, to suppress and blunt their malice and malevolence; these likewise have their dwellings in the air or the Universal Element. From this it is clear that every president of those harmful winds is governed by a better, worthier, and more propitious intelligence, and is restrained from his malice at his pleasure. For the Text says:
> *And I saw an angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying: Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads, etc.*
<margin>Revelation 7:3</margin>

Others esteem him as the image of Eternal Wisdom, by which all things were made. In any case, he was that imperial angel who triumphed in his victory over the Dragon and his angels, and consequently held them under his dominion. So, just as Satan is the prince of darkness and an enemy to light and consequently to Christ and His creatures, so this great Angel (in whom is the name of Jehovah, as the scriptures recount), in whom is life and light without any darkness, is the prince of light. He has power over light, position, and life, and therefore is an enemy to the prince of darkness and the effects arising from them.
