But as for the four leaders of God, that they themselves are also the primary guardians and governors of the winds, <margin>Telec. lex lib. de 10. nume. rit.</margin> we gather from this speech of Rabbi *Tedaci*: *God*, he says, created four Angels for the four winds, who are set over them by day and by night: *Michael*, who is on the side of Clemency and mercy, is appointed as *Mamona* <note>a Hebrew term for a governor or steward</note>, that is, the prefect over the east wind until midday and until night; and *Raphael* rules the west wind, who is similarly of the side of Clemency; then *Gabriel*, in the power of judgment and severity, is prefect over the North wind over half the night and two measures of the world; but *Noriel* or *Uriel* presides over the South, etc. Thus, we see that, just as there are good irradiations and more benign spirits, who by a secret emanation extend themselves from the Angels of the winds into the open air—namely those who emanate in a secret and arcane manner from the benign attributes of Jehovah, such as *El* through Jupiter, *Eloah* through the Sun, *Shaddai* <note>original: "Sadas"</note> through Venus, etc.—then *Michael*, *Raphael*, *Gabriel*, and *Uriel*, by means of their legions, carry out the divine will. Besides these, there are evil and corrupt spirits of a contrary strength of wind, who have their origin from *Elohim*, *Elohim Gibbor*, and *Adonai* <note>here referring to the more severe or judgmental aspects of the divine names</note>, whose celestial storehouses are *Saturn*, *Mars*, and the *Moon*. Nor indeed should anyone be led by wonder that I derive the multiplicity of good and evil properties manifested by the winds from the divine essence, which imparted the power to fulfill its will through various properties to its four appointed Archangels; since the Prophet by divine command said:
<margin>Ezekiel 37.</margin>
> *Come, spirit, from the four winds and breathe upon these slain, that they may live, etc.*
> *By which the Prophet signifies, that there is but one life-giving spirit in science*

which fills this whole [world], and consequently, that the four opposite properties in the four Angels, who are the presidents of the winds, are influences or essential rays of one and the same Spirit of life in essence. By reason of these spirits of contrary strength in the air, sometimes good and propitious events happen to the creatures of the lower world—namely, when the good spirits have Dominion, and the salutary winds blow, which usually happens while the benign stars have Dominion in heaven—and sometimes when evil and pernicious ones are observed to blow with a privative and destructive success, when they are governed by depraved and malevolent spirits. Indeed, by their emanations, the malignant spirits flying and as if swimming everywhere in the air are encouraged and incited to perpetrate crimes against creatures; and in the invisible blasts or irradiations sent out by their cruel presidents, they exult and rejoice abundantly, because by these emissions those spirits of contrary strengths, formerly asleep, are now excited to war and fury. But all this is best explained by *Joseph of Castile* <note>Joseph Gikatilla, a famous Spanish Cabalist</note>. From the earth, he says, even unto the Firmament there is no empty place, but all is full of forms; of these some are pure; of these some are capable of grace and mercies; and there are below many foul, harmful, and tempting figures, all dwelling and flying in the air: and there is no empty place from the earth to heaven, but the whole is filled with species: of these for peace, of these for war, of these for good, of these for evil, of these for life, of these for death, and all that in the lower habitation in which we are, etc. *By which he argues, that the entire sublunary Element is filled with spirits both good and evil.* Therefore, it is beyond all controversy that between these spirits of contrary strength there is a constant war and conflict in this elementary region, of which *Agonists* <note>combatants or contestants</note> some are ordered under the veil of the prince of light and life or position, and others under those of darkness, privation, and death, of whom the latter are most ready to perform the pleasure of the dark prince. They are also very familiar with the moist nature or water, which is the matter of the world, and the offspring of the Chaos of darkness or the abyss. And therefore, by natural instinct, they have great Dominion over it: whence by reason of its inclinations toward darkness, it is very easily seduced from the society of light. Hence we understand from the Scriptures that the material world, the flesh, and the Devil are joined to each other by the tightest bonds: wherefore, every pious Christian is warned to beware of these three. Hence also Satan is called by the name of the prince of the air, which is the more spiritual part of the lower waters, from which the substance of the world arose; but those good ones attend the prince of light and life, their Lord, who is the Spirit of Wisdom proceeding from the most lucid word of eternity. From the positive side come the good qualities, such as joy, charity, hope, confidence, mercy, magnanimity, love or friendship, and concord; in the **Microcosm** <note>The human being as a "little world"</note> these arise from the dilation of the heart, and in the **Macrocosm** <note>The universe as a "great world"</note> they manifest as appetite, desire, delight, audacity or magnanimity, vegetation, and all beneficial actions within it, arising from the gracious rarefaction and dilation of its spirit through the mundane soul. Conversely, the depraved passions in the spirit of the microcosm, which are: Sadness, hatred, despair, fear, anger, fury, shame, and discord, proceed from the contraction of the heart. In the spirit of the greater world and its creatures, stupor, freezing, discord, irascibility, fear, hatred, and finally **Antipathy** <note>Natural aversion or repulsion</note> are formed by the contractive disposition of the mundane soul. All these passions either affect creatures well and lead to the solace and happiness of the vital spirits, or they weigh down their spirits and render them unhappy by reason of dark and contracting mists.

## CHAPTER V.

->Which actions in the spirit or soul generally produce **Sympathy** <note>Natural affinity or attraction</note> and which produce Antipathy, and how Sympathy or compassion proceeds from a certain dilation of the spirits in one or two particulars—or from the emission of rays of life or of a positive and benign essence from the center toward the circumference? And on the contrary, how Antipathy happens through the contraction of rays from the circumference to the center.<-

I have made known to you in the preceding sections that two properties existed in an **Archetypal** <note>The original divine pattern</note> or Ideal and "enfolded" manner within one radical unity or eternal essence: one of which was produced by His Will, and the other by His "Non-Will" <note>Latin: *Noluntate*, the divine withdrawal or negation</note>. Behold here the root from which both Sympathy and Antipathy originally arose; the latter takes its beginning from the privative property or divine Non-Will, while the former begins from the positive property or His Will. Then afterwards I recited to you that from that root or unity in the essence, a twin branch or double member was derived: expressing typically and explicitly the contrary effects and natures of those properties which were enfolded in the Ideal root—namely, **Darkness**, which is the fruit of His privative Non-Will; and **Light**, which is the true Character or undoubted sign of His Will. I then proved that these two were the principles of all things. Behold, therefore, here the two immediate principles of Sympathy and Antipathy, derived from a single stock or root. In the third place, I demonstrated to you that by the separation of the pure from the impure **Dark Chaos** (which was effected by the **Spagyric** <note>Alchemical separation and recombination</note> virtue of the most lucid emanation or Word of the eternal unity), the moist or watery nature of the world—the essential spirit informing all things—was created or essentially formed. Thus, in the union of those two contrary natures—namely, the informing essence or **Nurturing Nature** <note>Latin: *natura naturans*, God as the creative source</note> and the **Nurtured Nature** <note>Latin: *natura naturata*, the created world</note> or informed substance—the spirit of the world was animated into one. And then afterwards, according to the wise Philosophers, it was called the **Soul of the World**, which was that Angelic composition of the Two, which for this reason is called **Otherness** <note>Latin: *Alteritas*</note>; just as God, considered in His simple and eternal nature, is called **Identity**. Now indeed, the passive portion from which Otherness was made is called the created moist nature, or the "nurtured" matter of the world, whose active or internal essence is a living and agile emanation from eternity, which (as the Apostle teaches us) quickens all things and fills all things, and is all in all. The union of these two constitutes the Universal Soul of the World, which is called **Mind** <note>Latin: *Mens*</note> in respect to the simple creation and quickening emanation, and **Spirit** by reason of the spirit created from it, and **Soul** when considering both united into one. Behold here the third step of the Antipathetic and Sympathetic progression from the simple root of eternity: namely, created matter or spirit existing in the soul of the world, the offspring of the Dark Chaos; and for this reason, it is naturally inclined toward the privative and negative effects of darkness, and consequently is most fit for receiving Antipathetic or discordant impressions, which the Angelic spirits of darkness are accustomed to imprint upon it. For, just as the sacred Light—which animates the moist spirit of the world and consequently the entire mass of waters from which heaven and earth were made, as St. Peter asserts—is the most noble, active, and agile of all things, according to Solomon, so also on the opposite side is the matter which is informed (and therefore the created body and spirit is greatly degenerate from the light) and by its own nature is least...

is inclined toward motion and life: For these are the words of the **Philosophers** <note>original: "Philosophorum"; likely referring to the Neoplatonists or Hermetic thinkers</note>, that matter is of itself ineffective toward motion, degenerating clearly from the soul itself. Wherefore, by its twofold disposition, it willingly puts on the matter of **Chaos**, or the condition of dark **hyle** <term>hyle: a Greek term for "prime matter" or the raw, unformed substance of the universe</term>, which is prone to rest, immobility, darkness, coldness, thickness, and freezing. For this reason, therefore, watery matter suffers the impressions of both opposites: namely, sometimes it inclines toward darkness, and then it is thickened and rendered opaque, cold, fixed, and heavy. In this property, it tends downward and toward the cold center or seat of darkness, which serves as its mother; in this state, it is rendered rebellious and most opposed to light, motion, and heat. Thus, it is rendered **Antipathetic** <note>original: "Antipathetica"; acting in opposition or natural aversion</note> to the actions of light and life.

We see this in the air and the mundane spirit, which is elevated, **Diaphanous** <note>transparent</note>, thin, mobile, and tending upward—all of which it receives from the descending celestial light. Yet, on the other hand, by the approach or arrival of northern Cold (which is the offspring of dark Chaos), that spirit is suddenly changed; for it is frozen and rendered opaque, thick, immobile, and fixed, insofar as it is condensed into snow, frost, ice, hail, and the like. Thus, by the **Antipathetic** arrival of such cold darkness, it is made discordant and turned away from that lovely union and **Sympathetic** approach which it has with the region of light.

On the other side, the lucid form of the soul, which is the essence of that eternal emanation, gives to the air spirit, life, action, motion, heat, lightness or thinness, and transparency: or, as the Apostle holds, *life, breath, and all things.* <note>A reference to Acts 17:25</note> And we ought to note that the closer the spirit approaches the nature of light, the firmer are the bonds or knots of its **Sympathetic** concord. For, as **Sympathy** consists of things of a similar nature, so the more the spirit approaches the form, the firmer is its **Sympathy** or bond of concord, and the stronger and more effective its virtue. For the more the created spirit is illuminated, the less it remembers that natural inclination and love which it had for its obscure and deformed origin, so that through such a purified exaltation, it appears to approach the nature of divinity itself.

And therefore it is the opinion of **Plato** that if the middle spirit of the internal man—namely, that which is between the mental ray and the dark spirit of the body—adheres more to the good spirit, it will migrate into the **Elemental** nature <note>The text here suggests a transition toward a higher, more refined state of being</note>. But if it turns downward to the dark spirit of the body and the **Elemental** nature, then it is converted into the condition of a **Cacodaemon** <term>Cacodaemon: an evil spirit or demon</term>, and will be most near to the nature of its dark parent. We are also taught by the Scriptures that through the spiritual Christ, we shall finally be transformed into the same image—namely, if our intermediate internal spirit, by neglecting lower things (that is, by rejecting the lusts of the flesh), raises itself to the joys and purities of the higher realms.

But to return to the soul of the greater world <note>The Macrocosm</note>: If the airy spirit is delivered into the power of darkness and its prince, it becomes corporeal and is converted into the image of an opaque body, namely into frost, snow, hail, etc. But if the spirit, by heat and the act of formal light, prevails over the stupid cold of darkness, then the aforesaid body (whether of snow or ice, etc.) will cast off its opacity and be rendered **Diaphanous** and transparent; that is, it is led back from a fixed and opaque earthly nature into a watery, limpid, and flowing one. And again, through another degree of approach to the dominion of light, it will be further dilated, so that it is reduced from a visible watery state into an invisible and airy state.

Furthermore, by a third degree of approach to the light, it will be purified into the state and condition of fire. Finally, by a fourth degree, it will transmigrate into the nature of the ethereal or celestial substance, in which state it loses all appetite for change, and has now entirely forgotten the private stock from which it originally sprang. In this state, it also transcends the limits of corruption and puts on an incorruptible condition, being now least subject to changes. And at last, through a fifth degree, it transcends into the [extra-]temporal world and migrates into the bird-like or **Angelic** state: for it now holds itself equal with the condition of the **Empyrean** <note>The highest heaven, associated with pure fire and light</note> substance.

And thus it is more or less exalted in dignity, according as it is more or less obedient to the act of the eternal or **Catholic** <note>original: "Catholicæ"; here meaning universal or all-encompassing</note> formal influence. For we must understand that the entire inclination of the eternal emanation is to lead the offspring of darkness back from the confused mundane multitude to the unity and life of eternal light, so that the effort from the region of potential darkness may turn toward the opposite. The entire end of the action of creating light tends toward connecting all things in the world—which are divided and mutually contrary—into unity by the **Symphonic** bonds of friendship and unity. That is, to make the **Catholic** [universal] darkness similar to itself, so that **Antipathy** being finally banished into everlasting exile, the world and its supreme mind may **Sympathize** with each other in eternal love and friendship.

Yet, darkness resists this most excellent intention of light to the utmost, so that a duality of unity might perpetually remain in the world, whereby the union of concord and the laws of discord and **Antipathy** might be maintained to the detriment of friendship and peace among mundane things. From which it is clear that the subject, having been redeemed from the bowels of the dark and deformed **Chaos** by means of the emanation of light, now remains as a middle substance between those two extremes, namely, light...

### SECTION TWO, BOOK II. Member I.

...or the attribute of *Tiphereth* <note>Hebrew: "Beauty," the sixth Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, associated with the Sun and harmony.</note> in its ascent, from which it receives such great grace, beauty, and life-giving power; so much so, that the Solar light, by its emanation, penetrates and sees through all things. It is the Father not only of life, but also of vegetation, multiplication, and preservation. And this spirit placed its Tabernacle in the center of heaven for this reason: so that by one most perfect spiritual consonance—namely, the *Diapason* <note>The musical interval of an octave, representing perfect harmony.</note>—it might illuminate and strengthen the higher Angels, and also illustrate with its rays the stars disposed all around it, and penetrate other material things even unto the center of the Elemental world and its creatures, so that they might likewise be animated and quickened by the power of its rays. Consequently, the spirits of darkness would be weakened by the glorious sight of its face. 

It is as if a string were extended from the luminous source reigning at the summit of the heavens to the center of the dark abyss or the terrestrial globe; if that string is struck, it yields a unison. But if it is pressed in the middle, each half-part will sound a *diapason* to that unison, proving a double perfection proceeding from the universal luminous emanation: one of which is to impart life, vegetation, and every other virtue to the lower waters; and the other creates a sympathetic concord in the higher realms. 

Now indeed, as the Solar body and the substance of the spiritual Ether are of a consistency of matter midway between the waters, it is manifest that it is a subject most easily altered by passions, both *Sympathetic* and *Antipathetic*. For otherwise, it would not be the immediate receptacle of those opposite and contrary emanations which descend from the differing attributes of God. But we find the contrary from the effect: for some stars are friendly and sympathize in nature with certain sublunary creatures, while again others pursue each other with hatred, and consequently emit contrary effects into the lower world, which excite contrary passions or impressions in the vital spirits or souls of certain Elemental creatures. 

Furthermore, we find that animal life consists in opposite actions, namely in *Systole* and *Diastole* <note>The contraction and expansion of the heart.</note>—that is, contraction, which is caused by spiritual matter; and dilation, which is caused by the act of formal light. Thus, the nature of matter works through contraction from the circumference toward the center, but the condition of the formal essence is to dilate and emit its rays from the center to the circumference. Even philosophers and physicians testify that in sleep and rest, the vital spirits are accustomed to contract themselves from the circumference to the center, according to the condition of the dark chaos and the *Boreal* <note>Northern</note> wind, which by its attractive faculty causes the agile and volatile spirit or air of the lower world to be rendered quiet, fixed, and condensed. Thus also, by the contraction of the rays of the spirits, sleep is reconciled. But on the other hand, they conclude regarding wakefulness: that it occurs through the emission of rays or spirits from the center to the circumference. This is indeed an argument verifying the operation of the firmament in the souls or spirits of sublunary creatures through two contrary effects; and yet, by reason of the equality of every action and passion toward one another, they have a composite disposition, according as they agree among themselves in the natural operation of life which descends from above. Hence it is evident that from the starry heaven, *Sympathy* and *Antipathy* descend radically.

As far as the Elemental world is concerned, it is certain that it abounds with the manifest effects of these two contrarieties. Therefore, lest any continuous preternatural disturbance should follow—which would corrupt this great formal craftsman <note>The Demiurge or Creator</note> in his expected outcome, which was to place peace and concord in the machine formed by him—he distinguished everything of this sublunary heaven by number, measure, and weight. In this way, a friendly orb was placed as if between two extreme enemies; so that he assigned the smallest measure of form to the heavier portion of the lower waters, so that by reason of its weight it might fall to the center of the whole fabric and remain fixed in it, and it was called **Earth**. 

Then, to the second portion of the lower waters, he imparted a double proportion of formal light, so that by means of it, it might be elevated one degree higher. Whence it happened that the sphere of waters nearest to the earth was made thinner, lighter, and more mobile than the earth. For a double proportion of light would cause the frozen and fixed water to melt a little and be rendered fluid and transparent; so that, partly because of the continuity of its substance with that of the earth, and partly in respect to its coldness, it is a temperate and indifferent friend to the earth, and a friendly mediator between the earth and the **Air**, which are most hostile to each other. For it is not as cold and foul [as earth], nor as moist as air. 

Next, the luminous agent of the world assigned to another portion of the lower waters—or the *Universal Element*—three parts of its light, so that it was converted into an existence thinner and lighter than was the sphere of waters nearest the earth, and that orb is called **Air**. By reason of its triple proportion in formal light, it was hotter and more dilated than water. Wherefore, as water was cold; and yet not so cold...

...sorrow and fear: for we are accustomed to feel sorrow already in that which we hate, or we are accustomed to fear that which would make us suffer. And indeed, once a proper inquiry has been made, we shall find that these four affections of the microcosmic soul <note>The "microcosmic soul" refers to the human soul, viewed as a small-scale reflection of the entire universe.</note> are not only the principles and common subjects of all moral vices and virtues, but are also the origins of both the abstruse or secret, and the manifest and apparent Sympathies and Antipathies in the greater world <note>The "greater world" or Macrocosm refers to the universe/heavens.</note> and its creatures, as well as in the lesser. For I would not wish you to be ignorant of the fact that, since the soul of man arises from the eternal emanation dwelling in the worldly tabernacle, it must necessarily follow that the soul in the great world possesses all the same faculties within itself with which that of the microcosm or human soul is endowed. For that well-worn axiom of the Philosophers holds: *That which makes a thing such, is itself more so* <note>original: "Quod facit tale, est magistale" — a scholastic principle meaning a cause must possess the quality it gives to its effect in a higher degree.</note>. But all the aforementioned virtues or properties in the human soul proceed from the soul of the macrocosm and the divine mind which animated it.

From this it follows that there is rationality, as well as concupiscibility <note>The faculty of desire or longing.</note> and irascibility <note>The faculty of anger or spiritedness.</note> in the soul of the greater world, even if they are not manifested to us. And we prove this first, because God has the attributes of Irascibility and severity within Himself: For from the attribute of the divine name *Elohim Gibbor* <note>Hebrew: "God the Mighty," associated with judgment.</note>, namely through the gate of *Geburah* <note>The Sephirah of "Strength" or "Severity" in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.</note>, are emitted the fires and flame-vomiting rays of divine wrath, with the *Archangel Samael* as leader into the sphere of Mars; these are the authors of Anger and Bile in creatures, and consequently the origin of the irascible faculty in the greater world. Whence it happens that by such influences, angry and fiery effects are produced in the Elemental world, such as thunders, lightnings, comets, and all wrathful accidents. Wherefore, by the testimony of Holy Scripture, these are arguments of divine wrath and vengeance: since their effects are frequently war, plague, famine, etc. For they not only convert spirits into a wrathful nature, but also disseminate within them effects and bloody and ferocious imaginations, malice, ambition, violence, discord, betrayal, robbery, and others of that kind.

Furthermore, the name of God *Elohim* also flows its influences through the gate of *Binah* <note>The Sephirah of "Understanding."</note> into the Sphere of Saturn, and from there into the sublunary region; it is the cause of fear, hatred, suspicion, sadness, and malevolence in the great world as well as in the lesser. Behold here the roots of the irascible faculty and of the affections of fear itself, namely sorrow and fear.

On the other hand, the name of God *Jehovah Sabaoth* <note>Hebrew: "Lord of Hosts."</note> pours out concupiscible rays through the gate of *Netzach* <note>The Sephirah of "Victory" or "Endurance," often associated with Venus.</note>, with the Archangel Anael as leader into the globe of Venus; and for this reason, Philosophers and Astronomers, taught by experience and observation, have made that star the ruler of the concupiscible faculty. Just as also the denomination of God *El* pours out the rays of reason, justice, and religion, and even of natural vegetation, into the sphere of Jupiter. But besides the rest, that *Isab* <note>Likely a reference to a specific divine name or angelic power in the author's system.</note> liberally pours out the natural faculty through the gate of wisdom.

Secondly, because the great world has an intellectual or rational heaven, and a concupiscible property made manifest in every creature—animal and vegetable as well as mineral—and an irascible one, which appears among things by reason of hatred and horror. Also, that there is an irascible property in the Elemental region is witnessed by that enmity which exists between water and fire, and air and earth. That there is also love and desire among things is made evident in it, because like rejoices in its like, and nature delights in nature: and therefore every thing is moved by a certain natural inclination, as far as possible, and turns itself toward its like. Thus we see that fire is inclined to move toward fire, water toward water, and earth tends toward earth.

But above all, the vivifying spirit of any living thing, which is celestial and therefore exceeds the place and seat of the Elements, ardently affects and gasps for its like, and is delighted in its presence and society; so that for this reason, the passion of any creature will be toward more Sympathetic things. And Sympathy between things is of greater power the closer they are in nature and kinship, whether the things are present or absent or distant. For example, if both are of the same mineral or substance in number, or if they are specific individuals differing only in number, such as *Unea* <note>Likely referring to *Usnea*, a moss or lichen used in "weapon salve" and sympathetic medicine.</note>, the fat or human blood of one man can Sympathize with another at a distance. A Magnet of one mine can affect the iron of another in a Sympathetic manner at a distance. And I have recited the reason for this thing, both radical and immediate, in the preceding pages: namely, because both natures belong to a single divine influence; that is, they proceed from Angelic rays, or irradiation emitted from one and the same star, whether fixed or erratic <note>A planet.</note>. For it has been said: there is no animal, vegetable, or mineral upon the earth or in the sea that does not have its own peculiar star in heaven, from which it draws its virtue and influence of life, vegetation, preservation, and multiplication. Now indeed, every Angelic nature has its appropriated rays from some emanation of the divine attributes, which is transferred into some one of the sacred stars, and which is poured out by the act of the Olympic spirits and imparted to the spiritual ministers subject to them in the elemental region: which stellar emanation then works in every specified individual...

Wherefore, as God sends out his emanation, of which the Angelic world is the image in a diversity of modes and a multiplicity of respects: so the Angelic spirits pour out their different and distinct lights to the lower orders, and every superior sphere to the lower ones, and thus from the stars, which also apply their lights to each other through various aspects, those things are rained down step by step into and upon the creatures even to the center of the earth: which creatures, according to the patterns of their stars, eject both **Sympathetic** and **Antipathetic** rays toward each other, albeit invisibly: Nor indeed ought we to doubt that such rays are concordant and discordant in lower things, since in the very source of unity, from which all things emanate, we observe an opposition of properties, namely a **privative Will** and a **positive Will**: and it is to be believed in no other way than that the passive spiritual matter of the soul of the world is that subject, by means of which and in which that divine unity, by abundantly pouring out loving and positive—that is, Sympathetic—passions and quickening rays of life, is accustomed to excite joys and delights with the fulfillment of the appetite of spiritual matter: so that it now holds its natural root, namely the mother, **Chaos** or the dark abyss, in oblivion, and is converted into the offspring or son of light through adoption: and therefore in this state it seems to participate and Sympathize with those golden showers of nourishing and quickening light, which are rained down from the beneficial attributes of God, and now it begins to hate and avoid with fear all those privative influences which are poured out from the severe, unhealthful, and destructive attributes of God: in no other way than we see light shrink from the sight of darkness and delight in the presence of its like, or as life is shaken with terror by death and good by the evil contrary to it. Hence, therefore, it comes to pass that the **children of light**, who are founded upon or grafted into the illuminated Universal spirit, flee from and avoid as a plague the **children of darkness**, and hold their works in horror and hatred.

Whence it happened that it immediately lost its light and beauty and, contrary to the common custom and laws of nature, was rendered dark and like black pitch; so that the pleasant **Sympathy** which it imparted to the lower creatures and even the celestial ones by its presence was, by such an accident, changed into **Antipathy** for a space of time. This, therefore, was a privative passion in the heart of the macrocosm, and a kind of syncope <note>fainting or loss of consciousness</note> of the same, when that most beautiful attribute of God, **Eloah** <note>A Hebrew name for God</note>, abstained for a time from the pouring out of his lucid effluences through the beautiful gate of **Tiphareth** <note>The sphere of Beauty in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life</note>. The other virtue in the vital spirit is involuntary, being that which is commanded and governed at the pleasure of the intellectual or rational ray: Not otherwise than the lower spheres are compelled to move according to the will of the first mover in the *Primum Mobile*. Thus, the vital action in man is a unique branch of those things which are involuntary and is subject to the mental will no differently than the starry heaven (which is the seat of life, inasmuch as the Sun, which is the heart of the world, has its residence therein) obeys the commands of the empyrean heaven.

Now indeed, as we find that according to the will of the divine essence infused into the celestial region (and consequently into the lower ones), the efflux or effect—whether lovely and delightful for exciting pleasures and joys in the creature—proceeds from the positive or dilatative <note>expanding</note> property of Unity; so do the sad and hateful effects proceed from the privative and contractive virtue of the same, in which God turns the face of his kindness away from the creature (and hence both concupiscible or **Sympathetic** passions and hateful and irascible or **Antipathetic** ones are produced in this world). So indeed, both by experience and by the observation of the most learned philosophers and physicians, we are taught that the vital action, which is governed according to the mind of the superior will, is either dilated by the dilatative will of the first mover and opens the sanctuary of the heart to produce those good passions in the vital spirit which **Sympathize** with life and light—namely hope, confidence, Love, mercy, and gentleness—or it is contracted, and by closing the chambers of the heart, gathers the spirits within it into one. # SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Part II.

<image-desc>An illustration of a monochord, a stringed instrument with a single string stretched over a graduated rule, with a tuning peg on the right and a weight or tensioning mechanism on the left. The string is marked with letters A, B, C, D, E, F, and numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.</image-desc>

Where string A <note>original: "chorda A"</note> of one monochord <term>monochord: a single-stringed instrument used by ancient and Renaissance scientists to measure musical intervals and mathematical proportions</term> is struck, it will produce a discord with the sound of string B, D, or F of another monochord; but if A is struck in one, it will harmonize with the portion of string C or E of the other. From this it is clear that, although both strings are of the same width, nevertheless, always in respect to their shortness or length, the air—observed in both proportion and disposition through rarefaction and condensation—is found to produce various voices upon them, both dissonant and consonant. For a shorter string of the same tension thins the air more by its greater and stronger vibration, and consequently renders a higher pitch. On the other hand, a longer string of the same tension, such as A, makes a deeper and shorter sound, because the air in such a soft motion is less rarefied, and consequently the voice is more heavy, deep, and as if suffocated by reason of the density of the air. Finally, whether in deep sounds or high or mixed, the proportion and weight of the air is the cause of Symphony <note>original: "Symphoniæ"; here meaning harmony</note> or antiphony <note>original: "antiphoniæ"; here meaning discord or opposition</note> by means of the act of the Universal Spirit <note>original: "spiritus... Catholici"</note> within it, which we compare to one blowing a pipe or striking a string; for without this, no voice, neither concordant nor discordant, is rendered in the said instruments. By which we conclude that the medium in which and through which the divine spirit acts both Sympathetically and Antipathetically in this world is the air or spirit, which acts in creatures no differently than the air in a pipe or any other musical instrument.

Therefore, so that I may proceed more methodically in this part of the book, I shall set forth only the principal foundation, upon which I will build several experimental conclusions. By these, I may direct and lead the incredulous—who until now, by reason of their ignorance, have remained rebellious and obstinate in their erroneous infidelity—to a more certain and secure port of faith. And since the acts of Sympathy, and also that Antipathy, are effected in every thing by Magnetic virtue and power (the nature of which is to resist by a visible and "irascible" expulsion) <column-break/> as well as to allure to itself by a "concupiscible" attraction (as will be said below), I deem it necessary and convenient that we inquire with diligence, and that with the eyes of Argus <note>Argus Panoptes, the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth, signifying all-seeing vigilance</note>. For the secret operation of the weapon salve <note>original: "unguenti armarij"; a controversial 17th-century medical theory where an ointment was applied to the weapon that caused a wound to heal the patient via sympathy</note>, which the ignorant worldlings have pursued with such hatred and reproach, as well as the method of extracting Mummy <note>original: "Mummiae"; a medicinal substance believed to contain the "vital breath" or spirit of a once-living body</note>, both bodily and spiritual, from men and beasts; and also the transplantation of the vital, unhealthy nature of an animal into some vegetable or the nature of another healthy animal, with the manner of succession, virtue, and strength of one animal and the infusion of the same into another; [and] the secret binding of the Spirit of some plant with that of a man or another animal: so that whatever happens to one, namely either moisture or dryness or heat or cold, the other will also participate in it; since, I say, things of this sort...

# ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY.

Operations of this kind are called **Magnetic**, insofar as they imitate the active virtues of the **Magnet** <note>The lodestone or magnet was a central metaphor in 17th-century "Mosaic" or "Chemical" philosophy for invisible attraction and spiritual influence.</note>; I shall strive with my utmost power and effort to open a way into the anatomy and revelation of all those mysteries. Namely, by the dissection of the **Magnet of the Spiritual Treasure**, I shall act so that, by this method, I may look into the source and foundations of the formal, interior, or central and essential action—or virtue—of both the irascible and the concupiscible passion <note>The "irascible" (anger/strength) and "concupiscible" (desire/lust) were the two primary divisions of the soul's passions in classical and medieval psychology.</note>. For if, by subtle reasoning, we can find the invisible channels and secret caves of the same through our intuition, and then afterwards observe the central point or essence of those essences, and finally detect the internal cause of any action, it would be very easy to overcome the rest. This is because those things which appear by external effect must necessarily be homogeneous—that is, of one and the same condition—with respect to their internal natures, as will be explained more broadly below.

But alas! Why do I presume—I, who am the least of the Apostles, or at least the least out of a thousand—to take a path or journey so dangerous to that unknown island where the hidden nature of the magnet dwells in the midst of inaccessible rocks full of peril? For so many wise **Philosophers** have sailed and wandered upon the uncertain and tempestuous seas of opinions, and finally, returning home, have reported only those new things concerning the mystery of that matter—namely, concerning the existence of the Magnet and the essence of its active virtues—which were predicted by others. Thus, they have nothing at all of their own, except what they have understood either by external operation or from the reports of others.

Good God! How many ships full of fools are there in this world, who, after they have spent many years in their studies and sciences, plowing the seas of vain and scarcely probable imagination, have returned in their old age to the harbor of childhood? They have their wits and understanding burdened with poor fragments or merchandise of "he himself said it" <note>original: "ipse dixit" - a reference to dogmatic appeals to authority, usually Aristotle, without personal proof.</note>, or the opinions of others. But concerning the central science of that secret, they have nothing of their own to say. Thus we Christians, after the pilgrimage of our life and our studies in this world, finally think it sufficient to assert that **Aristotle**, **Plato**, **Galen**, **Hippocrates**, or at least this or that man said this, and consequently, that it is certain and infallible. On the contrary, we perceive that the Scriptures teach us a truer and more certain Philosophy, which is most opposed to that of the Heathens. Therefore, worldly students of this kind are best pointed out by these words of the Apostle, namely, as those whom he describes as *always learning, but never arriving at the knowledge of the truth*. For, I ask you, how is it possible for the blind to lead the blind directly?

<margin>2 Timothy 3</margin> Others, steering their ship here and there for a long time and directing it toward the seat where the virtues of that stone dwell, have scarcely—if at all—reached the limits of its rocky island; and yet they have returned not without wonderful histories or reports collected from such a journey. And in the end, their new discoveries are found to be so superficial, and the effects of their scrutiny or inquiry so frivolous, that finally the whole is proven to be nothing but conjectural.

Others have been led so far in their inquiry by the allurements of the pole star that they have become firmly stuck with their ship in the icy sea, unable to progress further. But when the ice melted, they returned filled with wonderful imaginations about **Magnetic** mountains and iron castles, even reaching eight degrees above the moon up to the eighth sphere. Indeed, there are even others who fly above that starry place. From which one may conceive how any of the Philosophers, according to the laws of the **Chimera** of his own **Fantasy**, imagines phantasms—not only in the air, but even above the stars themselves—in order to find the magnetic soul.

There are some who, in the investigation of the same, do not depart from the continent of the earth, but think that the earth itself is to be numbered among the stars of heaven, having the sun as its fixed center, around which they are perpetually observed to move peripherally. Thus, they fashion the earth itself to have a stellar form, far differing from that **Peripatetic** <note>The Peripatetic school refers to the followers of Aristotle, who believed the earth was stationary at the center of the universe.</note> form. Finally, each of these has his own opinion differing from the other.

However, so that you may understand that all of this is true, I will recite to you in a few words some of the new things pertaining to such a **Magnetic** inquiry, after their long path of serious contemplation on the fluctuating sea. Among them, some who think more loftily in such an effort seem to invoke the heavens as witnesses to confirm their assertion; others tend even toward the Hyperborean mountains; others to strange Northern Islands to detect the foundation of such a great miracle. Others, plunging the spirits of their inquiry into the bowels of the earth, find that its entire form is stellar. Some wish that such a virtue occurs by way of an atomic emission from the body of the stone and the attractable object.

But among all others endowed with reason who have sailed in the ship of fools, I scarcely dare to count one who seems to be most similar to another **Grillus** <note>Likely a reference to a character representing a "swinish" or foolish person, or a specific obscure critic.</note>, insofar as he opined that the **Magnetic** virtue was **Cacomagical** <note>Evil magic or sorcery.</note> or an act of the **Devil**. And now, of those who have made a way with their spirit into heaven to find that mystery, one wishes that the reason for the direction of the Magnet is to be gathered from the tail of the constellation of the **Bear** <note>Ursa Major or Minor.</note>, affirming that this star in the Bear prevails and possesses dominion over that stone, and it is drawn toward the iron. This is the opinion of **Marsilio Ficino**...

# SECTION TWO. BOOK II. Member II.

<page-num>N</page-num>

...But I respond that the matter cannot be so, since experience testifies that iron of itself enjoys its own poles just as much as the lodestone <note>original: *magnetem*</note>, and as it desires, it seeks them out through proper adaptation; by its own natural instinct, it turns and directs itself into the proper station of its poles. Into this opinion of Marsilio Ficino <note>A famous 15th-century Italian Neoplatonist philosopher</note> also falls Peter Peregrinus, who, following the rules of Friar Bacon, investigated magnetic direction from the poles of the heavens. Even Cardano maintains that the immediate cause of the variation of this stone's powers arises from the star existing in the tail of the Great Bear <note>The constellation Ursa Major</note>. Lucas Gauricus also seems to agree with them in this matter, but he simultaneously adds to this business the power of Saturn and Mars, and even says the principal constellation in the Zodiac contributing to this, and to whose influences the stone itself is subjected, is Virgo. Albertus Magnus concludes that the lodestone itself and even the iron are directed toward the Pole Star, and says they follow it no differently than the Heliotrope herb <note>The sunflower or turnsole</note> follows the sun. Beifardus made his own opinion of this stone differ from others, indeed thinking that the pole of the Zodiac is the source of magnetic power. Again, the College of Coimbra <note>A Jesuit center of learning in Portugal</note> places the cause of this thing in some part of the heavens not far distant from the Pole.

But truly, Martin Cortes thinks that this attractive power descends from a place beyond the poles or the moving heavens. On the other hand, Gaudentius Merula seems to assert that the lodestone draws iron to itself with the intention of directing it to the North Pole, because it is of a higher order than iron, associated with the constellation of the Bear. I confess, therefore, that the rays which are spread out to redeem their captive brothers <note>A metaphorical reference to the "trapped" magnetic spirits in iron</note> and restore their liberty to them, and to direct them to their own fatherland, are most useful and inclined by brotherly piety. But I cannot understand the sayings of Merula in this sense. Others think the heavens in general are the origin of that stone's power: For Paracelsus says there are stars which, being full of magnetic power, will attract iron to themselves, etc. And this opinion would seem probable, since iron moves to its poles even in the absence of a lodestone (as has been said). Fernelius seems to hesitate, at one moment confessing the cause of this action is hidden, and at another—namely elsewhere—making the heavens the causes of this action. Scaliger, approaching closer to the point of truth, assigns to this action or power a certain celestial cause entirely unknown to him, asserting that the terrestrial lodestone is not derived from stellar globes or mountains, but from that essential power or essence which was their maker, which governs in that portion of heaven that hangs at the northern point. And Plato seems to adhere to this opinion, as one who seems to recognize that the magnetic essence is a divine power. And indeed they speak well in this matter, but in a sense so broad that their assertion, well considered in itself, appears to their disciples like explaining the unknown by the more unknown <note>original: *ignotum per ignotius*</note>. For we can affirm in such general terms that all things are from God.

But we shall now descend from their celestial speculation and look to the humility of those who, being more cautious in what they see and attending to that old proverb **"Be not high-minded"** <note>original: *Noli altum sapere* - a Latin Vulgate reference to Romans 11:20, warning against intellectual pride</note>, look more downward, since they respect only the earth and its effects. And of this series is Fracastoro, who, inquiring into the reason and original cause of the attractive magnetic power, imagines that the Hyperborean Mountains <note>Mythical mountains in the far north</note>, which abound in cliffs of this stone, attract iron subjects of this kind to themselves. And this fiction of his seems so plausible and agreeable to reason to certain learned men that they follow it both in their astronomical writings and geographical tables, and in descriptions of the world and sea charts. Which, nevertheless, if it were true, would more easily draw ships passing in the Northern Sea toward them by attraction. Olaus Magnus, and several others who uphold his tradition, will have it that an attractive force of this kind proceeds from certain northern islands which abound in such magnetic material. But committing these fantasies of theirs to the empty wind, we proceed to the opinions of others in this matter.

Lucretius Carus, a certain poet of the Epicurean sect, seems to dream that the attraction of iron proceeds from an efflux of atoms from the subject: For just as (he says) according to the opinion of the Epicureans, subtle atoms emanate from any thing, so likewise atoms, like magnetic seeds, are emitted from iron through a certain union of itself with the lodestone into the interposed place or space between them; and through the union or entanglement of both bodies, the iron is attracted, etc. Toward this opinion, Alexander of Aphrodisias, Johannes Costeus, Plutarch, and even Thomas Aquinas are observed to incline. When in truth they ought to know that no attraction is made by emission from the center to the circumference—that is, by dilation and dissipation—but on the contrary by attraction and introduction from the circumference to the center, just as we see in a syringe <note>original: *syringa*</note>, by whose attraction water is drawn into its cavity by the drawing out of its plunger, and is emitted from the moving hand as if from a center, etc. Wherefore it follows that the emission of rays or atomic seeds from the iron cannot be the cause of its union or motion to the stone, but it must necessarily be the lodestone which has the faculty of attracting the rays or spirits out of the iron: For it appears evidently that iron does not attract itself to the stone, but is [attracted] by it.

<margin>f. page 147.</margin> Whence the royal Psalmist says: *He sends forth snow like wool and scatters frost like ashes; who can stand before his cold?* <note>Psalm 147:16-17</note> It is clear, therefore, that there is a contractive and coagulating act of **Jehovah** in the property of his name **Elohim**, who immediately governs these things through his Northern organs: first the Angelic, then the stellar through the angelic (inasmuch as they are animated by the Angelic), and finally the windy and Elemental organs, which are animated by stellar influences and led by lower angels. Thus, the essence of all things acting centrally is nothing but the one in God **Jehovah**, and from Him, who is unique in essence and is expressed solely by the essential name **Jehovah**, yet in respect to the variety of properties, is distributed into many branches according to the varying will of the one divine essence. And every branch, illuminating itself, divides into many formal shoots or various rays, and these into infinite actions not differing from the property of the capital or radical emanation. For example: the influence descending from **Elohim** falls into the sphere of **Saturn**, under whose dominion are infinite creatures: namely those which from their first creation are subjected to its influences, just as earthly things are imbued with its condition—namely cold, dry, woody, attractive, retentive, etc. But leaving this Cabalistic and Astrological path of proof, I shall now descend to such testimonies as **Sacred Philosophy** has granted me.

In the preceding sections, I related that the eternal unity, in an eternally one essence, dividing or transforming itself ideally into a **Triunity** through its property, shaped or described the **Archetypal** or internal world. According to this pattern, He then necessarily fabricated the typical or external world to come into existence. Whence it must follow that if the typical natural world were in the image of the Idea of the internal or mental world, then whatever parts and properties are manifested to our capacity in this world were also the same in the Archetype. For that which makes a thing such, is itself more so. There was no house which the Architect intended to build that was not first ideally sketched in the mind of the builder, then afterwards depicted upon paper, and finally actually built from stones or bricks and wood. So also **David** confesses that he had the temple, which **Solomon** afterwards constructed, ideally depicted by the finger of God. Now truly, since God in His secret counsel had in this manner sketched and ordered the **Ideal world** in Himself, so that He might compare that spiritual world explicitly and realistically to human sense, He sent Himself forth from Himself—no division of His essence being made meanwhile—in the form of an eternal emanation (which was called His image and wisdom). By means of this, this general world, with every one of its particles, was fabricated according to the effigy or ideal pattern which was in Him. Since this is so, and since the divine essence cannot in any respect be divided into parts, however much it seems to vary in property, it follows that every particular ray which is sent forth in various forms from this **Universal** <note>original: "Catholica"</note> emanation for the creation of various things, is one and indivisible with the radical emanation of the essence. And <margin>Wisdom 12.</margin> hence it is said by the Apostle and **Solomon** that He fills all things, and is all in all, and exists incorruptibly in every thing, and fills the orb of the earth. I proceed, therefore, in this way: If the created world has its effigy and its members and all its particular properties from the formal and vivifying world, which was ideally sketched or described in that divine and all-informing and creating emanation or spirit of wisdom; then consequently all the members, properties, and natures of this world are graphically and admirably described in the supernatural world, while it nonetheless remains one and the same in essence. And therefore, just as the Universal image of the eternal world is contained in it, so every ray or irradiation which goes out indivisibly from it contains in itself a figure of this kind. And for this reason, the wise **Philosophers** said that every creature possesses a certain proportion of the **Greater World** <note>The Macrocosm</note>, through which it is made a **Little World** <note>The Microcosm</note> in itself, as will be shown. And again, **Man** is called "every creature" insofar as he participates in all things, so that his soul is handed down as being made in the image of wisdom, of all—

Thales and Anaxagoras believe that the Magnet possesses its own life within itself, since it is observed to attract a substance similar to itself, not otherwise than living creatures do. It is his mind that this Magnetic or attractive force in the Magnet proceeds from formal actions, that is, from original and primary virtues or vigors: for he concludes that the magnetic virtue is derived from a peculiar or singular form, differing from that specific form or cause in mixed bodies mentioned by the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle.</note>. And he says there is a certain form which is proper to the stellar globes and their parts, a homogeneous or incorruptible essence or entity, which he calls the primary, radical, and astral form, namely such as is in the sun, Moon, and other celestial stars. And he also says, in a similar manner, that there is a "star" in the earth, which is that true magnetic power called the first act or vigor; and he concludes that this form is not derived from the whole heaven, and affirms it is not procreated by influence or occult qualities, nor even from any particular star: For the Magnet has its virtues from the earth, etc. 

This was the opinion of my once most learned colleague concerning the magnetic act; whose labors and industry in the diligent investigation of Magnetic nature, as I cannot but highly commend, so on the other hand, reason does not permit me to entirely stand by his speculative foundation or root in this matter. For who can believe that the earth, much less its particular parts, can have any radical virtue from themselves, when it is evident that both the earth and the heaven arose first from the waters? And therefore, as the heaven was before the earth, it must necessarily follow that the formal virtue of the earth descends totally from the heaven, and consequently the earth did not have such a property from itself, but from that spirit which created it, as will be more clearly explained below. 

Among the Heathen Philosophers, Plato, and among the Christians, Scaliger and Fernelius believe the cause of that attraction to be divine and from above, but how, or by what reason it descends, they do not even express. And therefore, although in generality they have spoken nothing but the truth, yet in words so expanded they seem to express nothing in particular. I will conclude now with the last opinion, which is of all the most vain and ridiculous: Franciscus Rucus seems to doubt the virtue of the magnet: for he does not hesitate to think all effects of this kind, as being beyond his grasp, to be "cacomagical" <note>Evil magic; from the Greek *kakos* (evil) and *magia* (magic).</note>, that is, derived from the imposture and subtle delusion of a Cacodemon or the Devil. And yet this man is more tolerable than those scrupulous men who do not blush to boldly assert that the admirable act in the "weapon salve" <note>A medicinal ointment believed to heal a wound by being applied to the weapon that caused it, a major point of controversy in 17th-century science.</note> is absolutely Diabolical and cacomagical: for this man does not speak as they do, determinately and without further risk of doubt, but only doubtfully.

Hence it is that the Northern wind affects the Northern world with cold, frost, ice, snow, and hail: for that which makes a thing such, is itself more such: But that star by its influx and breath contracts, freezes, coagulates, thickens, and retains...

Al-Kindi <note>Al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD), a famous Arab philosopher and scientist known as the "Philosopher of the Arabs."</note>, in the Astrological manner, discourses thus: "If it were granted to anyone to comprehend the entire condition of the celestial harmony, he would fully know the world of elements with each of its contents in any place and at any time, just as an effect is known through its causes. If he also knew any single thing of this world in its entire condition, the condition of the celestial harmony itself would not be hidden from him, but he would even comprehend the cause, as if through its effect. For every thing, however small, acting in the world of elements, is an effect of the whole celestial Harmony." These are his words. By which words this man, who seems deeply versed in the mysteries of nature, asserts that, just as there is a descent from unity into multiplicity, so indeed that multiplicity is unfolded implicitly in the radical unity, so that even this unity fills every multiplicity. By this reasoning, unity (or 1) is in 2, and 2 in 3, and 3 in 4, and 4 in 5, etc. And yet that unity, which is the beginning, is also the end and the middle and the "all in all" of any number whatsoever. In this same way, light informs the Angelic creature, the Angelic informs the stellar, the stellar informs the Elemental, and the Elemental informs the composite creature. But there is always only one unique and indivisible light which acts centrally and works in all of these. Therefore, let the composite creature be opened and the Elements inspected; let them be divided from the pure, and we shall find the stellar nature or the <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence," a refined substance beyond the four earthly elements (earth, air, fire, water).</note>. And if that stellar substance be opened, we shall perceive that subtle "otherness" of the Angelic nature, in which consists the divine act or the immediate ray from God. In this work, therefore, there concurs a separation of the former sensible aspect from the latter intellectual intuition: so that you may be able to observe how all things are in any one thing, and any one thing is in every thing. And hence Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the Hermetic corpus is attributed.</note>, speaking Mystically and not according to common sense, says: *He who does not build the furnace according to our cunning, melts down a new world.* But what need is there for more words, when we find all of this to be true by ocular demonstration? For we know that the Magnet is nothing but a small portion of general iron, and yet it comprehends in itself all the circles of heaven and earth with both their poles; indeed, it even contains that very nature in every respect between the two poles and circles which the general earth possesses, whence it is called by some a *Terella*, as if a "minimal earth." And so also the whole earth can be called a "small world" <note>Microcosm.</note>, insofar as it has in itself two poles, circles, and even the astral and elemental natures of the great world <note>Macrocosm.</note>, no differently than the great world in all these respects re-

# ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY.

<note>The author is likely Robert Fludd, discussing how God shapes the physical world through spiritual "breaths" or winds.</note>
He alters one form into another through the spirit of his nostrils (as the Scriptures say, speaking in an Allegorical manner) or through those windy emissions or Angelic emanations, which he sends forth from nearly the four Corners. Thus, by means of his spirit from the Northern region or Corner, he exercises his attractive, contractive, retentive, and aggregative property, by which he flees and contracts from the circumference to the center, and thus congeals, coagulates, thickens, hardens, and fixes soft spirits through the contraction of those parts which were previously porous and dilated. But some will perhaps reply and say: How is it probable that such an emanation or emission of spirits from the gate of *Binah* <note>The Hebrew Sephirot representing "Understanding" or the feminine principle of contraction.</note> under the name *Elohim*, or the irradiation or emission of spirit from the North and its two collateral winds, can harden soft things through contraction, or suck toward itself and introduce spirits from the circumference to the center, since their emissions are directed from the North toward the South, and make no reflection by which any such contraction from the circumference to the center might occur? I answer, that this is performed in a wonderful manner to be observed by the more select intellects. We ought, therefore, in the first order, to consider the property of the attribute *Binah*, over which the name *Elohim* presides, to be ordained before every beginning, so that it might put on the negative or contractive nature of the Will or the darkness of the eternal unity. For, when God does not wish to emit the light of his countenance, he reflects the heat and power of his light back into himself (to use the words of Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with alchemy and hermetic philosophy.</note>, which do not differ from the sacred scriptures in this matter); that is, he contracts from the circumference into the center, and by this reasoning the creature is deprived of light and life. Thus the property of God is Antipathetic <note>Opposed in nature; a term from natural magic and early science.</note> to those parts of the world, and also to creatures, which have life from natural heat, which derives its beginning from the benevolent act and emanation of God, in which he emitted his will or positive power from himself—that is, from unity to multiplicity, as if from the center toward the circumference or the creatures. It follows, therefore, that although the emission of winds from the North is direct, nevertheless their essential property, proceeding immediately from the Angelic organs of God, is contractive and attractive from the circumference to the center, insofar as it is an emanation which, through the animation of the divine spirit and action in the nature of *Elohim*, renders things cold, dry, coagulative, congealing, and disposed to rest; and therefore it is Antipathetic and opposing to the disposition of the air, which is indeed hot and moist and consequently animated by that dilating act which the Universal Spirit breathes out. For this reason it happens that, when Northern spirits are emitted into the air, it must necessarily follow that at the Antipathetic contact of those cold spirits, the natural heat or life of the air flees and contracts itself from its circumference toward the center; and thus the air—partly through that contractive motion in itself from the ancient state, and through the mixing of the form made by the terrestrial *antiperistasis* <note>A philosophical concept where one quality is heightened by being surrounded by its opposite, e.g., internal heat increasing when surrounded by cold.</note> or the concourse of its contraction—is congealed with it, and is precipitated to the earth as if dead and immobile in the form of snow, hail, frost, or ice. The retrograde motion of the warm life of the air from the circumference to the center through the vehement contact of Northern cold is clearly declared by an experiment of this kind: For, if you desire the best spirit of wine <note>Alcohol or ethanol.</note> extracted without fire, let a jar full of wine be exposed to the open air while the greatest inclemency of cold and Northern winds urges in the sky, and unbearable frost and ice severely rage on the earth and waters; and within a few days you will find the outer part of the wine constrained by ice, but if you wish to pierce the center, you will see the best spirit of wine flow out. By which it is evident that the life of the wine, at the contact of the most vehement cold, flees from the circumference to the center of its body, as if to a place more remote from the seats and dominion of the cold. In a similar way, one may also see the aerial life in other creatures—whose formal existence consists in the dilating property of God—forced by the inclemency of cold to fly from the circumference to the center, leaving the exterior parts frozen, rigid, and subject to the coagulation of dead and Lethal rest. This we observe not only in animal creatures, but also in vegetables, when their blood (so to speak) or sap in winter time, shrinking from the Northern cold, is congealed in their center, so that they seem as if dead, until the spring Sun vivifies their spirits—which were slumbering in the center, resting and as if dead (by dissolving the Northern knot)—and calls them forth to the circumference, where they may again exercise their vital and vegetative function. For this reason, therefore, it is clear that in the truth of the matter there is but one Universal Element, which is partly subjected to the privative, dark, and consequently contractive property of God, and is partly capable of putting on his positive, lucid, and dilating disposition. And it is evident that this common subject is the spirit or air of the sublunary world, which is reduced into water by a lesser thickening or contraction made by the Western winds, but into a terrestrial nature by a greater compression and constriction made by the Northern winds; on the contrary, by a lesser dilation and rarefaction made by the southern winds, it becomes vapor or smoky air, and by a still greater rarefaction and subtilization from the dominion of the Eastern winds—especially in summer time—fire or lightning is produced, as was related before. And both these multiform properties lead to one and the same...

But, to return to the marrow of our proposal, it is manifest from what has been said that the Northern spirit <note>original: *spiritum Borealem*</note> is contractive, attractive, thickening <note>original: *inspissativum*</note>, and prone toward darkness, immobility, and rest; and the Southern spirit, or rather the wind blowing from the equinox, is contrary to it in nature, insofar as it is prepared to destroy those effects which the Northern winds have produced—namely, to resolve frozen air, and snow, frost, hail, and ice into water, and to refine water into air, and to make the opaque transparent, and the dense subtle. Therefore, between these opposite properties, no more sympathy is found than I have demonstrated above to exist between the equator of a Magnet and its Pole, which cannot agree with one another. And again, that both these opposite natures proceed from one and the same divinity or essential Catholic spirit <note>The "Catholic spirit" here refers to the universal or all-pervading spirit of the world, from the Greek *katholikos* meaning universal.</note>, whose work it is to operate all things in all places, and consequently to confirm this testimony of true Philosophy as much on earth as in the heavens. For when God sends forth (says the Text) his word to the earth, it runs most swiftly; he who sends forth snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes, casts down ice like morsels; who can stand before his cold? He sends forth his word and melts them; as soon as he breathes his wind, the waters flow, etc. <note>A translation of Psalm 147:15-18.</note> By which it is manifest that the same word or spirit of God freezes by one property and dissolves by another; and consequently, as God is one in essence, so indeed is the same spirit which effects these fourfold alterations in the single mundane spirit—which the ancients called distinct Elements, because until this day they have not been able to determine what the essential form of the Elements might be.

But, if they had well considered the four Elements, about which they have made so many words, yet (as it seems) understood them with so little essentiality, they would have rightly perceived that the heaven and the earth were first created out of water and through water, consisting by the word of God, as sacred Philosophy teaches us <margin>P. 147.</margin> <margin>2 Peter 3.</margin>; then, without doubt, their common substance was nothing but a single created spirit, brought into light by the mediation of the divine spirit. And also, that the fourfold informing of that substance was effected by a single uncreated essence, which informs this Catholic Element in a manifold way by a fourfold emanation (as we have often proved), so that the will of the one creating spirit, effected through and operating in the four Angels of opposite natures, makes, disposes, and daily alters this spiritual watery subject into this or that state, in which, according to the nature of the subject, they seem to distinguish it by the name of this or that element—all of which is evidently proved by the demonstration of our experimental instrument <note>Likely referring to a weather glass or early thermoscope.</note>. For the air included in it, either by contraction or by dilation, converts itself into the form of any Element, and in its prison or receptacle is altered according to the natures of the winds reigning at various times in the Macrocosmic air.

Now indeed, just as it may be asked whence the earth and waters (which reside perpetually here below and hold the place of elements) derive their origin: I answer that they are effects which the winds originally produced from the waters, God or the *Ruach-Elohim* <note>Hebrew: Spirit of God</note> so willing; and these effects were derived first from the air or invisible waters, by thickening them by one degree into visible water, and by thickening that through another degree into a more gross, solid, and fixed substance, namely dry earth, as is declared from the doctrine of Moses. For the Apostle and sacred Philosopher seems to verify this where he says: It is to be believed through faith that those things which are visible were first made from things invisible. And again, if the two lower bodies did not resolve themselves little by little and step by step into air, though not unproductively, it would be impossible for the earth or water to give such a quantity of rain water, stones, sulfur, and other such solid and sensible things which daily fall from the sky or air, and that without the increase of the water or sea, or the diminution of the air; indeed, they are always found in the same natural proportion of magnitude. Whence the wise man said: all rivers enter into the sea, and the sea does not overflow, etc.
