But truly, attraction in <margin>Magnets</margin> happens far differently: For the magnet itself, clothed in the natural virtue of its "earthly death" <note>referring to the inert, mineral state of the stone</note> and possessing within itself the essence of the North Star <note>original: "stellæ Borealis"</note>, which is of the nature of Saturn and Venus: greedily and with no small concupiscence and desire, it draws the masculine spirits of sulfur out of the iron to itself and strongly retains them. This attraction does not happen in the same way as that **Antipathetic** attraction, which is absolutely from the circumference to the center; namely, when a thing, as if struck by fear, contracts the rays of its life into the center so that it might decline from those adversaries moving about its circumference and hide itself—that is, not so that it might be joined with its like, but so that it might be separated from its contrary.

Magnetic attraction, I say, behaves differently: For, whereas in Antipathetic attraction there is an angry separation from the rays of the beholding enemy, and an exact contraction from the outside to the inside without any attraction (or rather with a certain expulsion of the pursuer or onlooker); so, on the contrary, in this kind of Magnetic attraction, there occurs an emission of rays from the center beyond its own circumference, as if congratulating the arrival of a friend. Whence it embraces its like even beyond the dimension of its own body, and is courteously received by its like in a reciprocal manner, and finally draws it to its own lodging—not to pursue it with hatred, but to affect it with friendship and natural joy, and to make it glad, according to that saying of the <margin>Empedocles.</margin> Philosopher <note>referring to Empedocles</note>: *Nature rejoices and delights in nature.* Whence it happens that in this kind of motion, its spirits do not recede or contract from the circumference to the center, but remain cheerfully without fear with their friend and move about the circumference.

I cannot indeed better describe the meeting or embrace of these two than by the example of a certain singular friend who [awaits] an absent friend; whom, as soon as the master of the palace perceives him coming from afar while looking out from the gate, he suddenly goes out, receives him kindly, and leads him by the hand to his house; or, if a woman meets her husband, long absent, likewise on the road, and receives him to herself with many preceding embraces.

But if that love of the Magnet be for the sake of its nourishment (for they say the Magnet is nourished, strengthened, and animated by iron filings), then indeed I can not inaptly compare the spirits in the Magnet and their motion to a spider, whose home is a certain cave in a corner of its web; once a fly is caught in its net, the spider suddenly and with joy comes out, seizes the fly, and carries it to its domicile so that it may be refreshed by its body. Thus, you see even here there is a certain **Sympathy** between the spirit of the fly and that of the spider: For otherwise, such great concupiscence would not affect the essence of the fly, which was without doubt similar to it in nature. But this cannot be so properly held as Sympathy.

On the other hand, the Antipathetic attraction or contraction, which is usually done partly in anger and partly by the approach of fear, I might not foolishly compare to a tortoise and a snail, which are animal-like <insert>creatures</insert>; where no danger or harm is present, they put forth their heads and the snail its horns from the shell, just as a worm emerges in part from the earth after rain, delighted by the solar heat. But if either the tortoise, the snail, or the worm sees someone to be feared, or someone invading it, they suddenly contract themselves into themselves and hide in their houses. The matter is no different with spirits affected by **Antipathy**: for they do not draw contrary spirits to themselves, but they "attract" by contracting themselves into themselves from the sight of the outside to the inside.

But leaving aside the opinions of those who believe that this attraction of the Magnet is for the sake of its nourishment rather than Sympathetic love, we incline toward those who hold to their sympathetic embrace. For since it is certain that both iron and the Magnet are extracted from the same mine, vein, and nature—for both are of an earthly and Northern <note>original: "Borealis"</note> disposition—and since the Magnet and its formal spirits are more adorned and burdened with superfluities than iron examined and purified by fire, they attempt to draw their like from the purified iron or steel with great appetite, so that they might better be liberated from such a burden by their assistance. In such an action, they allure the iron to themselves (which, as if unwilling to leave its formal spirits, [follows] the motion of its formal rays through a certain natural continuity) and bring some refreshment; not otherwise than feminine matter allures and desires the formal male, so that it may be refreshed by his masculine seed and sulfurous form—which form they both originally received from the Northern nature of the Ideal Catholic Agent <note>The "Catholic Agent" refers to a universal creative force or spirit</note>, who sustains and animates the earth as Job testifies.

I will prove this same thing by another similitude, but from the vegetable kingdom. We observe that a grain of wheat, not participating with the nature of the earth—that is, as long as it is above the earth and not sown in the earth—cannot attract its like from heaven by which it might be multiplied. But after it is committed to the matrix of the earth, or buried in the ground, and the earth has dissolved the bonds of its composition through corruption, and has liberated the spirits caught in this way, then the spirits begin to allure to themselves and draw downward to themselves the solar rays and the influences of their constellation (both fixed and wandering), so that by their help they may be entirely liberated from their **Elemental** <term>Elementatibus: pertaining to the four physical elements</term> bonds, and by the mediation of such rays of their nature sent from heaven, they may be raised upward and, as it were, re-ascend into their fatherland. Thus, like added to like is made stronger in its ascent: For we are taught by experience that the celestial form or **vital ray** <note>original: "radius vitalis"</note> included [within] step by step...

And therefore those Philosophers are deceived who deny that the **Magnet** is nourished in an occult manner by the formal spirits of iron, and who say that, although they found its virtue increased by its immersion or burial in iron filings, yet because the iron was not diminished in its weight, they conclude it is not nourished. And finally, we find their mixture is effected in this manner: The Mercurial liquor, being of a stony, earthy, or Saturnine nature still in its first matter and as if in a shell, and being a close neighbor to the Mercury of Mars—for these two natures are commonly found near one another in the same vein of the earth, or in society with each other—has acquired a slight transmutation for that reason. And so these two natures appear acted upon together as contiguous things, so that this composition is a medium between the nature of the **Martial metal** <note>Iron</note> and the **Saturnine stone**, and not inaptly is it a species of Mercury transmuted in an imperfect way, or a species of **Saturnine Hermaphroditic Mercury**. Now truly, since every spirit—and consequently that of the magnetic stone—desires to be greedily nourished by that which is most similar to it in nature (which nourishment or nourishing spirit is chiefly found in iron <note>original: "farre", likely a typo for "ferro"</note>), it happens for this cause that the internal Martial spirit in the Magnet attracts iron to itself, and in a certain hidden way is seen to suck and entice nourishment from it to itself. I conceive, therefore, that the fixed salt in iron or the Magnet is partly from a hot and dry Martial nature and therefore of a fiery, earthy condition; and partly from a cold and dry, styptic and Saturnine faculty, which it also receives from the earth. Thus, two testimonies of wonderful attraction concur in the Magnet. Truly, if we look more closely into the internal nature of iron or steel, we shall elicit all of this more effectively: For by a certain familiar solvent <note>term: "menstruo" - a chemical solvent used to dissolve solids</note> I have reduced the body of iron or steel into a species of **Copperas** or **Vitriol**, which mineral salt nature is as familiar to copper as it is to iron: For Vitriol is extracted from copper by the same method. From this it is clear that the Martial and Saturnine, as well as the Venereal condition, concur in the magnetic and ferruginous salt.

Furthermore, we shall find that the influences of Mars naturally mix themselves with the **Northern winds**, and agree very well with the nature of the earth. Since in the circulation of the elements, the earth, in respect to its dryness, agrees and sympathizes with the waters. Moreover, **Ptolemy** ascribes those North winds, which are violent, to the influences of Mars. Furthermore, that the Martial spirit is the cause of the attractive virtue in any ferrous salt and also in herbs and gums, appears clearly from **Euphorbium**, **Chamomile**, **Spurge**, **Spearwort**, and hot corrosive poisons: For such simples (as **Hermes** teaches us) are subject to the power and constellation of Mars. Hence experience testifies that vitriol is cold, acid, and styptic in its exterior, and yet hot, caustic, and corrosive in its interior: And again Iron, which is called **Mars**, insofar as it is subject to the influences of Mars, is vitriol or Copperas in its interior, just as copper is known to obey the influences of Venus, whence it is also called **Venus**.

### CHAPTER III.
*On the excellence of man in the animal kingdom and on the admirable nature of the Magnet in the mineral kingdom.*

I shall boldly, and not inaptly, compare the condition of the **Magnet** with that of **man**, by considering the admirable virtues and dignity of the one in the animal kingdom and the miraculous and mystical properties and operations of the other in the mineral kingdom. As for what pertains to man, I shall make mention of him in the first place for the sake of his dignity: A treasure so supereminent and admirable is hidden within him, that the wise have judged the highest wisdom of this world to consist in the true knowledge of oneself—that is, in the revelation of that secret mystery which lies hidden in man. For man is said to be the center of every creature and the center and miracle of the world, comprehending in himself the properties of all creatures, both celestial and terrestrial, and consequently of the Magnet itself, whence he is also called the **Microcosm** <note>original: "Microcosmes" - the 'little world' that mirrors the universe</note>: he is also called the Temple...

## SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Part II.

...the temple of God, a member of Christ, and a dwelling place of the Holy Spirit (as we are taught by the Apostle); nor indeed should it be imagined that God wished for Himself a dwelling in a place unworthy of consideration. In the investigation of a secret matter of such great importance, we have need, with our most exact discretion and judgment, to proceed from the visible things in man to his invisible things. That is, with the sharper edge of our intellect, by way of a demonstration *from the effect* <note>original: "a posteriori" - reasoning from observed facts back to causes</note>, we must penetrate from the external man into the secret, mystical, and internal organs of his existence. Therefore, we proceed in this manner: Since man is handed down by Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with alchemy and philosophy</note>—not without justice—as being the "son of the world," just as he called the world itself the "son of God," insofar as it is fashioned after the image of the Archetype; and for that reason he is called the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: "Little World," the idea that man contains the entire universe in miniature</term>; it will be worth the effort to understand that he himself, in the manner of the **Macrocosm** <term>Macrocosm: "Great World," the universe as a whole</term>, is divided into heaven and earth. Consequently, he contains within himself his own circles, heavens, poles, and stars in a proportion fitting to him, no differently than the Macrocosm. And also, as we find, the spiritual icons of the heavens with their circles and poles are delineated even in the earth of the Macrocosm and in every particle of it—just as can be seen in the Magnet and in iron. In this way, the Character of the internal man is delineated and expressed in the external man: no differently than we can judge the shape of a sword from the proportion of its scabbard, or the likeness of a kernel from its husk.

Regarding the discovery of the worldly poles in man, no small controversy has arisen among the Philosophers. Plato, Pythagoras, and Aristotle assigned the right hand of man to the eastern region. Their reasoning is that the diurnal motion of the heavens, which proceeds from the *first movable* <note>original: "primo mobili" - the outermost sphere of the universe in Ptolemaic astronomy</note>, is carried out from east to west; and therefore, by this reasoning of theirs, his western region ought to correspond to the left, and in arranging man according to that position, his face ought to look toward the North, and his back toward the South. And Empedocles seems to oppose this opinion, asserting that the Summer Solstice or the **Tropic of Cancer** is assigned to the right part of the world; and then it follows that the station of the winter sun or the **Tropic of Capricorn** is dedicated to the left. According to that direction, the human face ought to look toward the West.

But the sentiment of my mind is entirely opposed to these opinions of theirs. Because I am persuaded, as much by Theological reasons as by those collected from the sacred scriptures, that the human face ought to be adapted by its natural position to the rising of the sun or the eastern region; then his back will look toward the west, and consequently his left hand will indicate the North Pole, and his right the South. This position is proved first by sacred testimony: For the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles, in their greater devotion, turned their faces toward the east. This was indeed an argument that that region of the world was divinely dedicated to the anterior part of man. Furthermore, we read in the <margin>Mark, 1.</margin> Evangelist that the lightning comes out from the East and passes into the West. And elsewhere it is said: Measure toward the <margin>Numbers.</margin> Eastern region, and toward the Southern region, and toward the Western region, and toward the Northern region, etc. As if he had said: Measure the fields before you, and to your right, and behind your back, and to your left. And in Job we find: "If I go to the East, he is not apparent; if to the West, I shall not perceive him; if to the left, what shall I do? <margin>Job, 23:1.</margin> I shall not apprehend him; if I turn myself to the right, I shall not see him." Or, as Franciscus Vatablus and Pagninus interpret it: "If I turn myself to the North while he is working, I will not see; he hides himself in the South, and I shall not see." But Tremellius interprets it thus: "Behold, if I go forward, he will not be there; but if backward, I will not notice him: when he acts to the left, yet I will not see; he covers the southern region, yet I will not look," etc. Thus, what Pagninus makes the "East" of the world, Tremellius calls the "face" or the "anterior part" of the world, etc.

From which, without further controversy, I believe it will appear that the direct disposition of man according to the situation of the greater world is such that his face is adapted to the eastern corner of the earth. For this reason, his two eyes—and also those of other creatures—are disposed in the frontispiece of his fabric, so that after the long darkness of the night, they may look upon the Eastern sun with delight and desire, so that in its presence they might richly adore the Creator dwelling therein. In its golden aspect, it is the master of the dark night to expel it, and consequently to greet it as a type of the eternal and invisible sun, which also (as the scriptures teach us) will appear on the last day from the east to renew and purify the corruptible world with fire. It follows, therefore, that the right part of man ought to look toward the South, so that his left portion looks toward the north. ## CHAPTER V. IV.

### ->On the dual attractive disposition in man, of which one agrees with the nature of the Magnet, while the other differs from it; in this chapter also, the reason why the corpse of a dead man is endowed with Magnetic or attractive power is clearly explained.<-

Just as in the dimension of the Magnet many species or modes of attracting are observed (for its attractive faculty is affected differently around its poles—namely, perpendicularly—than at its equator, which draws iron to itself in a prone and prostrate manner), so also a great difference is found between the effects of that attractive power found in man. For the spleen, having the nature and property of the North Pole <note>original: "Borealis Poli"</note>, directly attracts its like—namely, Melancholic and earthy juices—by a power that is, as it were, Saturnine. But the gallbladder receives its faculty of attracting from a Martial, Sulphurous, or fiery-earthy property; and the liver, by a southern or equinoctial dilation, disperses and pours the blood (which it previously made red) through the entire Microcosmic earth <note>The human body</note> by means of the venous channels. 

But in the first place, it attracts the chylous substance of food from the intestines through porous organs; it would never exercise all these faculties of attracting and expanding unless it were animated for that work by the incitements of natural heat. And, although that heat by its nature dissipates more by dilating than it contracts by attracting, it nevertheless incites and animates certain bodily instruments which are ordained by nature to perform such work—namely, to suck and allure to themselves through contraction, and again to dilate themselves through relaxation. And for this reason the Heart, Stomach, intestines, veins, etc., are formed and compacted of direct fibers for the sake of attraction, transverse fibers for the sake of retention, and oblique fibers for the sake of expulsion. 

Furthermore, the attraction of air through the windpipe <note>original: "asperam arteriam"</note> and nostrils could not be perfected without the help and aid of the lungs, which could by no means work or move without the animation and incitement of dilating and vivifying heat. Thus, in this case, all attraction of external air—which occurs through the pores into the fleshy parts, and through the lungs into the Left Chamber of the heart—proceeds immediately from the dilative action of natural heat and is perfected by means of instruments, especially through the lungs and heart. It is no different than what we see with a Syringe or pipe: if its internal part is pulled out, it draws little air or water to itself; but if I push that internal part back in, it emits or expels it. 

<column-break/>

But, to return to the direct path of this discourse: yet both of these opposite natures in a single instrument proceed from a single expanded human Spirit which operates them. We ought therefore to understand (as was said before) that man is composed of matter, which is his passive part, and form, which is his active agent. And just as matter formerly proceeded from the watery subject of the dark abyss emerging from chaos, it is therefore of itself North-leaning <note>original: "Boreali"</note> and prone to a private disposition—namely, to rest, cold, mortification, and immobility. Indeed, it is this matter which causes contraction both in the heart (and consequently in the motion of the pulses) and in other parts of the body; that is, the natural inclination of matter in man is to contract the Spirits from the circumference to the center. 

Conversely, the form, which is derived from light, is occupied in dilation and therefore in the animation and agitation of matter, which without such an agent would remain stupid and as if dead from the Northern cold of its mother. And this is the reason for Systole and Diastole <note>The contraction and expansion of the heart</note> in the motion of the heart, which arises from that action and passion—or operation and resistance—which occurs between light and the dark, cold, golden-matter <note>original: "aurolarem"</note> in the human composition. From this it is evident that, just as the greater world <note>the universe</note> is composed of contraries, the lesser world <note>man</note> is also rightly said to be composed of the offspring of light and that of darkness. 

Now, however, the attractive faculty of a living man seems to differ from that of the Magnet in this: because the Magnet does not appear to the human sense to be as alive and agile as a man, but in a certain way seems dead, insofar as it is divided from its ferruginous <note>iron-bearing</note> vein. And again, the Magnet itself does not act by an evident dilation proceeding from vivifying heat through an organic substance, but by a contractive power—partly earthy and partly celestial—which first sent out its rays by dilation and only then contracted to allure to itself. For that reason, its greatest power of attracting consists in the pole. But the attraction of a living man proceeds from the dilation of vivifying heat from the center toward the circumference, so that the material instruments may perform their duties for attraction as well as retention and expulsion; and sometimes it operates chiefly toward contraction—that is, it moves from the circumference toward the center—namely, when by divine will the private emanation...

For I warn such audacious and rash judges to know that, just as the Magnet (however much the mass appears dead to the eyes) is observed to seek and affect the rays of the spirits with the body of another Magnet by a living central appetite—and the whole Magnet and any portion of it divided from the whole will perform this according to its proportion—so also I can prove and confirm by ocular demonstration that by the proper application of flesh taken from some member of a corpse to the flesh of a living man for several hours, the man to whom it is applied will be rendered weak and invalid. And yet, shortly after the removal of that corporeal **Magnetic Mummy** <note>A term for the vital essence or "balsam" preserved in a body after death</note>, he will recover his former strength.

But, lest this report of mine seem a fiction to adversaries—insofar as they might allege that the application of such things operates more in the imagination of the living man than in his body, and that he persuades himself he is weak without a true foundation, and that no external effect can be produced to prove this—I respond that this application is of such efficacy that it is observed to extract the **Spiritual mummy** in a visible form. For by reason of the external cold of the member, the mummy thus extracted is condensed on the surface of the Magnetic body, no differently than air into a cloud or a cloud into snow. The incorruptible Spirit of God <note>original: "incorruptibilem Dei Spiritum"; a reference to the Book of Wisdom 12:1, "For thy incorruptible spirit is in all things."</note> is in all things, and consequently as much in the dead as in the living. This may be seen in vegetables, which appear dead in the winter time; because the spirits of life leave their circumference and hide themselves in the center, as if in a place further removed from the assaults of the cold, and there they seem to rest.

United with the celestial rays which are sent down from above to their aid, it attempts with its greatest power to expel the dark deprivation and the freezing cold from its tabernacle, so that it may proceed more freely to the act of vegetation and multiplication, as is evident in wheat buried or sown in the earth. In no other way, I say, is the nature of the **Martial Magnet** <note><term>Martial Magnet</term>: Iron or magnetized ore, associated with the planet Mars.</note>—with its **Saturnine spirit** <note><term>Saturnine spirit</term>: Lead-like, cold, or contracted energy associated with the planet Saturn.</note> originally contracted into its center—shaken and incited; and with equal joy it draws to itself the formal rays of iron, from whose **Martial Sulphurous spirit** <note><term>Sulphurous spirit</term>: In alchemy, "Sulphur" represents the active, combustible, and formative principle.</note> they originally gushed forth. And in such a manner also the spirit of a **Corpse**, driven by the mediating mortifying cold from the circumference into the center and remaining there in rest and without action, renders the body and every part of it fixed and immobile.

But truly, when it makes an appearance or application toward the circumference of its own living species, then indeed it rises up from its center even to the circumference (as if it were oppressed by hunger in the center) and, with a greedy appetite, attracts to itself its like in the living man—which dilates itself and projects through the pores in a radiant manner to bring help to it—by means of a **Spiritual Mummy** <note><term>Mummy</term>: Not an Egyptian corpse, but a Paracelsian term for the vital essence or "marrow" of a body that retains healing or magnetic power after death.</note> toward the center, so that it may be clothed again with the life by which it lived before, and that it may be refreshed by its presence. But the oily spiritual mummy of the dead man, filled with lucid spirits and suddenly thickened by the cold upon the surface of the living man, is congealed and can be reserved for private use.

Indeed, this cannot be better confirmed than by the example of the contractive, restrictive, or congealing virtue of the smoky outgrowth of salt contained in the bones of the dead. For by the application of that—namely, the **Usnea** <note><term>Usnea</term>: A type of moss or lichen, specifically "Muscus Cranii Humani," which grew on the skulls of criminals left on gibbets; it was highly prized in sympathetic medicine to stop bleeding.</note> or moss growing upon the skull of the dead—to a burst of blood in a living man, the warm blood in the living man, moved by a kind of **Antipathetic** affection, retreats, and its exit is denied by the congealing and astringent operation of this "Boreally" <note>North-like or cold</note> affected outgrowth.

But omitting for a time such conclusions which look toward the **Mummial Magnet** of a dead man and its virtues, what will you say if there be a **Microcosmic Magnet** <note><term>Microcosmic Magnet</term>: A magnetic force derived from the "Microcosm" (the human being) while still alive.</note> which can be collected from a living man without any detriment to his life or body? Its virtues—both in respect to its natural and monstrous generation and birth (as being derived from dissimilar parents, and also from substances differing in species like a mule, namely, composed of earthy Mercury and the Choleric human spirits of Sulphur), as well as by reason of its attraction of the spiritual Mummy from a living man, and even (which is still more admirable) its transplantation into both animal and vegetable species—operate in a strange and wonderful way, as much **Sympathetically** as **Antipathetically**.

I know for certain that these new things will immediately be reputed as **Diabolical** acts and illicit ways by those who are prone to unjust and iniquitous judgment, insofar as these things exceed the sphere of their capacity. And yet I understand for a certainty that they are true, and have been experienced by some, not without the admiration of many. Indeed, we are not ignorant of this **Microcosmic Magnet** nor the use of it; its acts and the effects of its acts, when they shall be proved by the wise, will appear as natural as their effects (well-weighed by them) will seem at first glance admirable, foreign to human capacity, and exceedingly abstruse. But truly, if those things which have been recited by me before are rightly understood and seriously weighed, the cause of them will not appear so abstruse as to exceed the limits of nature. Concerning the action of such a Microcosmic Magnet, both Sympathetic and Antipathetic, I have proposed (God granting) to discourse more in the following parts, namely, in the last book of this work.

### CHAPTER V.

->*In this chapter is explained the secret cause why, and the manner how, the Magnet—both Microcosmic <note>the human version</note> and Macrocosmic <note>the universal version</note>—is accustomed to operate at an instant, and indeed across an unknown dimension or an indeterminate interval.*<-

Foster, in a certain book of his entitled *Hoplocrisma Spongus* <note>original: "Hoplocrifma fpongius"; likely referring to William Foster's 1631 work "The Sponge to Wipe Away the Weapon-Salve," which attacked the idea of sympathetic magic</note>, expressed the thinness of his philosophy more than enough when he said that, because the light of the sun and stars cannot penetrate dark clouds and opaque bodies, therefore the formal essence of man is not able, in its motion or course, to move toward some distant goal through mountains, castles, groves, and the like. But, if he had immersed himself a little more deeply into the bowels of true Philosophy, then without a doubt he would recognize that the ethereal seed, or stellar influences, are by nature much more subtle than are the vehicles of visible light. Indeed, they are thin and strictly spiritual and exceedingly mobile, and so penetrating and alive that they are powerful, and even accustomed to penetrate perpetually without any manifest obstacle or resistance to the bowels or center of the earth, and there to generate metals of all species according to the condition of the influence. And all Philosophers, both ancient and modern, bear witness to this matter.

Plotinus, following the mind of Plato, seems to explain the subtlety of this Spirit in these words: "So great is the thinness of the Ether that it penetrates all bodies of the universe, both above and below, and being joined or entwined with them, it does not make the larger things any bigger, because that interior spirit nourishes and preserves all their works with its minimal mass, receiving no increase at all." Thus he spoke. And by reason of the purity and subtlety of that celestial nature, the heaven is called by mystical Philosophers and Poets the husband or spouse of the earth, whom they called Vesta. Indeed, the very stars of heaven, in whose series the Copernicans <note>followers of Copernicus's heliocentric model</note> number the earth, are likened to the wives of heaven, inasmuch as they are drawn out from it no differently than Eve from the side of Adam. For they define them to be the denser parts of their orbs, whence it happens that they are considered members of heaven; nothing is so thin, subtle, and penetrating as is that spirit from which they themselves are derived through condensation.

This, moreover, is the reason why true Alchemists tell so many wonderful things about their "heaven," which they also call the *quintessence* <note>the "fifth essence" or purest element</note>, arguing from this that by reason of its purity and subtlety it can penetrate all things. And Philosophers say that this quintessence is that nature of theirs which they define as a certain infinite power in things, permeating all beings, generating all things and increasing, nourishing, and procreating like from like. And certainly, if anyone chooses to consider realistically those things which were previously cited by me, he will remember me having said that Angelic virtues flow from the archetypal emanation and are types of the Divine Ideas, and also that the ethereal spirit is filled with Angelic influences which have their essential root from God and in God. So, in the truth of the matter, it is not stellar light which penetrates so deeply or operates so universally, but that eternal, most central spirit, which by its divine and irresistible essence penetrates and permeates through all things; as much in the heaven above as in the earth and waters below.

And all this seems to be confirmed by the Mystical Philosophers (albeit only obscurely) when they call Saturn—who was the Father of Jove or the head or *Kether* <note>Hebrew: "Crown," the highest Sephirah in the Kabbalah</note> of the Universal emanation—the father of heaven and earth, arguing from this that in the emission of the spirit of wisdom he created and formed the heavens, according to that passage of Job: *By his Spirit he has garnished the heavens.* <margin>Job 26:13</margin> And David: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and all the host of them by the spirit of his mouth.* <margin>Psalm 33:6</margin> And St. Peter has it: *The heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and through the water by the word of God.* <margin>2 Peter 3:5</margin> It is certain, therefore, that the whole essential act in the ethereal spirit is an act of divine emanation, or the "bright spirit of the incorruptible God," to use the words of Solomon. <margin>Wisdom 12:1</margin> And therefore it necessarily follows that that Spirit, which deserves to be the immediate vehicle of such an irresistible and most powerful influence, must be conformable in purity and subtlety to the very nature that informed it. Which is said by Solomon to be "more mobile than any thing and more subtle, reaching everywhere because of its cleanness, renewing all things and filling the whole world." <margin>Wisdom 7:24</margin> This, therefore, was that which compelled some even among the Christian Philosophers to break out into this speech: *God is nature, and nature is God.* By which they seem to understand that "naturing nature" <note>Latin: *natura naturans*, the creative principle</note> and radically informing nature was that eternal emanation which made and informed the moist nature of the world, which for that reason was called "natured nature" <note>Latin: *natura naturata*, the created world</note>, namely by the presence of that naturing nature, or the Divine Spirit of God, which was moved over the waters, and imparted to them a fiery vigor or virtue, as can be seen partly by the testimony of holy letters and partly by the assertion of St. Augustine. It is necessary, therefore, that we [give] due [consideration] of these... <margin>Wisdom 1:7</margin>

# SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Member II.

Based on the consideration of the things we have alleged, let us know that if an influence is completely animated by the incorruptible spirit of the Lord, then it must necessarily be imbued with the properties of the nature of that Divine spirit. Consequently, it must be the most subtle, agile, mobile, and penetrating of all spirits. In that respect, it will be more powerful for penetrating all solid things without any hindrance or resistance, and also more accommodated and ready for generating, increasing, and nourishing all things. And if it should be incorporated or specified <note>i.e., taken on a specific physical form</note>, it is accustomed to procreate similar individuals from similar ones. Furthermore, in respect to human capacity, it has an infinite extension in the emission of its rays, and therefore, it is impossible for it to be limited.

I will demonstrate all of this by experience or by ocular demonstration of this kind. We find in **Magnetic practice** that the **Magnet**, by the power of its subtle Spirit which animates it intrinsically and centrally, is rendered so powerful in its attractive virtue that it is able to transmit the rays of its activity through the hardest rocks, thick woods, the most compact metals, and even through glass (which is otherwise impenetrable) without any resistance. This is the most evident argument that this spirit is of a nature far more penetrable and subtle than that sublunary air, insofar as the air is denied passage through such things.

By the same reasoning, the internal celestial spirit of man, which is the vehicle of that life-giving ray, is so subtle in itself that nothing can resist it when the internal mental ray aims at any goal whatsoever, no matter how remote from the man or inaccessible to human capacity. For, since that celestial Spirit in man is formed after the pattern of the Divine spirit, it must necessarily be that He limits it in such an action of its own. Now, the subtlety of the Divine act in the human spirit is expressed by **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many mystical and alchemical texts are attributed</note> in this manner: *Whoever is supported by this nature of God, they embrace all things with their intelligence—those which are on the earth and those in the sea, and if there is anything besides above the heaven—and they raise themselves up so far that they behold the Good itself, etc.*

By these words, he seems to signify the all-sufficient God in his penetration and transmigration through all things. This act consists in the mental ray; by not resisting its act, celestial influences penetrate and work everywhere on the earth and in the sea without any resistance or intermediate impediment. From these things, therefore, it is evident that just as every specific inferior creature is endowed with this essential spirit and consists in it, it builds upon it as if upon the real foundation of its truth or its true cornerstone.

So indeed, the emission of its rays is not to be terminated by any sphere of activity, as certain 
<margin>Finland. 4.</margin> 
indiscreet and more sensual than intellectual Philosophers have not blushed to assert. For, according to the testimony of the crowd of the wisest Philosophers, that spirit is defined to be an infinite force of things, and consequently not defined or determined. For, as far as it emits the rays of its activity from the center of a celestial star, even so far can that central spirit in the earth and its creatures extend the diameter of its own emanation. Thus, just as the radiant influence of a celestial star penetrates downward even to the center of the earth, in exactly the same way any [terrestrial] star <note>referring to the "star" or essential spark within a physical object</note> penetrates by ascending even to the center of its own celestial star from which it was radically derived. And the more opulent, rich, and more exalted that stellar form shall be in a creature, the more closely it approaches the nature of a more worthy and occult star in heaven, and consequently makes the extension of its rays (or the semi-diameter of its emission) longer and stronger.

Now indeed, we see how every astral influence in a creature, by a certain natural instinct and in a **Sympathetic** manner, looks toward the celestial source or star from which it first arose. Likewise, that celestial star, with a certain paternal respect, emits its influences downward to its earthly son—or to cherish and nourish its filial form or fire in the creature—so much so that both of them seem to rejoice mutually among themselves and receive each other in a reciprocal embrace, according to that saying of the Philosophers: *Nature rejoices in nature and contains nature.* O nature of celestial truth, multiplying the natures of God mutually!

So also the species of creatures, which are clothed in one and the same influence, are accustomed by reason of their similarity to ejaculate **sympathetic** rays toward each other—that is, rays consenting by nature—by which they meet in concord and love. And for that reason, the axiom of the Philosophers previously alleged is this: *Nature is accustomed to procreate from similar things.* And this is the cause why every specific form is observed to rejoice in its like, and to procreate its like without transgression from the limits of its species. For example, human nature produces a human, equine nature a horse, the seed of fennel produces fennel, a bean a bean, a grain of wheat produces wheat, etc.

Furthermore, the nature of a thing so created is most friendly to its own likeness, and emits lovely rays of sympathy so that they may agree and concur with the rays emitted by its like, so that both natures consent and mutually embrace: as is to be seen in the **Magnet with the Magnet**, and the **Magnet with iron**. For if one Magnet finds or meets another, both will behold each other by the power of the **Saturnine Sulphurous Spirit** <note>A technical term in alchemy/hermeticism referring to the specific "soul" or active principle of the mineral</note> and will mutually embrace each other. For by their due application one to another, by the emission of rays from the center to the circumference...

For we are taught by experience that the female stone <note>The lodestone or magnet</note>, quite like a wanton harlot, attracts and desires the male iron: and not the other way around, as Averroes, Scaliger, and Cardinal Cusanus erroneously and falsely believe. *For* it is their opinion that the iron itself allures the Magnet to it as if to its own Origin and matrix from which it had arisen. Now, however, to confirm the infinite efficacy of these central rays in the said two bodies, namely of the polar star and the Magnet or iron, it is necessary that we first be led by a certain suitable Theory, so that afterwards we may descend into practice with an easier Method. The ray (says <margin>Alkindus, *On Stellar Rays*.</margin> Alkindus <note>Al-Kindi, a 9th-century philosopher who wrote on the power of stellar radiation.</note>) which proceeds from the center of a star to the center of the earth is proved to be the strongest in the operation of its own kind, etc. By which he seems to argue for the distance at which the hidden ray or radiant influence of a star operates and acts, even in its image or likeness on earth. For elsewhere he says this: It is clear that stellar rays constitute the diverse individuals in this world, etc. Again, in favor of the central stars or stellar influences of inferior bodies, and their radiant extensions, he says elsewhere: The Elemental world is a copy of the Sidereal world, so that whatever thing is contained in it contains the likeness of the star itself; it is manifest that every thing of this world produces rays in its own way after the likeness of the Stars, otherwise it would not fully possess the form of the Star of the world, but this is also manifested gradually in some things. For fire transmits rays of heat to nearby places, and the earth rays of cold. Assuming this therefore as true, we say that everything which has actual existence in the world of Elements emits rays in every direction, which fill the whole Elemental world in their own way. Furthermore, the distance of one thing from another makes a difference in the effect of the rays in the things of this world: Thus he spoke. By this discourse he makes us more certain; First, that there is nothing in the lower world which does not have its likeness in that upper world from which it receives the rays and influences of its essence.

And again, that just as that celestial star shoots its rays even to the center of the earth, and therefore has so wide a sphere of activity that it searches every portion of the whole concave of the world, so also those stellar or radiant sparks, which it emits to the creatures subject to it—since their stars are one and the same in substance and form with their source and consequently are continued with it, and are by no means indivisible from it in spirit and light—search all the corners of the sublunary region. Indeed, they are accustomed to penetrate to their celestial source, from which they obtain their power of life, as will be demonstrated below; and that is indicated all the more clearly because any portion of a large Magnet, however small, claims for itself its own distinct poles and circles, just as that large or whole one from which it was cut. By these things, therefore, it is rendered apparent that the action of any elemental thing is effected as much at a distance as when two bodies are joined together by mutual contact. Truly, the action of Elemental things when they are separated from each other is perfected by a due application and an infusion of radiant influences into one another, which would seem scarcely credible by reason of the hiddenness of the action itself, unless experience from the observation of the attraction of iron by the Magnet at a distance taught us so. Furthermore, we also notice that the images of things are discerned from afar in optical mirrors. Nor was it the least artifice among the Pythagoreans, and some of the Christian Philosophers, to express their minds or intentions to others living in different places or regions far distant from them, by reason of reflections through glasses mathematically prepared and arranged on the disk of the moon. But truly our external Philosophers, who wish to be governed by sense alone, dream of a certain determined sphere of activity, and do not blush to assign limits to this spirit or mystic nature. For example, because a Magnet attracts iron, for the most part, only at a distance of half a table or one ell; therefore they think and conclude that the vivifying act of its virtue cannot penetrate further or extend itself in the air, and consequently, led only by the eyes of the body and not of the intellect, they wish to terminate the Spiritual extension of the Magnet by this external observation of theirs. But; if they would wish, after the manner of the most skilled Philosophers, to behold the marrow of such an abstruse action with the mental light, they would indeed perceive that the extension of the radiant Spirit in the Magnet is equal to the semi-diameter of its own celestial star, since both are of one and the same essence: And likewise there is a similar spirit in iron and any portion of it, but there are many things which can hinder the evident effect in the Magnet,

In which **A** is the Pole of the Magnet, and **B. D.** is the base of its rays with its full vigor, which terminates and adapts itself at the beginning of the iron rod **B, D**. But truly, when the iron is placed at a longer distance or further from the Magnet, namely at **C**, then indeed a larger portion of the Spiritual Base of the pyramidal emission is dilated and passes outside the sides of the iron without any contact or direct encounter with it. Thus, the act of Magnetic virtue is rendered too weak to attract such a heavy thing to itself at such a distance.

And the Magnet itself, thus animated and increased in its life-giving vigor, corresponds to the action of that star, penetrating by one and the same sympathetic consent even to the center of its celestial source. This can be most easily accomplished in it, since both are of one and the same essence. Do we not perceive this to be true by external observation, when we observe the Northern pole of the Magnet constantly looking toward the polar star at such a great distance in a due natural and obedient respect? This could not happen otherwise, unless their rays were joined in the midst of the air, indeed in the ether itself, and even in the earth and sea. 

For who can deny that the rays of the polar star itself descend into the earth and work and join with rays similar to themselves in the magnet, in iron, and even in fired earth <note>Likely referring to bricks or ceramics that have acquired magnetic properties through heating.</note>, since we are taught this very thing by ocular experience? If, therefore, the Magnet and iron and earth are sparks of that star, why, I pray, in the manner of their source, would these sparks not likewise flash forth and ascend or emit their rays toward that celestial Star? For it is certain and proven by experience that even the smallest fragment of a *Terrella* <term>Terrella: A "little earth," or a spherical magnet used to model the Earth's magnetic field.</term> or large Magnet, cut or divided from its whole, is just as complete in its circles and poles as the entire piece. 

From this it is clear that the virtue of any thing proceeds from the formal spark lurking within it: for a spark or ray of the Sun has the same power of acting and illuminating, according to its proportion, as its Solar source—not otherwise than we see a tiny candle shine according to its quantity in the same way as the larger one from which it took the beginning of its light. Therefore, it is not to be doubted that if the polar star pours its rays into the Magnetic body, the central Star of the magnetic body likewise emits its rays to the celestial seat of its polar source. 

But truly, we are taught by Astronomical practice that the distance or interval between these two bodies—namely the polar Star and the earth or Magnet—is so great and immense that a larger extension in the nature of things in respect to us can hardly be imagined: namely, that between the eighth heaven <note>In the Ptolemaic system, the sphere of the fixed stars.</note> in which the polar Star resides, and the earth. And yet we find that these two bodies look toward each other and work together with an admirable sympathy; indeed, sometimes, when there is not a straight disposition between them, they seem to disagree with a quite notable Antipathy. Is it to be believed that the imaginary limits of a certain sphere of activity are terminated according to the opinions of some unskilled men, who are too superficial in their understanding of the hidden treasures and secrets—or the central actions of God—at work within a creature? By the same reasoning, we are compelled to grant that there is a similar sympathetic meeting of hidden rays between iron and the Magnet <note>The lodestone or natural magnet</note>, since both of them possess within themselves central "Stars" or radiant influences of one and the same nature or essence descending from a single source. Their hidden emanations pass across a distance unknown to us, even if their effects do not appear to the senses any more than those celestial influences which descend from heaven upon minerals, vegetables, and animals. Nevertheless, if we give any credit to histories and accounts, we have learned from Serapion, Olaus Magnus, and the Moors themselves, that among the Indians toward the North Pole there are certain cliffs of a Magnetic consistency which draw ships to themselves from a great distance; indeed, so great is their power of attraction that they sometimes even pull the iron nails out of the wooden substance of the ships, which is why they are forced to build their ships and boats with wooden pegs rather than iron ones. And again, what is to be said regarding the opinion of that most learned physician and Philosopher, Fracastoro? For he, after his long inquiry into the nature of the Magnet, finally saw fit to conclude that the reason why the Magnet turns its pole toward the North is because in that corner of the world many mountains are found consisting of Magnetic stone, which attract iron to themselves from afar. This would happen just as if the iron followed them; such Magnetic cliffs were able to operate from the seat of the equinox to the frozen point of the North Pole. For we are taught by experience that sailors use the magnetic needle even as far as the equinoctial line <note>The Equator</note> to explore at what latitude they are sailing. Nevertheless, although this will seem foreign and impossible to some, there are indeed those skilled in the Geographic art and most well-versed in the composition of sea charts who firmly adhere to this opinion of Fracastoro. By these examples, one may see that some men, commonly considered wise and learned, seem to suggest that the limited sphere of activity assigned to the Magnet's power by the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle</note> and Christian academics is vain and of no importance.

But to ascend now from the mineral kingdom to the vegetable and animal: we observe indeed an admirable relationship between the fixed and wandering stars <note>The planets</note>, and by the same logic between plant and plant. For example, it has been discovered (as witnessed by <margin>Mizaldus, *Secrets*</margin>) that the rays and flowers of the Heliotrope herb <note>The sunflower or turnsole</note>, and those of the Chicory, are accustomed in a sympathetic manner to rejoice in the solar rays, and to harmonize with that radiant influence, embracing it courteously. For they turn themselves toward the daily motion of the Sun even on a cloudy day; in the absence of the Sun, their flowers contract as if they were enemies to the dark and cold night. Also, the onion in certain regions (as <margin>Plutarch</margin> testifies) grows green during the waning of the Moon, and is noted to wither again as it waxes. There is also a great sympathetic relationship between the crab, the oyster, and the Moon: for while the Moon waxes, their juices increase, but as it wanes, they likewise diminish in their substance. Furthermore, as far as the irradiation of one plant toward another is concerned, it has been observed that the herb Rue regards the Fig tree with the greatest friendship; hence it happens that this plant flourishes nowhere better or more abundantly, nor lives with happier success, than if it is planted under a Fig tree. And that there is also a notable Sympathy between their natures is made manifest because they are not dissimilar in taste and smell. Moreover, if Myrtle is planted near a Pomegranate tree, it makes it more fertile and fruitful, and on the other hand, the pomegranate renders the myrtle more fragrant. From this it is clear that one rejoices and delights in the presence of the other. And in truth, both are noticed to agree in one Elemental condition, insofar as these trees are cold, dry, and astringent. 

But to express that vast sympathetic relationship which exists between the vegetable and mineral nature, we ought especially and with diligence to observe that hidden property in the Hazel: for if at a certain stated time, a Hazel rod forked at the end is gathered from its tree, and each forked part is held in each hand—on the condition that the place where the little rods join the trunk or Staff, together with the trunk—

Such, I well know, will be the judgment of those who are most ready to judge before the matter is understood as it truly is.

In truth, there is a proportioned harmony in all inferior creatures, by which they correspond to the celestial or rather Divine bodies in their influences. These influences derive their origin from a single, chief, universal <note>original: *Catholica*</note>, and eternal emanation, which pours its rays—both essential and sympathetic, as well as antipathetic—immediately into every stellar globe. And these globes likewise rain them down into the Elementary world, effecting through this communion a harmonic contentment between these two regions. And therefore <margin>Al-Kindi, *On the Rays of the Stars*</margin> all things that happen in this world and occur in the world of the Elements are translated from celestial Harmony. It is certain, therefore, that the metallic rays concurring in their act with the influential rays of the forked rod are the cause for that portion of the hazel <note>original: *Corylacæ*</note> rod to incline downward, no differently than a magnet is observed to strongly attract iron and another magnet through its pole. I know it will seem strange to such men that a metallic substance emits rays from its veins; but if they were as well-versed in the living natures of metals as those craftsmen who work in the mines of the mountains of Tyrol and Hungary, then they would be made certain by ocular experience that metals sometimes emit lightning and thunder in the hollows of the earth. These are so dangerous to the workmen that unless they immediately exit the mine after the supports are placed, or lie flat on the ground, they suffer the ultimate end. I have received this from noble Germans worthy of trust, some of whom were eyewitnesses.

But to proceed in our purpose, there is likewise an antipathetic aspect among inferior creatures, no differently than among certain special stars of heaven, both wandering <note>planets</note> and fixed. The aspect of one creature is known to abhor that of another, so that in the application of their rays, one is observed to turn away and reflect from the other with an angry, fearful, or hateful aversion. Mizaldus says that the cucumber, as if <margin>Mizaldus, Book 1</margin> terrified by the sound of thunder, is often changed by it. The onion is rejected by the Egyptians in their food because it is observed to differ greatly from other vegetables; for, while all other herbs besides it grow during the waxing of the moon, the onion alone, by contrast, suffers detriment and diminution while the moon is flourishing. There is also a notable antipathy between the fig tree, the sea-calf <note>seal</note>, and lightning; whence it arises that these two are never struck by lightning. Furthermore, no small hatred is noticed between the reed and the fern; so much so that if the root of <margin>Pliny, Book 10</margin> one is placed upon the branches of the other, it is cast down with a certain contempt and hatred. Among all beasts, the elephant hates the tiny mouse; whence it happens that if any grain provided for their nourishment is eaten or touched by mice, they immediately reject and abhor it. A similar <margin>Ibid. 12</margin> antipathy is observed to exist between the natures of the Catablepas <note>A legendary Ethiopian beast that kills with its gaze</note> and many blood-weasels <note>original: *hæmamustelæ*</note>; <margin>Pliny, Book 13</margin> weasels are like poison to the catablepas. The domestic cock avoids the fox in an antipathetic <margin>Pliny, Book 13, ch. 13</margin> manner. All serpents and snakes fear and avoid the ash tree, and therefore with the greatest care they flee its shadow, both in the morning and the afternoon. Again, Dioscorides says the yew tree <note>original: *Taxum*</note> is so poisonous that if anyone sits beneath it, they will receive harm from it and sometimes lose their life. Rodiginus <note>Lodovicus Caelius Rhodiginus (1469–1525), an Italian scholar known for his encyclopedic works on natural wonders.</note> asserts that a serpent is struck with terror at the sight of a naked man. It is well known and confirmed by many authors that the catablepa <note>original: "catablepam"; likely referring to the Catoblepas, a mythical beast from Ethiopia said to kill with its gaze</note>, which is but a tiny animal, can nevertheless kill at a distance of a thousand paces by its mere gaze. Even a man afflicted with bleary eyes <note>original: "lippitudine oculorum"; a reference to contagious ophthalmia or "sore eyes"</note> is capable of infecting another person at a considerable distance through a certain secret emission of contagious rays, thereby making them bleary-eyed as well. We see that an onion can draw out tears from a person at a distance, and that by the mere ejaculation of its rays. Furthermore, it is a known fact that, just as a healthy thing tends to receive its like in a salutary manner, so also a corrupted thing, by way of Antipathy <term>Antipathy: a natural repulsion or "counter-feeling" between two substances</term>, infects and poisons its like (which was previously healthy) even at a distance. Just as we observe, the eye of one man afflicted with ophthalmia infects no other limb of another man except the eye. And even one who is consumptive <note>original: "phthificus"; suffering from tuberculosis</note> or has ulcerated lungs, wounds and harms the lungs of another man by his breath at a suitable distance; this occurs by the application or concurrence of two irradiations of one nature, one of which is affected by Antipathy and poison, whence it is accustomed to contaminate the other to which it is applied.

But, to return to our Magnetic Goal, which is as much Spiritual as it is corporeal: I affirm that there is such a spiritual regard of Sympathy <term>Sympathy: a natural attraction or "shared feeling" between things of a similar nature</term> between one creature and another, that the beloved, by a wonderful manner of spirits, attracts and allures the lover to itself. I myself have seen this wonderfully performed by my water dog. For on my journey toward Lyon in France, I lost my traveling bag <note>original: "penularium"</note> which was hanging over the saddle-bow (in which, among other necessities, letters of exchange were enclosed). When I attempted to turn back to search for it, I could by no means compel the messenger's horse to go backward against its habit. Wherefore, I was forced by necessity to send the dog to search for my lost goods and bring them back to me. The dog departed, and after being absent for nearly half an hour, he brought back that bag of mine in his mouth. This was indeed admirable, considering I had been on horseback, so that he could not have perceived any track or scent of my feet; and yet, he hurried directly to the bag I had left behind <note>original: "Tantaleam hiatum"; literally "Tantalus-like gap," implying a void or loss</note>, and perceiving my scent in it, he recognized it immediately and brought it to me at a swift run.

But to approach this more closely and pertinently: a certain friend who was in my company at that time lost his water dog in the city of London at night. Meanwhile, we both entered a certain private house where he had hardly ever been before. While we were having a private conversation in a room of that house with the door closed, a little after half an hour the dog returned and came to the gate, scratching it vigorously with his claws so that it might be opened for him to reach his master. From these things it is evident that the rays of the dog's affection, although his body was absent from his Master, nevertheless did not desert the rays of his Master’s affection; whence it happened that they guided him so directly to an unknown place.

Is there not also that admirable Sympathetic emanation from the pigeon called the "carrier" <note>original: "tabellaria"</note>, which by its light is accustomed to tend so directly across so many thousands of miles to the home in which it was born and bred? For that reason, it loves and affects that place so dearly that, even if it be carried 500 miles away shut in its basket, it will nevertheless fly directly back with letters suspended from its neck. This is indeed an evident argument that it is guided directly by the rays of its affection on the way, which are continued and united in a certain Spiritual manner, and are not separated from the place in which it takes the greatest delight.

What shall we say of two persons, one of whom loves a male and the other a female, and is affected without any reason? And therefore, one follows the beloved with rays of affection, even though the other party abhors and neglects them, and cannot receive them with a reciprocal degree of affection, but turns the rays of love into hatred. But truly, where two receive each other with mutual affection and Sympathetic union, there indeed the power of the action will produce its effects at a longer distance; not otherwise than when two stars of heaven emit their rays diametrically and meet in one and the same Harmonic point of affection.

Indeed, as we see taught by experience, there is a great Antipathy between the contracted Spirit of a murdered man and the murderer; so much so, that the vital Spirit of the dead man, contracted in its center by the touch of cold after death, is observed to move again from the center to the circumference through a certain irascible, Antipathetic passion, causing the congealed blood to flow back again and move toward the murderer, as if it wished to resist a second insult from its enemy, or to take or seek vengeance against him. So indeed we ought to acknowledge and confess, that where one Spirit concurs with another of similar nature by reason of Sympathy, there the power must be greater, and consequently its action can exercise its force at a longer distance, as is evidently demonstrated in the abstruse operation between the wound-dressing <note>original: "telam vulnerariam"</note>, the weapon salve <note>original: "unguentum armarium"; a controversial 17th-century remedy where the ointment was applied to the weapon that caused the wound rather than the wound itself</note>, and the wounded person. Concerning these things, I have spoken many words in that hostile encounter which took place between Foster the Priest <note>William Foster, who attacked Fludd's theories in "Hoplocrisma-Spongus" (1631)</note> and myself.

But observe, I pray, this second experiment concerning the weapon salve. **Sir Bevis Thelwell**, a knight, related to me on his word of honor that a certain maker of wooden wheels had been gravely wounded by an axe. When these things were reported to the gentlewoman, as she was of a humorous disposition, she said laughing: "Then I shall try an experiment related to me by the giver of this ointment." She immediately went to the box of ointment, extracted the toothpick belonging to this woman, and threw it into a basin full of water. Once this was done, the reckless woman's pains returned, and only after a reconciliation was made was she cured a second time. And finally, the spirit (according to the testimony of Ezekiel <note>original: "Ezechielis"</note> in the two properties which blow from the north and from the south) undergoes an imbalance; a confinement and freezing of the Spirit occurs in the weapon <note>The "telum" or weapon that caused the wound, often used in sympathetic medicine.</note> from the effect of the withdrawal of the summoned rays, and as if by a scarring of the suffering wound. Again, we must consider that any separated blood possesses within itself a regard for the Microcosm <note>The human body as a "little world" reflecting the universe.</note>: in no other way than how a single portion of a Magnet, divided from the whole, possesses in itself all the proportions of the entire Macrocosm, namely the poles, the Equinox, etc. It is equal to the whole, so much so that the Idea of the wounded limb exists in the Spirits of the emitted blood, and makes its relation to any part of the same, just as the poles of some portion of a whole Magnet, however small, have regard for the whole. So also there is a similar hidden attraction and emission of rays between a small amount of emitted blood and the whole mass of blood retained in the veins, as there is between a small Magnet cut from a Large one, and the whole. I conclude, therefore, that just as the Spirits of the severed Blood, frozen and now possessing the iron <note>The weapon's metal</note> by virtue of the homogeneous heat and the oiliness of the ointment, are observed to refresh themselves as if maturely and exhale little by little by insensible respiration toward their source—not otherwise than a spark in a grain of wheat strives to breathe in its Earthy Borders and tend upward toward the celestial sun—so indeed we have seen a wound in a wounded person healed little by little. And thus far, concerning the mode of action between the wound and the armorial or Magnetic ointment—that is, concerning the interval or space which is situated between the wound and the ointment—I shall discourse in a few words.

The distance between the Polar Star and the Magnet is unknown, and yet one acts upon the other through a reciprocal emission of their rays upward and downward: from which it is established that no sphere of activity can be ascribed to these actions of theirs. The Sun and the Spirit in a grain of wheat act between themselves in plainly the same manner: namely, by the continuation of one and the same nature. Behold, therefore, here the limited and bounded sphere of activity is altogether abolished, since no one can justly determine the extension of the Solar influence, in whose essence the grain in the wheat participates: no differently than a tiny Magnet cut from a Large one similarly enjoys its poles and circles with that Large one. Man has a most subtle influence and a most vivid Spirit of life infused into him from on high, that is, inspired by divine inspiration, in which is situated the properties of the four winds, as the Prophet Ezekiel teaches us: and consequently he has the idea of every nature within himself. But the essence of that spirit is indivisible, and therefore the vivifying Spirit sent from it into man [possesses] all the properties of that Spirit which sent and infused it, no differently than <margin>Ezekiel 37.</margin> a smaller Magnet (to insist again and again upon this experiment) taken from a larger one acquires the property of the larger in every respect, and consequently the Spirit of one is no more divided from the other than the Solar rays from the Sun. But truly the Spirit of the Lord, which fills all things (as Solomon says), intends the power of its operation more or less in man according to His will, and therefore in no way admits that fantastical sphere of activity which human wisdom—I mean the subject of the Philosophy of the Pagans (which is foolishness before God)—has invented. For that reason, Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the Hermetic corpus is attributed.</note> has these words: *The Soul, full of mind and God,* <margin>To be examined <note>original: "rimandum"</note></margin> *fills the innermost parts of the world, embraces the outermost, and suggests life to all things; It gives life to that Great animal, the world, and Spirit to all things that live in it.* And he himself elsewhere: *Nothing is more capacious, nothing swifter, nothing more valid or powerful than an incorporeal Nature: So beginning again to meditate from yourself, command your soul, which will fly out faster than you can command; bid it, I say, to pass into the Ocean, and before you have ordered it, it will be there, by no means departing from where it now is. Bid it again to fly into heaven, it will need no wings; for nothing will obstruct its course, not the fire of the Sun, nor the amplitude of the ether, nor the turning of the heavens, nor the bodies of the ancient Stars, but penetrating all things it may transcend even to the supernal body. Nay, even if you wish to pass through all the globes of the heavens and investigate that which is above, that also will be permitted to you. Observe how great is the power of your soul, how great its speed.* These are his words: by which two testimonies of Hermes we can observe first, that the soul in general, and therefore in species or particular, is full of divinity, and by consequence, that Divine essence, which works all in all, is in this soul and in every member of the same, as the Apostle <note>St. Paul</note> testifies. And hence it is that this true Philosopher in the place cited before said that the soul is full of mind and God: Secondly, that this Divinity in the created Universal <note>original: "Catholico"</note> Spirit fills all things in a certain Angelic existence, that is, insofar as it is clothed in the vast worldly spirit as if in a garment. And the sacred page seems to agree with this, saying: *The incorruptible Spirit of God* <margin>Wisdom 12:1.</margin> *is in every thing,* and therefore it is the essential act of worldly life, as I proved in the first book of this Section; whence also the said Hermes elsewhere: *Universal souls flow through the whole world from the one soul of the entire world, as if distributed circumferences etc.* Which indeed agrees with that [saying] of Solomon <margin>To be examined, 14 <note>original: "rimand, 14"</note></margin> alleged before, namely, that all souls in this world are certain small-ray emanations proceeding from the Universal irradiation, which proceeds from the eternal source of the illuminating act, to some more sparingly, and to some more copiously.

# ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY. Page 120.

From this, therefore, man is said to be a little lower than the **Angels** in dignity, by reason of the large portion of the **Spirit of God** <note>original: *Spiritus Dei*</note> granted to him. The spirit of God (says Job) made me, but the inspiration of the Almighty made me intelligent. Because it is in nature through all things, and that to any distance whatever, it shall not be bounded by any imaginary sphere of activity.

But Mr. Foster <note>William Foster, a parson who attacked Robert Fludd’s sympathetic medicine as diabolical</note> with his associates says and repeats that this spirit, which must work into the blood and from the blood to the ointment, is natural and not at all divine. Truly, I cannot help but smile at this assertion of theirs; it is as if someone were to say that this life-giving act—and indeed all other faculties belonging to the human spirit—does not draw its origin from one and the same divine fountain, when we are taught by the Apostle that in Him we live, move, and have our being. Again, it is said that the seat of life or the **vital spirit** is in the blood. And St. John says: *In the Word was life.*

I will say, therefore, what a certain true **Philosopher** writes on this point. The **Soul** (he says), made in the likeness of all wisdom, bears every likeness within itself; it is an **intellectual spirit**, always living, always in motion, and according to the function of its work, it is called by various names:
* It is called **life** <note>original: *vita*</note>, while it gives growth;
* **Spirit**, while it contemplates;
* **Sense**, while it feels;
* **Soul** <note>original: *Animus*</note>, while it is wise;
* **Mind**, while it understands;
* **Reason**, while it discerns;
* **Memory**, while it remembers;
* When it wills, it is called **will**.

Yet all these are nothing but the single soul of one essence, however diverse they may be in property. Thus he writes. From which it is clear that it is the same essential act which creates life and contemplation, sense and intellect, and which produces memory and reason: finally, it is that which wills and does not will.

Since these things are so, do not men—overwhelmed by ignorance—sin gravely when they wish to claim that the hidden actions of this abstruse Spirit (by whose mediation they themselves live, move, understand, discern between good and evil, remember, see, hear, touch, and taste) are the effects of the **Devil**? And thus, the most splendid dignity and honor of the soul itself is violated irreligiously and falsely—by ascribing its secret operations to the Devil—instead of the thanksgivings due to God for His assistance, and it is defiled in the eyes of the world. And why, I ask, do they act so absurdly? Because, forsooth, they do not know how to immerse themselves into the deep marrow of that activity by which they live, move, and exist. Hence, they do not blush to limit the extension of its activity with boundaries according to their own pleasure—they who (however unknown this may be to them) receive their own life and will from it—assigning rash limits to it as judges according to their whim. It is infinite in its existence, insofar as it is a Spirit undivided from the divine emanation, which is infinite in its extension.

Therefore, it is rendered evident that this life-giving Spirit emits its actions to any goal in the world from any specific nature, but especially from the **microcosmic** creature <note>Man, viewed as a miniature version of the universe</note>; and it does so more quickly and willingly if the medium is of one and the same condition as the vehicle of the spirit, namely, the shed **blood**, measuring primarily the distance between the wound and the **ointment**.

Furthermore, we shall find this confirmed by other operations of the spirit effected in the same microcosmic mineral, from which it shoots out its rays to an undetermined distance. For example, it is proven by experience—and that by purely natural ways, with no **Devilish** delusion or superstitious artifice accompanying it—that if the **urine of a jaundiced person** <note>original: *urina icteritij*</note> is carried to a physician or to another person, even many miles distant from the sick man (as has been proven in over a hundred persons by the most noble Earl of **Mulgrave**, a man exceedingly just and religious), and the physician or another person composes a paste with that urine and ash-tree ashes, divides it into 3 or 5 portions, brings them into a round shape, makes a small hole in the top of each ball, fills it with urine and a single grain of saffron, and finally sets these globules aside in some vessel in a convenient place. The Earl himself, I say, with his daughters, testifies that this was true, and that by virtue of this kind he was often accustomed to cure, where medicinal experiments were found too weak and invalid for this work.

And now I will provide testimony of this matter: In the year 1630, the wife of a **Surgeon** living near the **Tower of London** was suffering severely from **jaundice** and griping of the belly. After several physicians applied their efforts in vain, they finally called me. But notwithstanding my endeavor, the disease persisted in its vigor. Wherefore, hearing me mention the cures performed by that Earl, she begged that I send my letters for her to that nobleman. A boy with the letters immediately carried the urine to the Earl's house, and found two strangers there acknowledging thanks for their cure of jaundice. For the love of me, the urine was received, and the servant returned.

But I would have you observe the sequel: as soon as the boy departed from her with the urine of his mistress, the sick woman's mind was greatly disturbed by certain talkative and superstitious women, etc., who made her certain that this thing could not be performed without the help of the **Devil** or **evil magic** <note>original: *cacomagie*</note>, and therefore this act would be dangerous for both her body and soul. Hearing this, as she was by nature quite superstitious, suspicious, and overly incredulous, she began to cry out against **Magic** and **witchcraft**, and became extremely restless. When I understood this, I refused to visit her further, as she was ungrateful and incredulous.

For the spirit of the Blood in the infected person has a continued relation to its own salt; indeed, its habitation is within the aerial <term>Salt of the Blood</term>, which Salt, since it is a subtle earth in whose center the Spirit is contracted, and since the <term>earthen Salt</term> is dispersed through the urine (which is the serum of the Blood), it nourishes and attracts to itself its like from the infected body.
