In this respect, therefore, we compare that composition of ashes, urine, and saffron in such an icteric cure with the weapon salve and the consolidation of wounds; and the urine transferred from the sick person to the mass so composed, we compare with the blood or spirit on the weapon or sword or similar things. What do we think of the wonderful effects upon other animals or vegetables? Certainly, it cannot be hidden from those who are versed in the <term>Mysteries of Natural Magic</term>, both <term>macrocosmic and microcosmic</term><note>The relationship between the great universe (macrocosm) and the human being (microcosm).</note>, that the <term>Spiritual Mummy</term><note>A term used by Paracelsus and his followers to describe the vital life force or "balsam" inherent in living bodies.</note>, whose seat is in the microcosmic blood, can be extracted from the human body by means of a certain <term>Magnetic substance</term> chosen from the same subject, and transplanted into a beast, a tree, or a plant; so that by this means also the disease of the sick person can be transferred from him into the said creatures by the virtue of such an operation or <term>microcosmic Magnet</term>, and the practice of this matter will be clearly explained in the following book. Similarly, Johannes Rumelius Pharamundus, a professor, [claims] that he has cured many suffering from <term>gout</term><note>original: "podagra".</note> by such a cure: namely, by cutting off the hair and nails of the patient's feet and shins, thrusting them into a hole made with a drill even unto the pith of an oak tree, and finally closing that hole firmly with a plug formed from the same tree, and lastly smearing the perforated place all over with cow dung. Then, (he says) if the gout does not return within the space of three months, the oak will be sufficient to attract the disease to itself in a <term>Magnetic manner</term>. But if it returns in that space, then this is an argument for the insufficient magnetic virtue of the oak. Wherefore he then proceeds in this manner: he drills another hole in another oak, as before, and collects the shavings which came out of the hole during the drilling; he bruises them, sews them into a linen bag, applies this bag to the painful place, and is accustomed to do this for three days before the <term>new moon</term>; then, at the hour of the new moon, he takes the bag from the place and extracts the wooden pieces, and puts them into the hole, closing it with a strong plug. But if at last after three months he is not perfectly cured, then he proceeds to his third operation, which is of this kind: he takes the hair and nails of the patient and binds them to the back of a <term>crayfish</term> or river-crab, and throws the animal thus into a river, and the patient will be cured. This the professor, a Doctor in medicine, [wrote] in a certain small book printed in the <term>German language</term><note>original: "idiomate Germanico".</note>: and in the same place it is seen by much public report that he cured many at the first attempt with this experiment of his, and not a few at the first and second, and finally that he [cured] very many gouty people who were [deplored/given up on]...

In that treatise of mine, called *The Squeezing of Foster’s Sponge* <note>A reference to Fludd's work *Spongia Fosteriana*, 1631, where he defended the "Weapon Salve" against the attacks of William Foster.</note>, I recited a sufficiently wonderful History concerning that marvelous Sympathy which exists between the herb called the Sun-rose <note>Latin: *rosa Solis*, likely Drosera or Sundew</note> and the womb <note>Latin: *matrix*</note> of a woman; and I said how, when placed in Plantain water, it closes or contracts itself, and that if part of that water is drunk by a woman laboring in childbirth, and the herb in the water is moved to another house, nevertheless, as her birth becomes imminent, the flower or herb will gradually open and dilate itself, not otherwise than the womb of the one giving birth is accustomed to do. This is truly an evident argument that the rays which are emitted from these two sympathize mutually with each other. I conclude, therefore, that it is manifest that, since the Spiritual attractive power in any inferior creature descends from the Stars of heaven, and is of one continued nature with them—just as solar rays, which are not divided on earth from their bright source—it follows that they emit their radiant influences to each other in no other way than two celestial stars, from which the stars of the creatures descend, are observed to make their aspects in the open air. Thus, if two stars in heaven are friendly, they are accustomed to sympathize mutually, and as if to embrace each other in their meeting or irradiation; but if they are enemies to each other, then in their applications they will feel Antipathy and will willingly turn away from the embrace. Moreover, as pertains to the distance which they observe in their mutual actions, we ought to imagine that it extends as far as the distance of their rays, which make the application to each other. And I would wish that those who are only occupied with sensible things <note>Physical things perceived by the five senses</note> should know that the action of these creatures works secretly through mutual application, even if the effect of that action is not always subjected to the senses; nor should they fail to conceive, I suggest, that the closer the Stars are in heaven in natural affinity, and consequently those inferior creatures which are subjected to the Spirits of the superiors, the more efficacious their sympathizing effects will be, because their rays will ejaculate and meet more directly, that is, without any deviation or declination toward each other.

->CHAPTER VI.<-

> That the Devil, for the perpetration of his stratagems against the human race, makes use of natural things or the creatures of God, without which he can perform nothing: And whether those natural things are therefore Evil-Magical <term>Cacomagical: from the Greek 'kakos' (evil), referring to black magic</term> and consequently to be avoided by men, because their occult effects sometimes conform themselves to the will of the Devil.

We read in many places of Holy Scripture that the Devil makes use of the creatures of God to perpetrate his stratagems and wicked machinations against the human race. For example, to take away the fortunes of Job and bring poverty upon him, Satan used the winds of God, and called (as the Text testifies) the fire of God from heaven to consume his beasts or herds. God, however, [taught] us Christians better than that those creatures of God should be held by us as Evil-Magical or Diabolical for that reason, just because God sometimes disposes them to execute His will through the Devil. He even made the Devil the prince of the air: so that in his power are placed the storms...

Indeed, we observe that all malignant water spirits are subject to her influences, and even Satan observes the times of the various positions or conjunctions and applications of the moon with other stars, both fixed and wandering <note>planets</note>, in his malignant actions. For he himself has been highly skilled in astrology for a long time and knows the effects of every position of the heavens; consequently, he is by no means ignorant of the details of their stronger influences upon animal, vegetable, or mineral creatures which are subject to them. And therefore he understands the times in which they are poured down from above, and he is greatly experienced in their virtues, which at that time are endowed with greater vigor and efficacy, when the powerful influence of their own constellations strikes directly upon them, and excites their central spirits to the extreme of their hidden and secret conditions, to be sent forth and manifested. And then, in that same instant, he collects herbs or stones to make use of the limbs of animals, or at least he teaches witches or enchantresses to perform this same thing, without any knowledge of the mystery of the constellations or the application of rays at the time of the collection of those creatures. So that, when they attempt to make use of these simples <note>medicinal plants</note> by themselves without their master, neglecting and being ignorant of the time of election <note>the astrologically favorable moment</note>, they find them weak and of no [effect]. The herb, animal, and mineral are weaker when the Star which is the nurse and, as it were, the celestial Mother of each of them, has the least power or dominion in the sky.

Every astrological physician, taught by experience, is not ignorant of this truth: for when he collects this or that herb at that point when the constellation, whether fixed or wandering, which has essential dominion over it, is in its greater dignity or power in the sky, he finds an admirable faculty and efficacy in it, as much in its hidden as in its manifest property. On the other hand, if the herb be collected at such a time when its patroness or celestial Mother and nurse is weak and void of virtue, it will appear in its operation as if dead and of hardly any efficacy. From which it is clearly evident that there are creatures of God which work by their essential natures or spirits, and produce effects both Sympathetic and Antipathetic, which the Devil uses to execute his malice, no differently than a physician, philosopher, or natural magus <note>practitioner of natural magic</note> attempts to perfect his good intentions with herbs, animals, and minerals.

What, therefore, is to be said? That those who use the creatures of God in their business, and work by means of their virtues, whether they be animal, vegetable, or mineral, are to be esteemed altogether as Evil Mages <term>Cacomagi: practitioners of black magic</term>, and their works held as Diabolical, because the Devil sometimes adapts their subtle and abstruse actions to establish and exalt his own name and fame among the wise of this world? Is it not God who is accustomed to work such effects through His creatures and produce them before the worldly? Did He not originally impart these virtues or faculties to the creatures by His word in the creation, and continue them through the succession of generation even unto this day? Why, therefore, is it not just as possible for man, who is formed in the image of God, to understand and employ the true times or hours of election for collecting those creatures and understanding their uses or virtues, just as well as the Devil? What? Has man himself, after the fall of Adam, been so blinded by ignorance that he can scarcely distinguish light from darkness? Moreover, we gather in part from the holy scriptures that Adam, after his fall, knew the virtues of the Stars and the condition of every particular earthly creature which is subject to any of them. For otherwise it would have been impossible for him to assign a genuine name, suited to its nature, to each of them.

But if the succession of Adam be so blind that it can in no way distinguish colors, and is therefore ignorant of such secret treasures of God: how, I ask, does the Devil have so profound an inspection into them, since it is certain that he, on account of his rebellion against his Creator, was cast down far lower than the human race, and consequently covered with a darker veil of shadows than man, whence he is not unjustly called the Prince of Darkness? But the worldly will reply, I know well enough, that the Devil is a spirit without a body, and for that reason is more powerful at discerning the secrets of God in creatures, wherefore he can comprehend them more quickly and better than man, being a gross, compact, and corporeal creature. And again, man dies in every age of the world, but the Devil, by reason of his longevity and perpetuity of life, is without doubt endowed with the greatest experience. I answer that, although man dies and is not accustomed to remain long in this world, and although he is somewhat obscured in his intellect by reason of the fall of his first parent; and although (as Solomon says) his soul is weighed down by a <margin>from Wisdom 9.</margin> <note>referring to the Book of Wisdom 9:15: "For the corruptible body presseth down the soul."</note> poorly digested body; so that he can scarcely distinguish by himself those things which are before his eyes, nevertheless it was granted to him in the Beginning after the fall of Adam...

After the ship had been outfitted, the remaining sailors, wishing to bid farewell to their captive comrade before they departed, hurried to the Jew's house. After they had asked to see him for the sake of saying goodbye, he led them into a square courtyard directly facing the sweltering sun. There, they saw that red-haired man <note>original: "ruffum"; the text later explains the specific "alchemical" significance of red-haired individuals in these dark recipes</note> with his back broken and a piece of wood fitted between his teeth. His jaws and throat were swollen because (as was later reported to them) they had thrust vipers into his mouth to wound him with their bites. He was suspended facing the sun, with a silver basin placed beneath his mouth to receive the liquid dripping from him. With great amazement, they saw how that inhuman Jew concocted a poison so lethal that it could kill men by touch alone. It was said that the Jew sold this poison to merchants as a certain poisonous powder.

A preparation of poison similar to this was related to me by a certain Papal Pharmacist <term>Pharmacopœus: a preparer of medicines or drugs</term> at Avignon, and since that time, I have had it confirmed by the testimony of others living in Rome. A certain Cardinal (he said), having made his mistress—who was adorned with red hair—pregnant, buried her in the earth up to her breasts after she had given birth to the infant. He applied two vipers (or as a German reported, two hungry toads) to her breasts, whose poisonous bites severely infected her blood. This done, she was suspended facing the sun in the manner mentioned above and yielded a most lethal liquid, and furthermore, her milk was then turned into a poison <note>original: "busum", likely a corruption of "pus" or "toxicum"</note> beyond compare.

The reason why a more pernicious poison is extracted from a red-haired man is because such people are subject to Solar influences from their birth, and consequently are more liable to corruption and putrefaction. Whence it happens that their Spiritual Mummy <term>Mummia: in Paracelsian medicine, the vital force or "spirit" remaining in a body after death or trapped in its parts</term>, when contaminated by animal venom, is rendered exceedingly subtle, penetrating, and malicious after its fermentation and putrefaction. And although there remains in the infected Mummy a Sympathetic desire to be joined with its like, nevertheless, because it is infected and intoxicated by the Antipathetic spirit of the poisonous beast which now predominates over it, it cannot embrace its like in a Sympathetic manner. Instead, by an Antipathetic addition, it contaminates the spirit similar to itself, and thus that foreign and heterogeneous poison converts both these spirits into its own destructive nature.

There was a certain Hermit living near Aquitaine in Provence (whose fame was fresh at the time I lived there and was on everyone's lips) who, with a similar poisonous philter <term>philrro: a potion or charm, usually for love, but here used for harm</term>, infected that entire city with a most desperate plague, so that a great portion of the people of that city were deprived of life. During the height of this contagion, if the Hermit was called to anyone, it was in his power alone to heal them; for this reason, he acquired the name of the "Holy Hermit." For just as he touched the knockers or handles <note>original: "tudites sive Marcolos"</note> of the doors of the city houses with a certain poison, so that whoever knocked on the doors would be killed, so he carried an Antidote with him, with which he used to restore the contaminated to their former state of health. This diabolical man was finally detected and suffered the heaviest penalties for his merits; for after various tortures, he was finally reduced to ashes by fire.

By a similar craft or sorcery, the Plague was introduced not long ago into the city of Turin in Piedmont <note>original: "Turingæ Pedimontanæ"</note> by certain pestiferous persons—incarnate Devils, as it were—who also paid the penalty for their crime; for once discovered, their flesh was torn and plucked away with glowing hot pincers. So also, the plague was ignited for certain merchants by a certain poisonous powder from Milan. From these things it is clear that by such wicked and impious inventions, the internal spirits of men have been corrupted, and the external air remains in some way polluted by the poison.

Nor should this appear foreign to a true Naturalist or a worthy Philosopher, since it is proven by experience that the South Wind <note>original: "statu Austri"</note> reduces healthy air into a corrupt and contagious disposition, and that air which was pure and unpolluted is now defiled and rendered poisonous by the breath of a person suffering from the plague, or by the breath of a pestilential Carbuncle or Anthrax <note>original: "Anthracis"; referring to the sores of the plague</note>. And that air so corrupted simultaneously corrupts the healthy air near it. It must be observed that the spirit of the Mummy easily infects the spirit of a healthy man at a considerable distance in persons tainted by plague, smallpox, measles, consumption <note>original: "Phthisi"</note>, or Ophthalmia. In the same way, the spirits of the leper, the epileptic, and those with the French Disease <note>original: "morbi Gallici"; a common historical term for Syphilis</note> are accustomed to do this through immediate contact. We shall find that even that which was healthily created in man has now become contaminated and poisonous through evil arrangement.

What then shall I say? Should we conclude from this that we should abandon or desert our nature because it is sometimes contaminated by evil and rendered lethal to us? Or should we judge human nature to be abominable and to be shrunk from by the Light itself, because sorcerers and enchanters (with the Devil teaching them) are accustomed to use flesh, hair, nails, excrement, blood, and even the Mummy itself—both corporal and spiritual—to perpetrate their incantations, philters, and sorceries? That this is so, we find not only by the testimony of History but also confirmed by the daily practice of truth. For Apuleius relates how his friend Fotis <note>original: "Fosis"</note> was used by a mistress (who was an enchantress of philters and...)

Should therefore, for that reason, the **magnetic effect** of human nature, or its **Spiritual Mummy** and similar things in man, be held as diabolical and damnable, because their mystery is revealed in an evil sense to sorcerers by the Devil, and their secret property is converted to an impious and least Christian use? Or is the **air** to be refused and rejected by us because it can be corrupted in most ruinous ways and modes and converted into lethal poison? Or is **fire** to be excluded from human society and held as damnable because, when badly applied, it is known to destroy and consume? When, on the contrary, if it be rightly applied, it brings nourishment and comfort to those standing by. If by the contamination or change of one Mummy into a contagious or poisonous disposition, another healthy one is infected—just as we see one infected with the **plague** affect another at a distance, and one house set on fire kindle another, even though they are not touching—should, I say, for this reason the use of either air or fire be banished into exile from human society? Or is the **fire of God** descending from heaven to be abhorred because **Satan** made use of it in a destructive sense, namely to consume the possessions of **Job**? Or is it to be said that the hidden property of the Spiritual Mummy, and the wonderful efficacy of the human Spirit in healthful and pious uses, is therefore to be rejected because it can, by corrupting, be converted into a poisonous disposition? Or is a good sword, ordained for the protection of the body, to be rejected or broken because a wicked man killed a good man with it? A good thing badly applied can bring harm. In exactly a similar way, if we descend from the animal sphere to the vegetable and mineral, we shall perceive that the famous enchantress **Medea** made special use in her incantations (as is also handed down concerning other sorcerers and necromancers) of herbs, stones, and minerals, without whose natural help neither she nor her Demon (who revealed their secret virtues and effects to her) could perform anything in their art to perpetrate their iniquitous desires. And for that reason (as we gather from **Ovid**) she herself traversed the high peaks of **Mount Oeta** to collect herbs serving her purpose there. There are very many magicians who, by the hidden property and virtue of stones revealed to them by the Devil, produce their evil-magic effects, even though they [claim] the influences of the Stars, which...

...they attribute powers to those stones, yet they are utterly ignorant of the times for collecting them and the methods of preparation required to produce such effects. For example, there was a certain sorceress <note>original: "venefica saga"</note> in Scotland who, during her examination, confessed that by a certain hidden property of a stone—which had been taken from her at that time—she was able to resolve any question asked of her. For she said that if the matter sought were true, the stone would immediately emit sweat; but if it were false, then no sweat would appear. She also said that this stone revealed many things to her by changing from color to color. Finally, when several bystanders desired to see an experiment of this matter, she replied that she would willingly do it, provided they would grant her that stone of hers. But they, fearing lest by its help she might escape from their hands, utterly denied her this request. This event took place at Queensferry in Scotland.

Others are instructed by the Devil to choose a certain metal and prepare it under a suitable constellation, engraving upon it the Characters of the Star to which it is subject, and describing the name of the Angel or Intelligence <note>A spiritual being believed in Renaissance philosophy to govern the movements of celestial bodies.</note> who is the Mistress of that Star. They attempt this especially at that time when that Star is stronger and more powerful in the heavens and more free from the impediments of other planets; and then they find that such metallic plates are quite effective in magical operation.

What then? Because the Devil knows the virtues and properties of natural things and is powerful enough to instruct his ministers in their evil use, does it therefore follow that Adam, Solomon, and the Wise Men coming from the East <note>The Magi of the Nativity story.</note>, as well as many other good and pious men, were ignorant of such virtues of natural simples <note>Medicinal herbs or minerals.</note>, the times of their selection and collection, and the modes of their application for a good and lawful purpose? Indeed, even if a just occasion presents itself in the contrary sense, and that without transgression of the limits of nature or lawful Magic—since the true subject of that operation is the Spirit of Wisdom, which is the basis or foundation of natural Philosophy—what do we make of the manner in which Moses used the scattering of those ashes, which produced the Egyptian ulcers <note>A reference to the ten plagues of Egypt.</note> to the astonishment of the inhabitants?

But others will reply and say that this was effected in a supernatural manner. Yet I would wish them to look into the hidden secrets and mysteries of the natures of animals, vegetables, and minerals, which are so wonderful; they will find that these things were naturally contained within them, setting aside all suspicion of Diabolical commerce. Is that reverend Father, Albertus Magnus <note>A 13th-century bishop and philosopher famed for his scientific and alchemical writings.</note>, to be considered a Black Magician <note>original: "Cacomago"</note> because he uncovered the abstruse, hidden, and mystical virtues of animals, vegetables, and stones? (Hermes, Plato, and other most profound Philosophers did the same.) Or should these men be numbered among the allies of the Devil because they knew the times or hours of collection and the mode of their preparation? Not at all, by Hercules! For they received these secrets from the tradition of the Philosophers or profound wise men, such as Adam, Solomon, Hermes, and other such true Magi, who left such mysteries to the world through Cabalistic tradition from age to age.

Was there not a wonderful property in the ring of Gyges <note>A mythical ring mentioned by Plato that granted invisibility.</note> which sometimes rendered him invisible? And yet the men of this world, blinded by ignorance, wish for such effects in creatures to proceed from the Devil, and not from the miraculous operation of the Divine Word. Whereby they seem to deprive the Omnipotent Spirit of God of His honor, even though Solomon confesses in open words that he received all secrets—the times of selection, the mystical natures of the Stars, the hidden virtues and properties of animals, plants, roots, and all other things, both hidden and manifest—from the Spirit of Wisdom alone; whence he concludes that discourse with these words: *For Wisdom, the worker of all things, taught me.* <margin>Wisdom 7.</margin> By which words he seems to infer: First, that the Spirit of Wisdom detects and opens to man the abstruse Mysteries of true Philosophy, which consist in the knowledge and revelation of natural virtues, both in the higher and lower realms. Secondly, that it is this same spirit who implanted such virtues in animals, vegetables, and minerals from below, and works through those mediums in all things.

Since this is so, what, I pray, can the Devil do in creating essential virtues for the perpetration of his stratagems or crimes more than man himself? Since man is a rational creature just as the Devil is? Or why should we attribute to him those things which, in truth, belong to the Spirit creating and operating all things in the internal creature? If it be man's part to ascribe the iniquity of any action to the Devil—who instigates man to evil and shows him the way to execute his evil and wicked wills—this indeed rightly pertains to the Devil himself, seeing as he was created to destroy (as the Prophet Isaiah says), and for the fulfillment of this office of his, the creatures created by God are put to use. For he employed the use of God's celestial fire to destroy the beasts of Job, to overturn the house, to destroy his sons, and to corrupt the air so that he might strike the Israelites with a plague. Nor indeed was it ever observed that he could do anything by himself against man, except by tempting and seducing the human Spirit and deluding the imagination of man with prestigious portents. But it is always observed that, either through the evil use of creatures, he destroys the bodies of mortals or renders them unhealthy and diseased. For by such natural Antipathizing <note>The concept that certain natural substances have an inherent "dislike" or opposing force to others.</note> ways and means—that is, through creatures which are by nature and condition...

<margin>Nicolas Rémy, *On Demonolatry*, Book 1.</margin>

For example, **Claude Thuringia**, on May 9, 1581, confessed that powders of a triple condition had been delivered to her by the Devil, which were even distinct in color: For (they say) that **black powder** kills by sprinkling it over food, or by rubbing the body with it, or by sprinkling it over clothing; but that of a **reddish color** produces diseases and infirmities; while the **white powder** is accustomed to cure those diseases which the red one produced. And **Odilla Boncourt**, examined on January 18, 1586, said that it was the custom for sorcerers of her order and condition to scatter a certain powder in the path through which those they pursued with hatred would travel. And **Françoise Périne** confessed on November 4, 1588, that a certain herb was delivered to her by the Devil to be placed in the path through which Riberianus would walk (because he had stolen her pears), by whose virulence he immediately fell sick. **François Follers**, **Margarita Watny**, and **Jacobit Equine** confessed on January 15, 1584, that they had ointments with which they smeared rods and whips; so much so, that if they touched only the garment of someone with them, it was necessary that the person die shortly after. They also said that if they anointed their hands with this **Magical ointment**, and if they touched the clothes of anyone, they would die within a few days. 

And from these examples you can see how the Devil truly does not know how to work evil except by poisons taken from creatures: for nothing of truth can come from him alone, but mere delusions and deceptive apparitions—namely, those things which are seen and yet in the effect of the reality are nothing more than a painted image compared to a true substance. And therefore, I would not wish the ministers of the Devil to boast that such wonders in nature come from the Devil's own invention or his act alone: For **true Alchemists** testify from their own experience and practice that their matter, when it remains in **putrefaction** <note>the 'black' stage of alchemy, or *nigredo*</note> and acquires a very black color, is more poisonous than a **Tyrian Serpent** <note>original: "Tyreo Serpente," a type of viper often cited in medical lore for its extreme toxicity</note>, and consequently kills suddenly; wherefore they warn the operators to beware of its fumes. But truly, when it appears in the cooking between redness and whiteness, it keeps the sufferer between death and health, and therefore reduces him to a diseased state; but in the act of its **whiteness**, which signifies perfection in maturity, it cures infirmities and prevents that malice which the black powder induced; so that

<column-break/>

it may be seen that the Devil cannot elicit more from the mysteries of nature than has been given to the human race to know. Again, regarding the scattering of such deadly powder through the streets of **Milan**, it is recorded that this happened in the year 1629. As for the lethal ointment which is accustomed to kill by touch alone, this was composed by the **Jew and the Cardinals** previously mentioned, so that they might violate the creatures of God just as much as the Devils do. And again, this was carried out in an impious manner by a **Hermit**, who infected the door-knockers with them (as was said), and he even had his own **Antidote** <term>Alexipharmacum: a preservative or remedy against poison</term> with him, just like the Devil and his Evil-Magician disciples. 

From these things, therefore, you can see that a man endowed with an impious mind or soul, and inclined to harm the good creatures of God, is just as prone as the Devil to turn herbs, animals, and minerals away from that true sense for which they were created by God—namely, for human benefit. Wherefore he may rightly be numbered among the Devils, and distinguished by the name of an **incarnate Devil**, because he himself, clothed in flesh and bone, finds many ways of destroying and killing with poison without the help of the Devil; no differently than the spiritual Devil, who is destitute of flesh and bone.

I conclude, therefore, that there is great absurdity and madness in worldly unbelievers to hold the hidden and secret wonders of God in his creatures with such temerity and audacity as the inventions and actions of the Devil, and to publish them to the world, even if their effects are ruinous to us—and much more so when they are good and health-giving, as is that **Weapon Salve** <note>original: "unguenti armarij," a controversial 17th-century remedy believed to heal a wound by anointing the weapon that caused it</note>. For it is known not only to God himself, but also to men enjoying true understanding, that whether it be an animal, vegetable, or mineral creature, it produces unhealthy and mournful effects through **abuse**, yet those same things are good in their due and appropriate faculty, which was originally ordained by God for the benefit and health of the human race. For God created all creatures good, and consequently for good uses: But it is the malice of the Devil which diverts them from the purpose ordained by the Creator, according to that saying of **Solomon**.

<margin>Wisdom 1. Wisdom 2:24.</margin>

> God created all things that they might exist, and he made the nations of the earth healthy, and there is no medicine of destruction in them, nor is there a kingdom of the underworld upon the earth; and he created man to be undying and made him in the image of his own likeness, but by the envy of the Devil death entered into the world, etc. <note>A translation of the Latin Vulgate text of the Book of Wisdom.</note>

...began to reign in the world, and evil, at its first entry or threshold into the world after the Fall, began to oppose itself to goodness and virtue; and in that primordial practice or conflict, injustice and vice prevailed against justice and virtue. Here, therefore, we can see, in the beginning of all things, how the Devil or the serpent laid the foundation of all evil by means of a natural thing—namely, the apple. And then, with a wooden club, the unjust **Cain** killed his just brother **Abel**; while on the other hand and in an opposite sense, this wood, in the form of a cross (evidencing that opposition which was made in this world between good and evil), was the instrument of His death, without which there was no certainty of salvation or redemption.

From these things, therefore, we observe that all hidden operations proceed from a power hidden in natural things or creatures, which was revealed by the Divine Spirit of God to the human race, just as it was grasped by the sharp observation of **Satan**. To good men, I say, it was revealed by the good Spirit of God for doing good and resisting evil. For, unless the wicked disposition of a creature is known, an **antidote** <term>alexipharmacon: a medicine used to ward off poison or infection</term> for its cure can hardly be obtained. Yet these things are also sometimes revealed to the wicked by the Devil for doing harm and executing iniquity. I shall now enumerate some of the hidden virtues in the three kingdoms of composite creatures: namely, the animal, vegetable, and mineral. First, then, in the animal kingdom, the owl is said by **Albertus Magnus** <note>a 13th-century philosopher and theologian known for his writings on the natural world</note> to contain many virtues within itself:

> For, he says, if its heart and right foot are placed upon a sleeping man, he will immediately reveal in his sleep whatever he has done, or whatever you shall ask of him;

And he says this was found to be true by certain of his brothers. And again, if these same parts are placed under one's armpit, no dog will dare to bark at him. Also, the blood of a he-goat is said to render glass not only malleable but also soft, like dough, provided the glass is boiled in it with vinegar; so much so, that if it is thrown against a wall, it will not break. And if someone makes an ointment from the same composition and smears his face with it, terrible things will appear to him. And if a portion of that composition is placed on a fire, and someone is present who suffers from **the falling sickness** <term>Epilepsia: a historical term for epilepsy</term>, and a **magnet** <note>lodestone</note> touches him, he will suddenly fall into an epileptic fit as if dead; but if cold water is given to him to drink, he will immediately rise again. These are his words. Furthermore, he says that if a candle is smeared with the blood of a camel, all the men in that place will appear to have the heads of camels. And so he proceeds in that history of his with descriptions of those wonders which are performed by the hidden properties of beasts, vegetables,

<column-break/>

and stones. If **Mr. Foster** <note>William Foster, a contemporary critic of the author who accused him of practicing witchcraft</note> with his companions replies and says that all these things are nothing but lies, I answer that a most learned philosopher and a theologian celebrated in fame was their author, who passed these things down on his own faith. And no doubt (if he were still among the living) he would affirm that they ought first to learn and understand the true **hours of election** <note>astrologically favorable times for gathering materials</note> in which those simple ingredients ought to be gathered, and also to know the stars which have dominion over them, along with the times of their greater strength and exaltation in the heavens. As for what concerns me, I confess that I am not ignorant of the wonderful secrets in man and beasts, for all of which the **Peripatetics** <term>followers of Aristotle’s philosophy</term> can give no sufficient reason at all. For example: that the dried intestines of a pike-fish powerfully provoke urine; that **the falling sickness** can be cured by the suction or attraction of blood from the severed nose of a **mole**, and that after swallowing that blood the patient will be exceedingly sick, just as we are taught by the experience of several people, and among the rest, by a certain most noble woman of the county of **Kent**. Also, that a **mole** burned and reduced to powder has a certain hidden power to expel the pain of **colic**. That the heart and liver of a frog is a medicine appropriated for the cure of epilepsy. That the shed skins of snakes expel the fetus in childbirth. That menstrual blood drunk by a woman induces leprosy. That a burnt toad stops blood flowing beyond measure; and even a live spider, if only it is applied to the nostrils. These things I, with many others, have experienced.

As for other hidden virtues of stones, metals, herbs, and animals, the true disciples and imitators of **Solomon**—**Hermes**, **Plato**, **Thabit ibn Qurra**, **Albertus Magnus**, **Dioscorides**, and others—teach them to us abundantly. All of whom, without a doubt, would not seem so foolish or void of truth and frivolous as to publish such great lies or such impossibilities to the world, nor would they falsely assert that those things had been brought to a conclusion in their own knowledge. To do so would be to lose, in such a stupid manner, that reputation among worldlings which they had earned for themselves by their remarkable wisdom. But now I shall betake myself to the practice of this our full business—namely, to that **Sympathetic** and **Antipathetic** relationship which exists between the various types of **Mummies** <note>medicinal substances or "vital spirits" extracted from the human body</note> of the human body, and the ocular demonstration produced by the property of the **Magnet**. And it is in my mind to prove to you, by demonstrating in this last book, more than anyone else has ever performed to this very day.

I have recounted to you in my preceding discourse, and proved by sufficient demonstration, that the Spiritual Christ, or the Divine Word, or eternal wisdom, is the true Basis or foundation of essential Philosophy; seeing that he is the secure and never-failing Cornerstone, in whom and upon whom the entire creation consists and is built up, insofar as life exists in him, and that life is that essential Light which gives life to all things, and consequently works all in all, as Scripture testifies in express words. For, if the Spirit of the Lord imparts life and inspiration and all things of life to the creature: And again, if that Spirit fills the world, and is within every single thing of this world, as Solomon writes; then it is necessary that we recognize that the central Spirit of any specific thing is that Divinity, in which the essential root of all Magnetic attraction and Antipathetic expulsion consists: For, since he himself is that Universal <note>original: "Catholicus," here meaning all-encompassing or universal rather than a specific denomination</note> love, which imparts itself to every particular existence, and assigns action and motion to it, by which it may entice a nature similar to itself toward itself, for the sake of nourishment, assistance, and consolation, so indeed he renders the organ in which he works strong and valid enough to expel and drive away such emanations which disagree with it either in order, quality, or essence, or which oppose its specific existence and conservation, or endeavor to inflict some harm. Therefore, for that reason, this Spirit endowed the creature with a double affection, namely, a concupiscible desire <note>the faculty of "wanting" or "desiring" what is perceived as good</note> and an irascible hatred <note>the faculty of "resisting" or "fighting" what is perceived as bad</note>, the former of which rejoices with and is accustomed to sympathize with its like, and therefore entices and attracts that to itself for its assistance and consolation; the latter, through a hateful or Antipathetic gaze, avoids and expels that which is opposite or harmful to it in nature. And this is the act of that Wisdom creating and sustaining all things, which created every creature with a certain successive preservation, which it attracts from its like so that it may exist in this world, and consequently granted it also the irascible faculty, so that it might fortify and defend itself from things contrary to it in nature: By which we can see how this Spirit, giving life to all things, governs with a hand that is by no means sparing; to such an extent that, although he created all things through opposition—namely light and darkness, and therefore in human respect good and evil—he nevertheless ordained and disposed that any individual should be endowed with the irascible faculty, and with Antipathetic hatred for avoiding and fleeing from evil, that is, [evil] being adverse to it either in order, or nature, or both, until that time be fulfilled in which, after his exaltation, he shall have cleared away all contrariety and discord from both worlds through the establishment of a firm union: Which even Saint <note>original: "D." for Divus, a traditional title for saints</note> Paul seems to confirm thus: *When he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power, it is necessary for him to reign until he has put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death, for he has put all things under his feet. But when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him who put all things under him...*

### OF THE SECOND SECTION, BOOK III. Member I.

<margin>John 12.</margin> ...all things to Him, so that God may be all in all, etc. This universal <note>original: "Catholica," here meaning all-encompassing or universal</note> Magnetic power is recognized by the Spirit, in Christ, from these words: *If I be lifted up from the earth, I will draw all things to myself,* etc. <note>Referring to John 12:32</note>. It is as if he had said: I, by my attractive and Magnetic power and union, shall lead all things back into my union and identity; that is, I shall graft them into my own nature. <margin>Revelation</margin> *Behold* (says the Text elsewhere) *I make all things new,* etc. <note>Revelation 21:5</note>. By these words it is clear that, just as in the beginning all things arose from the one—insofar as they were implicitly contained within it—and were then afterwards, in their explicit existence, held under two contrary Principles: so indeed in the end all things held under discordant Principles shall be led back to one and the same radical <note>meaning "at the root"</note> Principle. 

But for now, we are still subject to contrary Principles: For the whole world, along with the members of the same, is composed of strife and concord, of enmity and friendship, of darkness and light, of good and evil; and for that reason, they exist under the protection of this one Divine Wisdom, which governs all things and strives to have victory over confusion and discord. This is so that at last peace and union, or a universal consensus, may be achieved in this world, and consequently, that all things may return into that Wisdom, live within her, and be united with her, who is the one and only Charity <note>Divine Love</note>. The creature itself has the power to bring about a symphonic agreement with its own kind, and conversely—as if by a certain irritable or <term>Antipathetic<gloss>a natural force of repulsion or "dislike" between substances</term> property—it either avoids its contrary or repels it with its greatest effort.

Now, truly, since this Spirit is within all things, and therefore in every specific thing, it follows consequently that it attracts <term>Sympathetically<gloss>through "sympathy," the natural tendency for like things to be drawn together</gloss></term> that which is preservative of its own nature and condition in any specific thing from the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms: and it expels <term>Antipathetically<gloss>through "antipathy," the natural force of rejection</gloss></term> from itself that which is harmful, hateful, and detestable, or which is contrary to its disposition. And so much for the summary of my preceding Theory of Sympathy and Antipathy. 

Now, indeed, I shall immerse myself for a little while in the practice of both, so that by this reasoning you may be more easily led to believe that such things as were previously put forward by us in Theory are effective. I will show that a real practice can be produced gently (contrary to the vain opinion of certain foolish people of this world), and that it is produced naturally—that is, without any <term>Cacomagical<gloss>From the Greek "kakos" (evil); refers to "black magic" or demonic sorcery</gloss></term> or Diabolical operation. I shall proceed, therefore, to my purpose, and so that I may move forward more Methodically, I shall distinguish this book into two different members: the first will treat of Sympathetic effects; the latter will briefly explain those Antipathetic outcomes which are brought forth Magnetically in the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms.

Since it is a matter worthy of observation among wise men that there is nothing in the celestial kingdom which does not have its likeness in the terrestrial realm, so indeed there is nothing in the mineral kingdom that does not enjoy its likeness in the vegetable kingdom. And again, the image of the Vegetable sphere—both in love and hate, or in attraction and avoidance, or in union and divorce—is to be found in the animal. But, since in the mineral kingdom nothing is found closer to the power of action and animal life than the Magnet stone <note>the lodestone</note> itself, insofar as it sensibly affects its likeness in iron, and pursues it with a desirable love, and greedily attracts it, and finally joins and unites itself with it in a wondrous manner like a male and female in the animal kingdom. For this reason, every likeness in the animal or vegetable kingdom which operates according to this mode—namely, in attracting its own like—is not wrongly called "Magnetic." 

Hence, Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a famous physician and alchemist who pioneered the use of minerals in medicine</note>, who was most highly skilled in such mysteries, when he mentions mystical "mummies" <term>Mummia: in Paracelsian medicine, this refers to the vital life-force or "balsam" inherent in a living body, which can be extracted or transplanted for healing</term>, both corporeal and spiritual, and also the active ways and modes of extracting them from both the living and the dead body, produces examples drawn from the Magnet stone and iron for the better instruction of his disciples, and even those whom he calls the "sons of art" <note>a traditional term for practitioners of alchemy and hermetic science</note>. For through these examples, he clearly denotes the mode of extracting such Mummies; and consequently, in his own way, he explains what the animal and microcosmic <term>Microcosm: "the little world," a term for a human being viewed as a reflection of the entire universe (the macrocosm)</term> Magnet is, by means of which the microcosmic Mummy is drawn out from its body. Namely, he explains that it is a certain corporeal thing or substance, as it is permitted to gather from his own words: *The spiritual Mummy* (he says) *does not work; except through corporeal means.* <note>original: "Mummia Spiritualis non operatur; Nisi per corporalia media"</note> By which he argues for the corporeal modes, or those Magnetic bodies, which are accustomed to extract this Mummy from the body of a living animal, and cause it to work both at home through immediate contact, and from elsewhere at a distance; indeed, even at an unknown

<column-break/>

interval, and that by means of a proper transplantation. He, therefore, who is wise and deep in the mysteries of nature, and to whom sympathetic concordance, hidden properties, nature, virtue, and the origin of the Magnet and iron are well known, will undoubtedly recognize that these examples can be most aptly applied to man. For through them, one can very easily discern the microcosmic Magnet, and understand the reason for the extraction of the spiritual Mummy from man, and at the same time conceive of its use and purpose destined for human health. Therefore, so that these matters may be better expanded and explained to the reader, I think it worthwhile that I first strike the same chord of symphonic concordance concerning the nature and origin of the Magnet stone and iron, which I touched upon somewhat more fully in my preceding book, so that from there we may gather with greater ease who the microcosmic Magnets are.

As I revealed to you in chapter 3 of book 2 of this treatise, it was evident that the Magnet stone or Lodestone <note>original: "Calamita"</note> by no means proceeded from any natural origin, but rather from a monstrous birth or beginning. ### OF THE SECOND SECTION. BOOK II. Member II. ###

In their kinship (so to speak) or existence, only a light and easy transmutation was required to bind both into one body. And from this it follows that it retains a nature midway between metal and stone. Whence it may not inaptly be called a semi-transmuted **Saturnine Mercury** <note>In alchemy, 'Saturnine Mercury' refers to a heavy, cold, or 'leaden' state of the primal fluid matter</note>, into which, when **Martial Sulfur** <note>The fiery, active principle associated with iron (Mars)</note> enters as a metallic form, it holds it passively as its Mother; for it preserves the sulfur within itself and coagulates into a stony body, which is called the **lodestone**, or **Magnet stone**. 

But, since every Spirit desires and seeks to be nourished by that which is closer and more similar to its own nature—and this nature and Spirit is found chiefly in iron—it is observed that iron and Steel <note>original: "Chalybem"</note> of the most perfect kind come from the same mine or matrix, namely from the magnetic body. We must believe, from this consideration, that the Martial and Saturnine Spirit of the Magnet attracts the iron body to itself from its own center, and sends out its formal rays, as if extracting its spiritual nourishment from it. 

But, because the iron body will not so quickly leave its internal Spirit, it follows that it is attracted to the Magnet together with its Spirit. (For we are taught by experience that the Magnet is nourished by the Spirits of iron and is increased in its vigor). And again, the iron itself, finding Spirits similar to itself in the Magnet, likewise desires an equal union, so that it might become a participant; and the conjunction or union made between them is no different than that between a male and female. 

But, because the Magnet is fuller of stony Saturnine Mercury than the iron—which is more cleaned and purified from that superfluous matter by the power of fire, and consequently approaches closer to the nature of the male—therefore, it does not flee toward the Magnet as greedily as the Magnet flees toward it. For it is an old and well-confirmed axiom that **matter desires and seeks form**, and allures and embraces it as greedily as a female is accustomed to do a male. 

Indeed, that iron holds the place of the male is clear in this: it adds virtue and strength to the Magnet. For if the pole of a Magnet is "armed" with Steel or iron, it animates it far beyond its own nature; for this is the reason that the stone attracts a far heavier weight of iron to itself than it could have achieved without its iron attachment. 

This, therefore, being rightly considered, we can gather with greater ease what sort of thing and of what condition that **Microcosmic Magnet** <note>the 'small-world' magnet, referring to a substance derived from the human body</note> ought to be, which can extract the Spirit or **Spiritual Mummy** <note>In Paracelsian medicine, the 'mummy' is a vital essence or balsam that carries the life-force and can be used to heal or transfer disease</note> of the microcosm without any harm, detriment, or weakness to the body. If, therefore, we wish to undertake this work worthy of admiration, it is necessary that we do this with a **Corporeal Magnet** extracted from a living man,

<column-break/>

whose production and generation must in every respect agree with that earthly and mineral magnet of the microcosm, of which we made ample mention before. Indeed, I have not proposed to name it openly in this place, but rather to suggest it through circumstances alone, so that in this way it may be perceived by those worthy of virtue and honesty and skilled in true Philosophy, and hidden from the crowd of unworthy, malicious, and dull-witted people. 

For, just as great utility for human health can be brought about by means of this thing, so also, on the other hand, its powers could be used by a malevolent mind to produce many evils and perpetrate crimes not tolerable in a republic. It will suffice, therefore, for the Wise to understand that it is a certain thing, extracted from the body without violence, which has an earthy, mercurial, and Saturnine existence, changed or animated by a Martial (or sulfurous and choleric) form, like the mineral Magnet. After due preparation, it will have the specific virtue of extracting the **Spiritual Mummy**—whether healthy or infected—from the microcosmic body, which can then afterwards be transferred or transplanted to a distance from the patient.

I would wish, however, that every intelligent Philosopher know that the Magnetic nature of all things, both **Antipathetic** <note>repelling or 'against feeling'</note> and **Sympathetic** <note>attracting or 'with feeling'</note>, consists solely in the Sulfurous virtue of the vital spirits. These spirits, by reason of their "incarceration," are apt or ready to attract their like to their center from the circumference through their own contraction. 

Thus indeed, the animal, vegetable, and mineral subject—which is the immediate receptacle of the Sulfurous Spirit—attracts its like to the circumference by the power of the act of the enclosed Spirits, by reason of its pure Saturnine-Mercurial earth. By this means, they flourish both in the air and in their volatile salt, which is condensed like snow and frost in a certain Saturnine and **Boreal** <note>Northern/Cold</note> condition, within their ethereal and heavenly fire by which they live. 

And again, the Sulfurous Spirit flies back, or reflects its rays into its central salt, after it has emanated from the center to the circumference. This happens by reason of "Boreal accidents"—namely, external cold—as appears in the fiery or heavenly seeds of the air enclosed in our experimental instrument <note>likely referring to a thermoscope or weather-glass</note>. Indeed, it contracts with the blowing North wind <note>original: "Borea"</note> because the Spirit of Sulfur (or heavenly fire) within it, once expanded by heat, now avoids the assault of the cold opposite to its nature, recollecting itself into the center of the enclosed air and wrapping itself as if in an airy cloud, so that it may be better fortified from the inclemency of the cold. For (as will be shown hereafter in a certain Magnetic demonstration) the **Sulfurous equator** is greatly opposed to the cold **Mercurial poles**. Even in the human body, while a certain Boreal or numbing fear seizes it...

### OF THE SECOND SECTION, BOOK III. Member I. ###

We must hold it as an axiom <note>original: "Pro axiomate"; a self-evident truth or established principle</note> in general philosophy that what is corrupted takes on the nature of the corrupter: For example, if a human cadaver is corrupted in the earth, it then changes and passes into the nature of the earth, and becomes useless for human health; indeed, it is rendered more destructive than constructive or healthy. Again, if the corruption occurs in water, then indeed the corrupted flesh or dead body, soaked in water, will acquire and take on a mucilaginous nature; and for that reason, it will be inconvenient and useless for the conservation of the vital spirits. Finally, by the immoderate violence of fire, the Spirits in the Mummial body <note>A body containing "Mummia," the vital balsamic essence of life</note> will be consumed and will expire. Now, the reason why these so-called "corporal Mummies" are unsuitable for the protection of health in such a state is because those three aforementioned elements so destroy and corrupt their body that they force its earth, water, and fire to return to their own raw matter. Thus, since earth and water are ordained to be the receptacles of the two Elements—namely fire and air—both of which can only be preserved in an uncorrupted body, it must necessarily follow that in the three aforementioned Mummies, those vivifying Spirits must fly away and vanish for lack of a natural body, which has now become corrupted, putrid, and consequently unnatural. Since, therefore, nothing is required in a true Mummia except that which is fit for the conservation of life—or rather, for the sake of life itself, or the Spirit, which is air, which is exiled and expelled by the three aforementioned Mummies—therefore nothing can be extracted from them except sickness, death, and destruction, and consequently Antipathetic <note>original: "Antipatheticos"; acting in opposition to the natural flow of life</note> effects. Thus, if a healthy body that has been killed or suffocated is corrupted under the earth or in water, it will not be suitable or proper for the healthy use of the human body. That same regard must be had for such bodies that die from some infirmity; and although these are not visibly corrupted by the three said external Elements, nevertheless it sometimes happens that some invisible, corruptible influence or impression is made or caused by the external Element upon the internal. ->*An Experiment upon this.*<-

I myself took or selected a small portion of **Northern Mummia** <note>original: "Mummiæ Borealis"; referring to the "cold" or "dead" essence associated with the North</note>, namely the flesh of a hanged man, in which the central Mummia dwelt within its center. I applied it to a part of my body that was naturally closest in position to the applied Mummia. I bound it quite firmly in place for the whole night. I found it, at first contact, to be exceedingly cold and frozen, like **Northern ice**. However, after it had remained there for some time, I perceived—by the excitation of its frozen spirits (which were contracted "Boreal-wise" in the center) by the **equinoctial heat** <note>The "equinoctial" heat refers to the balanced, vital warmth of a living human body, contrasted with the "Boreal" cold of the corpse.</note> of my body—that something of my own living and vivifying Mummial spirits was greedily attracted. successive fits and starts, being sensibly and somewhat painfully pulled away and contracted through this **Magnetic operation**. Finally, after some time—specifically in the morning—I removed that physical Mummia of the dead man. I found it greatly altered both in smell and color, by reason of the quantity of my own spirits which it had attracted. I then prepared and reserved both of these spirits, thus gathered into one in a **Magnetic fashion**, for the healthy use of my body. But, because perhaps this assertion of mine will appear false to certain skeptics, I shall prove the possibility of every particular point or member of this matter with examples and demonstrations.

->*The first demonstration, made by relation to the nature of the microcosm.*<-

**I**n order to prove and demonstrate that the **Microcosmic spirit** <note>The "spirit of the Microcosm," meaning the vital spirit within a human being.</note> is fit to take on any polar impression, just like the **Macrocosmic air** <note>The atmosphere of the great world/universe.</note>, and is consequently more attractive and **Magnetic** in its Northern or cold property than in its equinoctial or Southern habit, we must look at our experimental machine or glass. This served for the universal demonstration in the first section of my Philosophy, in which we shall perceive that when the equinoctial winds blow—namely, either the South or East winds—then the air enclosed in the glass (and likewise the external universal air) is less Magnetic or attractive than when the Northern winds blow. And this is evidently proved therein because, when the said winds blow, the internal air (and consequently the external) is more fit to dilate itself, by reason of the emanation of those **sulfureous or celestial spirits** from the center to the circumference, which are inserted into every one of the said aerial spirits. For by such emanation, a certain expulsion occurs, or rather an expansion of the aerial parts through the **rarefaction** <note>The process of becoming less dense; thinning out.</note> of their body. Therefore, it may be observed in the instrument that while warm winds blow, the water does not rise in the neck of the glass beyond the mark or figure 1, but is rather driven further downward. On the contrary, when Northern winds blow, the air—which was dilated in the universal element and rendered more mobile—is condensed by contraction, and is reduced to immobile snow, ice, and
<column-break/>
frost; that is, it takes on an earthy condition. Thus we see that air in this state is wonderfully contractive. This is depicted to the life in the description of that instrument made in Book 1, Section 1 of this work. For the spirit enclosed in the glass attracts the heavy water (also enclosed) upward above the mark 1, and constrains and narrows itself into a smaller or more confined space. This becomes evident when snow and frost have long held dominion in the **Macrocosm**; at which time we shall observe the water to have climbed, against its own nature, as far as the mark 7 on the neck of the machine or glass. I have indicated the reason for this in the preceding pages: namely, because the hidden **sulfureous nature** of the spirit—which is the Sun, the driver of light and life—conveyed in its aerial spirit, avoids the assaults of the cold pursuing it. It remains against the actions of its enemy by having the air around its central seat drawn over it and condensed.

They greedily attract the spirits in the living body, as if imploring their help and assistance against their cold enemy, and they seem to rejoice in the possession of them, to be strengthened, and in a way, satisfied. ### 2. DEMONSTRATION.

That neither the Spirit in the body of the dead attracts dead Spirits, nor the Spirit in the body of the living attracts the living magnetically, except very slowly and moderately, is argued in this way from the observation of magnetic disposition.

## PROBLEM I.

The South Pole <note>original: "Polus Australis"</note> of one Magnet, by a certain natural hatred, avoids the south pole of another, and they will by no means allow themselves to be joined by the bonds of mutual love: but one, by a certain natural Antipathy, will flee the contact of the other. But truly, if the North Pole <note>original: "Polus Borealis"</note> of one is applied to the South Pole of the other, they will embrace each other with a natural inclination, and adhere to each other with a strong attraction.

->For example.<-

Take a Loadstone <term>Loadstone: a naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite, used here as a physical proof of the "sympathy" and "antipathy" found in nature.</term>, with its poles clearly distinguished and marked both south and North; place it in a small boat made of cork, or let it float in a basin or tub filled with water. Let the poles be correctly positioned relative to the horizontal plane, or at least not much raised or slanted. Hold the other stone in your hand, its poles also being known, so that its South Pole faces the North pole of the stone floating near it. For the floating stone follows the other stone immediately (provided it is within its strength and dominion), and it does not stop or leave until it sticks—unless, by withdrawing your hand, you cautiously avoid the union. Likewise, if [you oppose] the North pole of that...

<column-break/>

<margin>Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, book 1, chapter 5. <note>William Gilbert (1544–1603) was a physician to Elizabeth I and a pioneer in the study of magnetism.</note></margin>
<margin>Ridley, *Treatise on the Magnet*, 22 & 24. <note>Mark Ridley (1560–1624) was another prominent English magnetic philosopher.</note></margin>
<margin>Ridley, Folio 75.</margin>
...which you hold in your hand, you oppose to the south pole of the floating stone, they run together and mutually follow one another: for opposite poles entice their opposites. But if you oppose North to North and South to South in the same way, stone drives stone away, and just as a sailor turns a boat by pushing with an oar <note>original: "clavam"; literally a tiller or oar used for steering</note>, it veers away and sails in the opposite direction. It furrows the waters, nor does it stop or rest anywhere if the other pursues it. For stone arranges stone; one turns the other, reduces it to order, and leads it into its own harmonies. Thus says Gilbert in book 1, chapter 5 of *On the Magnet*, with whom Ridley agrees in chapters 22 and 24 of his magnetic treatise, by arranging two stones skillfully placed in their vessels or boats.

### 3. DEMONSTRATION.

Regarding the strengthening and increase of the Spirits in a Mummia that is as if dead and powerless, through contact with a Southern Mummia or living flesh, it is proven to be possible 
<column-break/>
in a magnetic manner by the following problematic demonstration. This teaches us that the Northern Magnet or aerial Mummia is raised up in its power by the Southern one.

### PROBLEM 2.

<margin>Gilbert, book 2, chapter 25, *On the Magnet*.</margin>
A stronger and larger magnet increases the strength of a weak and smaller magnet, and even of iron placed upon the pole of the larger magnet. If a smaller magnet is positioned there, its Northern pole will emerge stronger, and the needle <note>original: "obelus"; a small magnetic pointer or arrow used in experiments.</note> will cling to Pole A (the North) like an arrow, and not to Pole B at all. Also, when Pole A is in a straight line above the axis of both magnets joined 
<column-break/>
according to magnetic laws, it will lift the needle to a perpendicular position. This it cannot do if the Great Magnet is removed, because of the smaller magnet's own weaker powers. Thus says Gilbert in book 2, chapter 25 of *On the Magnet*, with whom Ridley <note>Mark Ridley (1560–1624), an English physician who wrote extensively on magnetical experiments.</note> seems to agree in chapter 23 of his magnetic treatise.

### APPLICATION.

In a clearly similar way, the Northern Mummia in dead flesh is excited and exalted in its strength by its conjunction with the southern nature or living flesh. For by this reasoning, it flees from and attracts new Spirits and a fuller 
<column-break/>
vigor to itself from the stronger Magnet, leaving the other weaker for that very reason. But this is declared more clearly by the following problem.

### PROBLEM 3.

If two Magnets armed with two iron or steel teeth are shown to you, of which one is stronger and the other much weaker, whose axes or diameters between the teeth are equal or of the same length: and if you then fit the 
<column-break/>
teeth of these together, coming from opposite poles, you will find that the stronger stone will seize and lift the weaker one. Furthermore, the weaker stone, united with the stronger and incorporated by that power which it receives from the stronger, will lift the stronger and larger one from the earth.

### *1. An experiment confirming the aforementioned proposition.*

A certain Italian nobleman had the misfortune of having his nose cut off and amputated. On the advice of his physician, he ordered a wound to be made in the arm of a certain servant or captive of his, to which wound he applied his own mutilated nose indirectly <note>Latin: *mediatè*; meaning the nose was joined to the servant's arm to establish a blood supply</note>, and bound it firmly to it, continuing in this state until a complete union was made between the flesh of the servant and his Master. After this, a portion or piece of the servant's flesh adhering to the nose was cut away and fashioned into the shape of a nose; meanwhile, the servant’s wound was healed by surgeons, and for his pain, patience, and merit, he was not only set free <note>Latin: *manu mittitur*; a formal legal term for manumission or the freeing of a slave</note> but also received a reward—namely, a good portion of money—and made his way toward Naples, which city was at least one hundred miles from his Master's house or residence. The adapted flesh of the nose flourished successfully, and it received its nourishment from the veins for as long as the servant lived. However, it happened that the freedman died in Naples, whereupon it occurred that the flesh adapted to the nose immediately began to wither and gradually become affected by gangrene, so much so that if the Master had not cut it off suddenly and without delay, he would undoubtedly have been in danger of death. This account of mine is confirmed as true by many learned and other trustworthy people; it is commonly publicized among the Italians and publicly upheld in his writings by a certain learned German.

By this story, therefore, we can see that as long as the two bodies which had made contact were of one and the same

<column-break/>

condition—namely, Southern <note>Latin: *Australis*; in this philosophy, "Southern" represents the vital, warm, and expansive quality of life</note> or equinoctial—they, however far removed from each other, would operate among themselves by a profound Spiritual Sympathy. That is, notwithstanding that great interval of distance, they were nonetheless present in Spirit, or they met one another by the aspect of sympathetic rays; and by this reasoning, the flesh of the one was Spiritually quickened by the living fountain of the other, just as a grain of wheat has its nourishment and is quickened by the application of solar rays to it. But when the Southern or Equinoctial property of the one (namely, the servant) was changed into a Northern <note>Latin: *Borealem*; representing the cold, contracting, and death-bringing quality</note>, dead, and cold nature, then the quickening Spirit within him ceased from its action—that is, it rested from its former application to the adapted flesh—and in place of that life-giving aspect, his Spirit, now reduced to a Northern condition, attracts and flees back to itself all that nature which its Southern disposition had imparted to it. This happens in exactly the same way that Northern frost in the world kills, as it were, and by its Northern and contractive faculty extracts the life of the grain, seed, plant, or herb. And for this reason, Gangrene (which is a Northern disease) occupied the portion of flesh adapted to the nose. Here, then, we see how the same Spirit, altered from a Southern or equinoctial to a Northern disposition, operates in a contrary, unnatural, and privative <note>Meaning a state of deprivation or lack of life</note> manner, and that secretly and from a distance.

But with an intellectual gaze, we can discern that this happens by the power of the living light in the air of a Sulphurous emanation <note>In the "chemical" philosophy of the time, "Sulphur" was the principle of heat and light</note>, by whose secret emission of rays the enclosed air is rarefied, and by that rarefaction it precipitates

But if that source becomes cold and icy, instead of the addition of the Southern action of life, it will produce a deadly and privative distraction; this is also very easily observed in my experimental instrument through the Spiritual concurrence, or rather the invisible and imperceptible continuity, which is established between both extremes in the instrument.

<margin>From a booklet of his printed in the German language.</margin>

### 3. An Experiment tested by the same Author.

That same Author seems to assert that he has cured a Hernia <note>A rupture or protrusion of an organ through its containing wall.</note> by this same method of transplantation, and his manner is of this kind. He takes a recently laid egg for the herniated person and with it, while still warm, rubs the gouty place <note>original: *locum podagricum*. The author likely means the site of the rupture, but uses the term for the general area of pain.</note>, but gently, and that quite often; Then he is accustomed to take away the bark of a Great tree and with a Great auger makes a hole, so Great that it is able to receive the egg into itself: Then he puts back the bark of the tree that was taken away, just as before, plugging the hole very well with it, then afterward smearing the place with cement or Tree-mud <note>A type of grafting wax used by early arborists.</note>. The whole business must be performed in the due order and time. He tells us that when the barks of the tree grow together and adhere to one another, at that time, even the hernia or rupture will be strengthened and the lips <note>The edges of the rupture or wound.</note> will be glued together; but, if it happens that the hernia is not cured in the space of one month, then he bores into another oak, and collects the fragments that fall while boring, and crushes them and encloses and sews them into a small bag, and applies it to the affected place for three days before the new moon, and then around the hour of the new moon into the hole—

<column-break/>

He also asserted to me that I would find the same effect if I had placed those waste products <note>original: *excrementa*</note> into the root of a Hazel tree (a hole having first been made), then afterward closing that hole with the bark of the same tree, and finally covering the spot with earth: He said on his faith, it had very often been experienced that, as that tree grew, so also the failing and languishing limb fared prosperously: But above all he warned me that I should observe the exact disposition of the heavens, for without it, this method of curing is found to be less effective.

—that this oak is too insufficient to strongly attract to itself Magnetically: And then he proceeds in this manner: He bores another hole in a second oak and keeps the fragments coming out of the hole during boring, and sews them into a small linen bag, which he then afterward applies to the painful place or the infected limb: And he undertakes this work for three days before the new moon, then in the very hour of the new moon he removes the bag from the affected place and includes it in the hole of the said tree and plugs it with a peg, as before, etc.

—of the oak he thrusts it, doing in all things as before. 
There are many other observations in that place as much in respect of the time, namely if the first increase of the Hernia was in the waxing or waning of the moon, all of which I leave here for the sake of brevity. 
Finally he says, that if the Hernia does not become consolidated by all this, then he bores a hole in an oak and places into it the nails and hairs of the hands and feet of the patient, and also the hairs of the private parts, then afterward plugging it, as has been said: For he affirms that when that hole shall be drawn together into one, then also the Hernia will be glued together: There also he shows the reason why sometimes he is forced to use more or fewer operations of that kind in that way of curing, according to the nature of the Hernia which he attempts to approach: Namely, in a beginning Hernia a single operation will prevail, but for long-standing ones more will be required: And he says that in this cure the time and the measure of the tree with the depth of the hole is to be especially considered.

### *3. Experimental demonstration.*

## 2. P R O P O S I T I O N.

A singular order—expressed both in the **Sympathy** and **Antipathy** of vegetable parts among themselves—is typically demonstrated by the relationship or regard held between them and the **Magnet**. By this, it is argued that the vegetable, the mineral, and consequently the animal kingdoms, observe one and the same Symphonic or Harmonic proportion, both in their orderly harmony and in their irregularity.

->Problem to confirm this proposition.<-

<margin>Gilbert, Book 3, chapter 6, *On the Magnet* <note>William Gilbert (1544–1603) was a pioneer in the study of magnetism</note></margin> In all magnetic things, whether they be vegetables, minerals, or consequently animals, nature always tends toward a fitting unity. ->*Demonstration from the mineral Magnet.*<-

Take an oblong <note>long and narrow</note> Magnet, and let it be C. D.

<image-desc>Two horizontal diagrams of cylindrical magnets. The first diagram (top) is labeled with points B, C, E, F, D, A, showing the cylinder split into two parts (B-C and D-A) with a gap (E-F).
