C. tends toward the Earth's North <note>original: *Boream*</note> B. and D. toward the South <note>original: *meridiem*</note> A. Divide this oblong stone in the middle between the two poles where the equator passes, namely between E. and F. Then E. will tend toward A. [South] and F. will tend toward B. [North]. For just as in the whole stone, so in the divided stone nature seeks these bodies; namely, the end E. fittingly and desirably meets and clings again with F. But E. never joins with D., nor F. with C. For then it would be necessary for C. to be turned against nature toward the South A., or D. toward the North B., which is foreign and inconsistent. Separate the stone at the cut and join D. to C., and they agree and combine perfectly; for D. tends to the South as before, and C. to the North. The parts E. and F., which were born together in the ore, are now greatly separated. For they do not flow together because of a similarity of material, but they receive their movement and inclination from their form. Thus the ends, whether joined or divided, tend magnetically in the same way toward the poles of the earth, in the first figure (whole) and the divided one, just as in the second figure, and the magnetic whole is perfected. In the second figure, F. E. flowed into one body, just as C. D. was originally created in its vein; and F. E. [turned] toward their own poles while floating on water. Thus, whether the ends of that stone are united or disjointed, they tend magnetically toward the poles of the earth in one single way, both in the figure of the whole stone and the divided one, as appears in the second example. And the magnetic meeting of F. E. into one body in the second figure will be so complete as if it were produced that way in its own vein.

If, when a breach of continuity <note>original: *continui solutione*; a medical term for a wound or cut</note> or wound has been made, a portion of the external or shed blood with its **Spirits** <note>In this context, "Spirits" refer to the vital, invisible gases or energies believed to carry life through the blood</note> is transferred to a suitable ointment—either by means of the weapon that caused it, or if a portion of the Spirits of that same blood (even without any blood being visible) penetrates into the weapon or into the depths of some other thing probing the wound—and if this is then transferred to a suitable ointment—that is, one whose composition is **Balsamic** <note>term: Balsamic (healing, soothing, and restorative like a natural resin)</note> and agreeable to the nature of the wounded creature—provided it is applied in a fitting order and, as it were, inserted and transplanted into it, then the ointment, thus animated by these Spirits, will immediately become **Magnetic**. These lively and **Southern** <note>term: Southern (original: *australes*); in magnetic theory of this era, the "Southern" pole represented active, radiating life-force</note> rays, gushing or shining forth from the wound, desire to animate and unite themselves—by means of the **Northern** <note>term: Northern (original: *Boreali*); the "Northern" pole represented the fixed, cool, or receptive principle</note> ointment, or rather by the attraction of the Spirits enclosed therein—after the Magnetic fashion. These Spirits, which were previously "transplanted" into the ointment, impart their **Balsamic** virtue to the Spirits in the wound (which were previously attracted Magnetically) through that same union or continuity. Thus, if the entire length of the weapon that made the wound is greased, covered, and defended from the cold, the person will find comfort and their pain will be mitigated. But, if a part of the ointment is scraped away with a knife or any other thing, or wiped off from the sword, axe, or other wounding weapon, a pain and a physical disturbance <note>original: *intemperies*</note> in the wound will be felt immediately afterward. Also, if the greased part of the weapon is kept moderately warm, the wound will behave in kind; but if the weapon itself is uncovered and kept in the cold air, then indeed it will happen that the wound will be tormented and affected by the cold.

### 4. A demonstration from iron.

<margin>In the same place.</margin>
This is proven in another way using a larger body: Let a long, polished iron rod (of the kind prepared for sails and window curtains) hang in balance by a thin silk thread. To one end of this rod, resting in the air, move a small, polished, oblong mass of iron to a suitable point at a distance of half a finger’s width. The balanced iron will turn itself toward the mass; if you withdraw your hand with the mass at the same speed in a circular path relative to the hanging balance, the end of the balanced iron follows and is turned in a circle.

## APPLICATION.

By these examples, therefore, it is made clear how two Spirits of similar disposition, or rather of one identity in nature, are suited and naturally disposed to desire and embrace their like. And this happens not only through contact but even at a distance—that is, where some space or interval of place is interposed between those two Magnetic bodies. Consequently, it is not the bodies that act (for they are divided from one another), but the formal Spirits <note>In early modern science, "formal spirits" refers to the invisible, active essence or "form" that gives a substance its specific properties.</note> within those bodies. These spirits, by a certain astral emanation, first look upon one another sympathetically and in a friendly manner, and then afterwards, through a single equal attraction, they embrace and, as it were, kiss one another. And therefore, it cannot seem foreign or impossible to wise men that the Blood-Spirits in an ointment, and those in a wounded person, are accustomed to meet and join across such a great distance as exists between the ointment and the wound. That is, they apply themselves to each other through a sympathetic gaze. For both of these Spirits are nothing but a single, indivisible, quintessential ray, no matter how much they are altered in their elemental properties—not unlike how air made by a North wind is seen to differ from that of a South wind, even though both of those airs in their existence are nothing but one essential and individual air.

As for the final branch of the aforementioned member, it argues indeed that the blood spirits can be imbibed by a wounding weapon; whence, according to this sort of axiom by Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), known as Paracelsus, was a Swiss physician who pioneered the use of chemicals and minerals in medicine and proposed the theory of "mummy" or vital force.</note>, the wounding part or portion of the weapon is made into a Magnet. ## 2. THEOREM.

It is then rightly said that a Magnet moves a Magnet, and that one of them disposes the other through their primary form <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, "form" is the essential nature or "soul" that makes a thing what it is.</note>, which it receives from the Stellar source: And therefore there was no absurdity in the wise Thales of Miletus <note>An ancient Greek philosopher (c. 624–546 BC) who famously claimed that magnets have souls because they can move iron.</note>, nor was there any madness in Scaliger <note>Julius Caesar Scaliger (1484–1558), a renowned Renaissance scholar.</note>, to assign a soul to the Magnet; since it is incited, directed, and moved circularly from a central and internal Principle.

### 1. A Problem confirming this Theorem.

If two Magnets were placed facing each other on the surface of the waters in their little boats <note>original: "navigijs"</note>, they do not immediately rush together, but first they turn toward each other, or the smaller obeys the larger by moving itself in a certain circular way, and finally when they are disposed according to nature, they run together: Thus says Gilbert <note>William Gilbert (1544–1603), author of the first great work on magnetism, *De Magnete*.</note> in Book 2, chapter 4.

That same effect will also appear between a Magnet and iron, as will be declared below.

## ADDITION.

And although someone might reply that this act in a Magnet with a Magnet, or in a Magnet with iron, seems to be determined by an external effect at a certain dimension <note>Meaning the power seems limited to a specific, measurable distance.</note> and consequently the words previously uttered by me do not yet contribute much to proving the indeterminate dimension of the emanation of Magnetic bodies: I respond, that the sensible act between Magnet and Magnet does not seem to argue this; For since those two heavy bodies have their evident motion only at such a distance, it does not follow that their Spirit cannot extend itself further or apply its rays further: For it is one thing to work sensibly through the violent attraction of a heavy mass, and another, that one form alone should be embraced, and concur with another in natural Harmony; and that alteration is precisely verified for those who are best versed in the properties of the Magnet by this following problem.

## 2. PROBLEM.

The sphere of virtue <note>original: "Orbis virtutis" — the field of influence surrounding a magnet.</note> extends wider than the sphere of any Magnetic motion; for a thing is made Magnetic at the furthest edge, even if it is not moved by the local motion which is caused when a Magnet is moved closer: For then the entire bodily mass will move toward it.

## 3. PROBLEM.

A Magnetically touched needle will look toward the North even from the equinoctial point <note>The Equator.</note>; Which indeed is a visible argument for the indeterminate extension of the virtue of the Magnetic stone.

### OF THE SECOND SECTION. BOOK III. Member I.

...if it is placed in a small boat <note>original: "cymbæ committatur"</note> so that it floats upon the water, [pointing] toward the North and South according to its poles; if (I say) a tiny fragment of the rod is broken off from its Northern end, that fragment will <column-break/> have its own poles, namely a Northern and a Southern one, just as its whole did: that is, the long rod from which it was taken.

### A P P L I C A T I O N.

From these things it is clear that if any portion or fragment of a Magnet or of iron possesses its own poles just as the whole does, then the **Spirit** <note>In this context, "Spirit" refers to a subtle, invisible substance that acts as the vehicle for natural forces like magnetism.</note> which is within them has its own relation or application to the pole star of the macrocosm <note>The "greater world" or the universe.</note>, and also regards the Southern power and the pole of the same: For, unless there were within it a spark of the **worldly soul** <note>The *Anima Mundi*, a philosophical concept of an intrinsic soul that enlivens all nature.</note>, which operates in it according to its tiny proportion just as it does in the greater world, it would be impossible for it to regard both poles with such exactness as experience testifies. And for this reason, just as the actions of the soul of the world are so universal <note>original: "Catholicæ"</note> that they cannot be confined within certain limits, so too are the Spiritual and Astral emanations or radiations of lower creatures.

## 5. P R O B L E M.

<margin>Gilbert, Book 1, Chapter 12</margin>
A straight iron rod six feet long and a finger thick (as before) is placed in perfect balance with a very thin and strong silk thread; the thread indeed ought to be woven in various ways, twisted from various silk strands and not by one simple path. Let it be in a small room with all doors and windows closed, lest the wind enter or the air of the chamber be moved in any way. It moves slowly until at last it comes to rest; as it settles, its ends point to the North and South, just as iron touched by a Magnet is accustomed to do in shadow-clocks <note>original: "Horologijs sciotericis," referring to sundials or instruments that use shadows to tell time.</note>, compasses, and the nautical box.

Furthermore, we shall find that a Magnet or any other thing excited by a Magnet, when placed in its little boats, will direct its gaze toward the needle in its vertical [plane], toward the North pole.

### C O N C L V S I O N.

It is therefore manifest that the **Spiritual** or formal extension of the Magnet's emanation, and also that of all other Magnetic bodies, is not to be confined within certain limits: insofar as it acts and applies its rays even to the seat and station of the pole star; and the Pole Star likewise, by its emitted influences, works in a reciprocal manner. It applies itself to, or gazes upon, the Magnet, and thus between those ascending rays and those descending rays a continued **Spiritual union** is made. For we discern with our eyes that both the Magnet and the iron, with great diligence and manifest **Sympathy** <note>The idea that objects with similar natures are naturally drawn to or affected by one another.</note>, gaze upon and are moved toward that star.

Therefore, these things being rightly weighed, I would wish one to consider how great that interval or space is which lies between the earth and the eighth sphere <note>In the geocentric model of the universe, the eighth sphere is the realm of the fixed stars.</note>; and without a doubt, he will perceive that it is as if infinite, or rather immeasurable. Consequently, the radiations made by a Magnetic body do not know how to terminate at some Fanciful and sensible boundary of activity (according to the imaginary opinion of certain fanciful philosophers).

But if such an act at such a distance—whether of the Pole Star or the Magnet—be denied by some, and if the opinion of **Fracastoro** <note>Girolamo Fracastoro (1478–1553), a scholar who proposed that magnets were attracted to "magnetic mountains" in the North rather than the stars.</note> and many other learned men be accepted and held as Authentic (which says that the Magnet and iron, and the needle touched by a Magnet, stretch toward the North by reason of the attraction of various Reefs consisting of Magnet-stone situated in the hyperborean mountains <note>Legendary mountains in the far North.</note>): if that opinion (I say) be established as true, yet even from it we can conclude that the act of the Magnet itself and the actual respect which Magnetic bodies have toward that [North] cannot be terminated by any certain limits. For even in that consideration, the radiations of such bodies will be observed to work together from the location of the Equator all the way to the Hyperborean reefs. But we have proved elsewhere that their opinion is false and vain. Now, however, we shall apply all this that has been said to our present purpose, namely the first article of this member.

### A P P L I C A T I O N.

The first and second problems teach us that there is such a celestial and Astral subtle Spirit in all magnetic bodies of the earth as there is in those celestial ones: and consequently, that the rays of any one of them can penetrate as far (even if that penetration cannot be discerned by the senses) as the rays of any star. By these things we can perceive that the celestial **Spirit** in man, which is of a purer and more subtle substance than that of the Magnet, is able to emit the rays of its virtue not only to that goal at which the Magnet aims, but even to the highest Throne of Divinity. Again, it is argued from this that the Spirit in transplanted blood is powerful enough to work upon a wound at any distance, and likewise that the radiant [Spirit] of a wound...

# DEMONSTRATION.

Now, it is demonstrated in various ways that the greatest attractive power comes from the North. First, if we suspend a long piece of iron by a thread (as was said before), the Northern part of the world will attract its extremity to itself, so that it looks directly toward the North and South.

<margin>Ridley, chapter 14.</margin>
Secondly, if an iron filament four fingers long is passed through a piece of cork, and is then excited by a Magnet and placed upon water, the <term>Pole Star</term> <note>original: "Stella Polaris"</note> will draw the end of the iron toward itself.

<margin>Ridley, chapter 17.</margin>
Thirdly, if a long piece of iron is forged in a North-South orientation and is placed so that it cools in that same position, it will then be animated and clothed with the power of the pole. If suspended in the air by a thread or placed on a small boat upon the water, it will move and be drawn toward the North, and <margin>Ridley, ibid.</margin> it will have a kind of <term>coition</term> <note>In 17th-century science, "coition" referred to the mutual attraction or "coming together" of magnetic bodies.</note> with the Northern

<column-break/>

Star.
Fourthly, if a long portion of clay or earth, recently fired, is allowed to cool toward the North and South, it will then receive magnetic power from the earth and the pole.

Fifthly, place two Magnets with their poles of the same name—namely, the North or South pole of each—at either end of a small piece of clay glowing white-hot from the fire. While it cools, each end will become of the same nature. <margin>Ridley.</margin>

Sixthly, let a portion of clay of an oblong shape be placed in the fire, and afterwards let it cool in a North-South orientation, and it will receive polar power. Following this, burn it again in the fire; the end that previously cooled toward the North, let it now cool toward the South, and it will be changed into a Southern nature, and the other into a Northern nature.

# APPLICATION.

From the first of these problems and experiments, it appears that the source of vigorous attraction is from the pole, because the property of Northern cold is to attract. Therefore, the <term>Sanguine Spirit</term> <note>The vital, airy essence found within the blood, believed by Fludd to carry the life force.</note>, by taking on a Northern nature, is rendered magnetic, just like the spirit in the clay or the iron.

I shall now proceed to demonstrate the effect which this Northern and Southern Spirit produce through their mutual encounter and union; just

<column-break/>

as we see the North and South poles, through their immediate encounter, bring forth the <term>Equinoctial</term> <note>The "Equinoctial" refers to the balance found at the equator, representing a temperate middle ground between the two poles.</note>, which is spring-like and temperate—that is, hot and moist, just like living blood. Thus, a middle nature, which participates in both extremes, is produced during the flowing together of their aspects or their application, which receives from one and communicates it to the other. These are my magnetic proofs:

Thus, it can cause any extreme nature to participate in the symptoms of the other, whether those symptoms be good and healthy, or malignant and painful.

There is a certain noble Earl, of no minor note among us English, and he is a wise, religious man of the highest reputation, who commonly used to cure jaundice <note>original: "icterum"</note> at a distance, sometimes (as he related to me) of 100 miles, and that only by means of the patient's urine being brought to him. And the method is this: he mixes the ashes of the ash tree <note>original: "fraxini"</note> with the patient's urine, and from that he makes a paste, and then into little balls, 3, 7, or 9 in number <note>odd numbers were traditionally believed to hold medicinal or magical potency</note>. And in the top of each of the said rounds, having made a hole, he places a filament of Saffron <note>original: "Croci"</note>, and so fills it up with the remainder of the urine. Then afterwards, he places or disposes these balls in some secret place where no one may disturb them: and immediately the jaundice in the patient—whether he is far away or near to the physician—will decrease. And this experiment has been proven in many hundreds of people, both poor and rich, and many of them were such that the regular doctors had despaired of them. Not only he himself, but also the daughters of a most noble Lady, who did good to many poor people for free for the sake of God's grace, affirm this to be true. And I can affirm this much: that being called to a Surgeon's wife in the year 1632, after other

<column-break/>

doctors had abandoned her, who was most foully infected with the said "bowed disease" <note>original: "morbo arquato," another term for jaundice, referring to the "rainbow" colors of the skin</note>, and had even used pharmacists’ drugs, but in vain: at her request, I sent her servant into the country with letters to the said noblewoman to implore her help. But in the meantime, while the urine was being sent, the said woman was persuaded by certain foolish old women that this was done by cunning and Magic. This so greatly disturbed her that she even treated her servant harshly upon his return. Hence, I dispatched a message immediately, requesting that her Ladyship destroy what she had caused to be done, because of the ingratitude of the said woman. She sent word back to me that she was willing to do so, but replied at the same time that it would be in vain; "For I will restore her to health now, let me do what I wish." And indeed, she recovered immediately. Similarly, there was a certain daughter of a noble Baron, and the wife of a most noble Knight, William Brooke, who was foully defiled by the said disease; and finding that the usual remedies in medicine contributed little or nothing to her, I sent her urine to the said noble Earl, who did what he could. ### *The Act of Transplanting the Spiritual Mummy.*

As far as the act or mode of transplantation is concerned, Paracelsus says that the extracted *Spiritual Mummy* does not work for health and preservation except through mineral, vegetable, and animal means: and therefore it is necessary that the *Spiritual Mummy*, attracted or extracted from the body by the power of the *Animal Magnet*, be introduced into a vegetable nature. We must, therefore, mix a small portion of this "soaked" *Magnet* with a certain proportion of the earth of that material, and in this composition sow the seeds of such herbs which are fit for expelling this or that disease, or for healing this or that poorly affected Principal part of the human body, or this or that infirm limb.

### *On the Use and Virtue of the Transplanted Mummy.*

Lastly, concerning the manner in which we ought to use this *transplanted Mummy* after it has been changed into a vegetable nature or condition, it should be known that:

If the disease is "humid" <note>In the humoral theory of medicine, diseases were classified by qualities: hot, cold, moist, or dry</note>, it is necessary that the herb be burned again along with the *Magnetic earth*. If the disease is more temperate—namely, between the extremes of water and fire—then hang the herb in the air or smoke to dry, and the disease will gradually fade away as the herb withers. Alternatively, if you give that herb or the fruit to be eaten by a beast that is of a stronger nature than the sick person, the beast will be infected by that disease, and the sick man will be freed.

If, however, the disease is "dry" and of a combustible nature, such as jaundice, *Phthisis* <term>Phthisis: A historical term for pulmonary tuberculosis or a wasting disease of the lungs</term>, etc., and one intends to cure it and expel it from the body, then take the herb with its *Magnetic earth* and throw it into running water, and the disease will fail and vanish little by little.

Similarly, if the *Spiritual Mummy* is extracted from a particular limb of a healthy man and preserved in its continuous vegetation; if, having taken its fruit, you transplant it into a solid oak, by this means the limb from which the *Mummy* was extracted will grow continually and be maintained in its natural and robust proportion of growth without defect.

Now, as to how this is possible in nature, I will briefly recount to you. Just as nature **Magnetically** affects and allures its like to itself, so indeed, if that "like" which it draws to itself is defiled by corruption, the said attracting spirit—however healthy it may be—quickly tastes of the *bittersweet* <note>original: "glycipicron"; a term used to describe something that seems attractive but contains hidden poison</note>, namely the poison. Thus, it is corrupted equally with that spirit which is of the same kind, in which the infection resides. It is suddenly forced to foster a conflicting dissension and **Antipathy**, and to receive it into its own Tabernacle. We see this, for example, in the healthy Spirit of an animal, which, thirsting for a similar spiritual celestial food that wanders secretly in the air to be refreshed by it, unexpectedly brings an enemy into itself—namely, a highly pestilential and corrupt air by which it is oppressed and inflamed with a putrid fire. Thus, it was not the desire or appetite of the healthy spirit to introduce that poison, but rather to introduce a spirit similar to itself which happened to be intoxicated. 

Furthermore, every spirit that is burdened by any **Antipathetic** and unnatural accident seeks to shake off the contentious Antipathy and resume that peaceful Sympathy which it enjoyed before. But finding itself too weak for this task, it is apt to cling to healthy and good Spirits for its own restoration; for a united force is stronger, and if many healthy Spirits of its own kind were joined to it, then it would more easily conquer and expel its Antipathetic adversary. Thus we also see that a bleary-eyed person, by casting out their contagious rays during recovery at a moderate distance, becomes a flame that ignites the healthy Spirit to which it is applied. For spiritual poisons are like the secret flames of a malignant fire. Therefore, just as Spirits are joined to one another in a certain union and are multiplied like oil added to oil, so the contagious flame increases and feeds equally upon both. It does not leave them until it has penetrated and gnawed even to their very vitals and poisoned them. And we must note that there is no poisonous Spirit that joins itself more quickly to another Spirit than one which is specific to it and of a homogenous nature. This is the reason why the Spirit of one man, infected by an epidemic, multiplies it so greatly, especially among his own kind; so much so that even that malignant infection, called *The Murrain* <note>A historical term for a plague or infectious disease affecting domestic animals, especially cattle or sheep</note>, rages

But if their words were to find a place among the wise, what, I ask, would become of the art of Solomon in Natural Magic? ...be it slow or at least weak: and so the Spiritual Mummia is equally corrupted and infected.

### An experiment to confirm this.

Many and various proofs and arguments are given to establish these things; for when a corrupted Spiritual Mummia <note>original: *Mummia Spiritualis*; in Fludd’s philosophy, this is the subtle, magnetic life-force or "balsam" that carries the vital spirit through the air and body.</note> is carried in the air from someone infected by a pestilential fever or smallpox, that infected Mummia, since it is of the same nature <note>original: *homogenea*</note> as the Spirit of a healthy man, unites itself with it. In this regard, one embraces the other: but the healthy Mummiated Spirit, perceiving and, as it were, "tasting" the foreign <note>original: *heterogeneam*</note> or infected nature which clings to its own likeness, expels it more sluggishly and slowly, or resists it. This happens because it desires its own likeness and therefore attracts it sympathetically, and in turn

<column-break/>

[it is] cast out, and the other; and in this way Sympathy is converted into Antipathy.

[It] pursues its own unlikeness with hatred, and therefore expels it Antipathetically <note>By natural repulsion.</note> only slowly and sluggishly, which is why it is done in this manner. And this is the cause why an expulsive crisis <note>A sudden turning point in a disease where the body attempts to throw off the infection.</note> does not happen immediately after a poisonous infection is received; nor do sweats, nor hemorrhages (the eruption of blood from the nostrils), which are signs of resistance and of the expulsive faculty against contagious Antipathy, wish to appear suddenly. And this is accomplished sometimes by the victory of the healthy Spirits, and sometimes by their vain and failed efforts.

### 5. PROPOSITION.

The Spiritual Mummia <note>original: *Mummia Spiritualis*; the subtle, magnetic life-force or "balsam" that Fludd believed permeated all things.</note>, which is Sympathetic by nature, when directed toward an Antipathetic nature, is able to infect not only the surrounding air but even a denser medium—namely, liquids.

#### A demonstration confirming this.

The story which can confirm this is of this sort, regarding a certain Brewer: In the city of Canterbury in the County of Kent, there was a certain man of great note and of no small reputation in his skill for the making of ale <note>original: *alla*</note>. It happened many times, for a reason not at all understood, that the ale he made suddenly be-

<column-break/>

-came very bad, dead, and as if of no value. He complained to many of his friends about this matter, nor could he investigate the reason why he, who had at other times made ale praised by everyone, had now so evidently failed on various occasions? One day he was informed by an old woman that this could happen due to the foul breath <note>original: *halitu fetido*</note> of some of the servants engaged in the preparation and boiling, and that this was known from her experience. Therefore, having examined the servants working in the preparation of the Ale, he found one among the rest affected by a very foul breath and a contagious spirit; having paid his wages, he ordered him to leave. He began to make new ale again, and without any obstacle, he created good ale, and he continually had such good success while that corrupt breath was absent. After the space of a year, for the sake of experiment, he again took back that servant affected by the corrupt breath and employed him in the business of his craft as before; which being done, he perceived his ale reduced to its former [bad] state. Having thus become more certain and sure of this matter, he again dismissed that servant whose spirit was so deadly to his ale. This is known to many trustworthy people.

### APPLICATION.

If, therefore, that Spirit be so deadly to a foreign spirit that it can corrupt it from a distance, it was undoubtedly much more Antipathetic to the Spirit of its own nature and species. This may be seen in the human spirit infected by the plague <note>original: *peste*</note>; for it has been observed that the last breath <note>original: *spiraculum*</note> of a man dying of the plague is exceedingly contagious to those present, being ruinous and lethal beyond measure.

### CONCLUSION.

I could indeed (judicious reader) gather an entire volume of experimental propositions, together with their proofs, concerning the abyss and infinite forest of Sympathetic and Antipathetic effects in the three kingdoms—namely, the animal, vegetable, and mineral—both mutually between any species, and from individuals from one genus to another. But I did not set out to express my more daring and constant opinions concerning true Philosophy and its appendages in a more ample style, considering the roughness and haste of my pen by reason of my defect and insufficiency in its polished nature. In turn, I am not ignorant that polished and decorated words and phrases are nothing but the fluttering bubbles and, as it were, shadows of a powerful and wealthy subject; just as they are Protean-like <note>Changing shape or color easily, like the sea-god Proteus.</note> in their changeability into infinite colors, so also the fantasies and judgments of men are greatly variable. According to the proverb: *As many men, so many opinions* <note>original: *Quot homines, tot sententiæ*</note>. I believe indeed, and my mind foretells, that however curious or exact I may be in my writing, or in my phrasing...

### SECOND SECTION. BOOK III. Member II.

...though my mode of expression is laborious, nevertheless my better efforts will appear not without fault or crime in the eyes of the curious, though perhaps they may be pleasing enough to others. For this reason, I think it sufficient that I dare to be confident in the fundamental subject of this <term>essential Philosophy</term> <note>Fludd refers to his "Mosaic Philosophy," which seeks the "essence" of reality through scripture and nature.</note>, as it possesses truth itself to defend and vindicate it without any decoration of superficial words. Furthermore, just as truth does not seek out dark corners, so it has no need for the expression of eloquent words, polished sentences, or sophisticated phrases to illustrate itself or make itself clearer in the eyes of the wise and the learned; for it can be hidden from no one that truth conquers all: 
<margin>Wisdom 7</margin> 
For she is a bright splendor or emanation, arising from the almighty and eternal source, which illuminates all things and reveals itself in effect to everyone. Therefore, she is so manifest in all her works that she does not require any golden-tongued orator, any charmingly methodical rhetorician, or any eloquent philosopher to reveal her excellence or relate the perfection of her delights to the whole world—even if the unworthy people of this world refuse to 

<column-break/>

acknowledge <note>original: *agnoscere*</note> or receive her with the reverence she deserves. Instead, they perpetually hide her with all their might behind a veil of dark ignorance. Thus, they do not cease to daily persecute and crucify the spiritual Christ, who is the only truth, the true wisdom, the true <term>Cornerstone</term> <note>original: *lapis Angularis*. In this context, the "Cornerstone" refers to both Christ and the "Philosophers' Stone" of the alchemists.</note> and the essential subject of a true and legitimate Philosophy. Blessed be His name forever; He alone founded the heavens, the earth, and all things within them, and He sustains and preserves them by the quickening of His spirit. He works all things in all people and reigns in glory and power with the Father forever. He will deign to defend His servants from the evil-hearted and protect the herald of His truth like a shield and a place of refuge from the viperous tongues of malicious veterans, from the backbiting of shifters, and from the poisonous taunts of the cynical and satirical <term>Momus</term> <note>Momus was the Greek god of mockery and unfair criticism; here, Fludd uses it to represent his academic and theological critics.</note>. It is He who handed down these words to the cultivator of His truth:
<margin>Luke 21</margin>
> I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will not be able to resist or contradict.
Therefore, I shall conclude with the Prophet David:
<margin>Psalm 63:8</margin>
> In the shadow of your wings I will sing: Lord, in you I trust: Vindicate and preserve me from my enemies according to your mercy. Amen.
